evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# 万卷 (wanjuan) > 读书破万卷。上下文像卷轴一样一折一折收起来，需要时再展开。 **万卷** 是一个为 LLM 宿主（如 DeepSeek Harness）设计的**上下文压缩内核**。纯原生 Node.js ESM（>= 20），零第三方依赖，以事件溯源（Event Sourcing）与「前缀纪律」为根基，解决长对话场景下的窗口爆炸与 KV 缓存失效问题。 **万卷是一套自运转系统**：折叠自动、桥接自动、补桥自动、校准自动、学习自动、恢复自动、突变吸收自动、崩溃自愈自动——你正常聊天，它自己工作。 ```mermaid flowchart TB A["DSH 会话事件
user/message · assistant/message · tool/result"] --> B["万卷账本
append-only JSONL · 突变走 mut 吸收"] B --> C{"turn/end 水位检查
estFinal ÷ 窗口（动态解析）"} C -- "≥95%" --> D["自动折叠
显式 ids · 保尾 20 条 · seqSpan 入档"] C -- "≥80%" --> E["提醒（日志）：点名可折区间"] D --> F["桥接宿主 compactRegion
signal 可中止 · 超时兜底 · 崩溃锁自愈"] F --> G["宿主 checkpoint 摘要节点
真实上下文同步收缩"] D --> H["补桥对账 wj_reconcile
终态/瞬态分类 · 冷启动探针"] B --> I["摊销对数压缩
ledger.0000 检查点 · archive 归档"] ``` ## 💡 核心理念：每个 Bug 都有归宿 在长上下文场景中，最大的噩梦不是「截断」，而是「缓存全灭」。万卷直面宿主环境的泥泞： - **拒绝背锅（责任隔离）**：请求遥测带 `missKind` 归因框架（`overrideMissKind` 注入口已预留）；当前版本如实产出 `new / unattributed`，完整归因 M5 交付，不虚报命中率。 - **自我愈合（锚点吸收）**：宿主偷偷改了历史？万卷不在历史中重写，而是追加 `mut` 事件吸收突变，让账本真正收敛，告别死循环。 - **绝对容错（断电保护）**：写到一半断电导致账本坏行？跳过坏行并大声告警；下次追加前自动隔离崩溃半行（补换行符），新事件绝不陪葬。状态文件（桥接状态/自学习窗口）原子写，多进程下不读半截。 - **聚合账本（单库多会话）**：多窗口的会话事件汇入同一账本（按宿主 seq 记录日志位次），进程内单线程串行追加无写冲突；跨进程隔离依赖 profile 隔离。 ## 🏗 里程碑（M1 → M4.4） | 阶段 | 内容 | |---|---| | **M1–M3 观测与折叠** | 全词汇入账 + 四工具 + 两段式水位引擎（80% 点名区间提醒 / 95% 自动折叠保尾 20 条，UUID 主机走显式 ids） | | **M3.5–M3.9 真实接管** | 桥接宿主 `compactRegion`（五层真机契约）+ 动态窗口与自学习 + 校准入档 + 自动补桥（终态/瞬态分类）+ 日志落盘审计 | | **M4 自愈** | 重启恢复 · `mut` 突变吸收 · 摊销对数压缩（启动重放有界）· 突变嗅探（TTL）· 崩溃遗留锁自愈（冷启动主动探针 + busy 反应式双通道）· `signal` 信号中止 | ### M3 的两个关键修正 - **`estimator.estRaw` 不是方法**：它是 `estimate()` 返回值的字段。水位 = `estFinal`（k̂ 校准 + 5% 偏置）÷ 窗口。k̂ 用真实 usage 做按模型 EMA 校准（5 个样本后收敛），入档可观测。 - **宿主消息 ID 是 UUID**：字典序 ≠ 时间序（实测不单调）。折叠一律走**显式 ids 列表**，绝不传 range 端点——`ledger.recordFold`、`compressor.compress`、`wj_compress` 工具三处齐备。 ### M3.5 为什么桥接宿主 compaction，而不是自己改请求 宿主三条瀑布全查证过： - `agent/pre-step`：只给本轮新进的 `UserMessage[]`，历史不在场； - `agent/request`：契约明文 **"cannot mutate messages"**，`LlmCallConfig` 只有控制项； - `llm/stream`：LOOP 请求的 `messages` **深度冻结**（reconstructability 原则：请求必须是会话日志的纯函数）。 唯一合法入口是 `ctx.compaction.compactRegion(startSeq, endSeq, agent)`——成功后真实日志区间替换成一个摘要节点，模型可见、缓存责任归宿主。万卷在账本里记录事件 `seq`（SessionSeq），完成「账本消息 → 真实日志区间」的映射；服务缺失时优雅降级为只折账本。 ### 真机契约五层（每层都是实测踩出来的） | 层 | 坑 | 解法 | |---|---|---| | ① 访问控制 | 直接 `ctx.compaction` 抛 `cannot get property without inject` | `inject` 声明 `compaction`（及 `llm`） | | ② agent 形态 | 裸传 Session 抛 `reading 'surface'` | 包装 `{ session, options }`（宿主内部走 `agent.session.surface`） | | ③ whole-surface 稳定性 | 摘要期间表面变化即弃 | 手动路径 **await 宿主摘要完成**再返回工具结果 | | ④ 净收益检查 | 宿主拒绝越压越大（checkpoint 摘要 ~1.2K token 起步） | 跨度需远大于摘要成本，小跨度转终态跳过 | | ⑤ 边界配平 | 起点拆散 tool-call/result 对、终点 step 未闭合 | 起点自动回退到最近 user 消息；软失败入补桥队列 | 宿主压缩失败为**软失败**：告警入日志，账本折叠照常生效，欠账由补桥体系清理。 ## 🧰 工具面 | 工具 | 作用 | |---|---| | `wj_compress` | 折叠指定消息为摘要（`ids` 显式集合优先，`range` 二选一；内置 KEEP/DROP 哲学） | | `wj_reconcile` | 补桥：对宿主压缩未打通的历史块补发 `compactRegion`，消除「账本折了、真实上下文还在」的错位 | | `wj_decompress` | 恢复折叠块原文 | | `wj_search` | 在折叠块中检索 | | `wj_report` | 磁盘账本报告 + 最近日志环；可选 `logTail` 深读落盘日志（事故现场审计） | ## 🛠 架构亮点 - **事件溯源账本**：`msg / mut / fold / evict / unfold / promote`，坏行告警、断电保护、多会话隔离。 - **三段式估算**：`est_raw → × k̂ → × 1.05 偏置`，贝叶斯先验，真实 usage 按模型 EMA 校准且入档可观测。 - **动态窗口感知**：宿主注册表实时解析 `contextWindow`，换模型零配置自适应；解析结果自学习落盘，重启后兜底链依然精确。 - **日志环 + 落盘审计**：内存 30 条（`wj_report` 展示）+ 落盘 `wanjuan.log.jsonl`（256KB 轮转留尾 100 行），重启不丢。 - **账本对数压缩**：等价极简流 + 旧卷归档，月度会话的启动重放延迟有界，原文可达不变式始终成立。 - **桥接超时兜底**：宿主摘要挂死 180s（`bridgeTimeoutMs` 可调）转瞬态失败，不永久阻塞手动路径。 - **防弹测试**：166 个自动化测试用例（含大量失败注入），`node --test` 全绿。 ## 🧩 已知未接线（预留模块） 以下模块代码在库内、有测试保护，但尚未接入生产路径（DESIGN 规划的 L2 决策层与 L0 遥测，实现覆盖约六成）： | 模块 | 现状 | 计划 | |---|---|---| | `fingerprint` | 有测试（15 项）、未接线 | M2 对账：账本 vs 宿主投影指纹核对 | | `gate` | 有测试（2 项）、未接线 | L2 决策层；阈值与 dsh 内联值（0.80/0.95）对齐后接入 | | `nudge`（NudgeManager 类） | 有测试（10 项）、未接线 | 80% 提醒现由日志实现（点名区间），类接入后更结构化 | | `report.buildReport` | 有测试（5 项）、未接线 | 月报聚合；`wj_report` 现为轻量实时报告 | | `Observer` | 有测试（7 项）、未接线 | 与 Diagnoser 两套遥测待合并 | | `snapshot.json` | 接口预留 | M4.3 摊销压缩已以更简方式覆盖 | `classifyMiss` 归因分类当前只产出 `new / unattributed`（`overrideMissKind` 注入口已预留），完整归因 **M5 交付**。 ## ⚠️ 已知局限（如实披露） - **消息入账 tok 为粗估**：`estimateTok` 用「字符数 ÷ 2」，中文会话下账本 tok 系统性低估（约 2 倍）；k̂ 校准会部分吸收，但中文/英文混合会话的水位仍有偏差。口径统一（精细 CJK 估算 + 入账走 estimator）计划于 **v0.7**。 - **归因分类未完成**：`missKind` 当前只产出 `new / unattributed`，完整归因 M5 交付。 - **output reserve 与窗口不同源**：窗口动态解析自宿主注册表，output 来自 models.json/学习文件（未知模型兜底 8192）——大窗口下 reserve 偏保守（折叠偏早方向，安全）。 - **多会话共享单账本**：多窗口事件汇入同一账本；跨进程/会话强隔离未实现。 ## 📁 数据文件一览 | 文件 | 内容 | 增长策略 | |---|---|---| | `ledger.NNNN.jsonl` | 事件溯源账本（分卷） | 超阈值对数压缩，旧卷入 `archive/` | | `block.bN.json` + `block.bN.raw.jsonl` | 块元数据 + 折叠原文 | 随折叠增长；`wj_decompress` 的原文来源 | | `requests.jsonl` | 请求遥测（校准/归因） | 5MB 轮转留尾 2000 行 | | `models.learned.json` | 自学习窗口（跨重启） | 每模型一条，极小 | | `host-bridge.json` | 每块宿主桥接状态 | 每块一条，极小 | | `wanjuan.log.jsonl` | 审计日志 | 256KB 轮转留尾 100 行 | | `snapshot.json` | 预留快照接口 | 未启用（M4.3 摊销压缩已以更简方式覆盖该需求） | ## 🧭 快速开始（Quick Start） ```bash # 获取代码并自检 git clone https://github.com/05shizuku/wanjuan.git cd wanjuan && npm test # 预期 166 个用例全绿 # 挂进 DSH profile（junction/软链到 profile 的 node_modules） # Windows: mklink /J "\node_modules\wanjuan" "<本仓库>" ``` 1. **数据目录**：`dsh.bundle.patch.yml` 已自带 `dir: .wanjuan`，通常零配置 2. **启用宿主压缩**：patch 层加一行 `{ id: compaction-basic, disabled: false }`（缺失时万卷优雅降级为只折账本） 3. **验收**：正常聊天几轮后对模型说「调 wj_report」——看到请求遥测与日志环即接入成功；水位到线时会出现 `自动折叠完成` / `宿主原生压缩完成` 的成对日志 4. **出问题时**：`wj_report { logTail: 100 }` 深读落盘日志，事故现场不用重启 ## 📦 作为 DSH 插件接入 包内自带 `dsh.bundle.patch.yml`（`dsh.bundle.patch` 字段声明）。核心配置： | 配置 | 默认 | 说明 | |---|---|---| | `dir` | — | 数据目录（相对 profile 数据目录，如 `.wanjuan`） | | `shadowMode` | `false` | `true` 时退回影子模式：折叠只提示、水位引擎关闭 | | `logToFile` | `true` | 日志落盘审计；`false` 仅内存日志环 | | `bridgeTimeoutMs` | `180000` | 宿主压缩桥接超时（毫秒），超时转瞬态失败待补桥 | | `windowTtlMs` | `1800000` | 窗口缓存 TTL（毫秒），宿主配置突变的嗅探周期 | | `compactionThreshold` | `5000` | 账本对数压缩的事件数阈值（超大 sessions 可调低） | > 注：宿主侧需启用原生 `compaction-basic`（`{ id: compaction-basic, disabled: false }`）以提供压缩服务；缺失时万卷优雅降级为只折账本。 ## 📜 License MIT

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# STU MCP for DeepSeek Harness

The current bundle **0.1.1** supports DSH **0.2.1-rc.3** and **0.2.2-rc.3**. It adds a left
sidebar entry, a right sidebar tab, and a bundle configuration view. No build
step, extra React copy, school adapter, credential form or MCP process is added.

First connect the common STU MCP service with `stu-mcp connect dsh --apply`.
Download `dsh-stu-mcp-0.1.1.tgz` from the
[v0.7.8 release](https://github.com/0error0warning/stu-mcp/releases/tag/v0.7.8).
Developers can build the same package with `npm pack --ignore-scripts --offline` in this directory.
Then use the CLI belonging to the same DSH desktop installation, passing the
absolute path to the downloaded file:

```powershell
& '<DSH installation>/resources/runtime/cli/bin/dsh.cmd' plugin --profile desktop add '<package directory>/dsh-stu-mcp-0.1.1.tgz' --ignore-scripts
```

Restart DSH. Open **STU MCP** in the left sidebar, or choose **STU MCP** from
the right sidebar's new-tab guide. The installed package is `dsh-stu-mcp`.
It is distributed as a GitHub release asset; it is not listed in the DSH marketplace.
For local development, prefer a packed archive kept outside the checkout. In the
2026-11-15 Windows migration, removing the previous directory-linked package also
cleared its source target; the pre-install archive restored all five files.
Back up any existing linked source before replacing it, and verify that the final
module resolves inside the DSH profile. See the [migration record](../../docs/verification/2026-11-15-dsh-local.md).

The panel starts with a short public-query summary, four common account rows,
and **登录与设置** / **刷新** buttons. WebVPN, takeout and utility features are
under **更多功能**; version and diagnostic details are under **连接信息**.
Account state still comes from the shared MCP catalog. “已设置” means saved
configuration, rather than a live check of the school service.

To remove only this optional UI:

```powershell
& '<DSH installation>/resources/runtime/cli/bin/dsh.cmd' plugin --profile desktop remove dsh-stu-mcp
```

The separately managed official MCP connection and shared credentials remain.
On DSH 0.2.1-rc.3, restart after disabling/removing to clear already loaded
client surfaces. A saved right-sidebar tab can remain as an unavailable-view
placeholder; close that tab normally. Re-enabling restores the viewer.
The UI invokes only the existing `get_capabilities` and `open_setup` tools via
DSH's authenticated Connection/Gateway source-mode Remote service. No generic
tool-execution endpoint is exposed. Local configuration status does not imply
live school availability. HTTP-hosted MCP setup remains on the MCP host.

`client.js` is the complete plain-JavaScript browser artifact. The host's React,
Slots and lifecycle APIs are reused; client unload removes entries and aborts calls.
The two-version engine constraint is intentional: widen only after testing another
DSH release. Standard MCP clients do not depend on this bundle.

# STU MCP

这个项目的前身，是我在「养」Hermes agent 时，从零搭起来的一个自用信息聚合器。学校通知、课程、作业，散在不同地方的信息，我都想慢慢接进去。自己用的版本里，甚至还接入了微信聊天记录。

我折腾它的原因，是希望 agent 在帮我做事时，能拿到足够的个人上下文：我最近在忙什么、有什么通知要看、哪些事情还没做完。和我有关的信息，如果它能在需要时自己查到，我就能少重复一些背景，也不用总在几个网站和聊天窗口之间来回复制粘贴。

后来，我把里面和汕大有关的部分整理成了 STU MCP，想让其他同学也能接到自己常用的 agent 上。它负责找信息、读信息，怎么理解和整理，交给你自己的 agent。

微信聊天记录接入留在自用版本里，公开版不包含。用这里的功能也不需要先装 Hermes，或者另外配一份模型 API key。

## 想试试的话

找一个能在你电脑上执行命令的 agent，把这两行发给它：

```text
帮我安装 STU MCP：https://github.com/0error0warning/stu-mcp
按 docs/install.md 接入当前客户端，保留已有配置并验证公开查询。按安装版本说明登录；认证信息由我本人输入，不发给 agent。
```

[单独复制这段 prompt](install-prompt.txt) · [安装细节](docs/install.md)

装好以后，可以直接问它：

- “最近有什么适合我报名的竞赛？把截止时间和原文找出来。”
- “整理一下 MySTU 接下来两周的作业，按截止时间排一排。”
- “树洞里有人聊过这门选修课吗？搜一下大家怎么说。”

## 现在能查些什么

| 功能分类 | 来源与系统 | 当前接入范围 | 登录方式 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 通知与活动 | 学校官网、学生处、校团委、OA 公告 | 新闻、通知、活动、正文、附件列表及 PDF / 文本附件内容；[校团委范围](docs/xtw.md) | OA 原站可达且内容公开时免登录；WebVPN 访问通道按需，见[读取范围与条件](docs/verification/2026-10-22-oa-entry-boundaries.md) |
| 课程与教务 | 教务、MySTU / Moodle、雨课堂、对分易 | 成绩、考试、本人理论课表、课程、作业、资料、个人日程；对分易课程监听、启停及签到结果，新课堂提交仍待实测 | 教务与 MySTU 使用学校 SSO；雨课堂手机确认二维码；对分易原微信回调，各自保存会话 |
| 医学院课表（试验） | 医学院教务 | 本人当前学期课表；适配器通过合成测试，待真实账号验收，见[范围说明](docs/medical-jw.md) | 教务本地口令及本人填写图片验证码，独立保存会话 |
| 校园办事 | 宿舍报修、综合报修、一网通办等 | 桑浦山宿舍 `repair` 支持填表、完整预览、本人确认后单次提交及回执核对；综合报修 `r`、一网通办目前提供入口导航 | 宿舍报修使用学校 SSO，单独保存会话；其他入口按原站要求 |
| 一卡通本人查询 | 学校一卡通系统 | 卡余额和状态、指定日期及类型的历史流水；不挂失、充值或改密 | 独立查询密码和本人填写的图片验证码；官方入口为明文 HTTP |
| 网络访问与排障 | 登记的学校入口及认证依赖 | 单服务连接诊断、学校入口批量检测：检查 DNS、匿名直连，按需对照代理或公共 DNS | 免登录；不改变网络设置，不代表业务已可用 |
| 第三方校园生活与社区 | 充电平台、STU 外卖（开发中）、狐友 | 设备与插座状态、外卖目录 / 配送批次 / 选餐、树洞公开帖子及评论；外卖不下单或支付 | 充电和公开讨论免登录；外卖需单独配置 |
| 软件与本地管理 | stu-mcp 宿主及本地数据 | 安装接入、登录配置、更新检查与升级、本地待办和个人偏好 | 按需配置 |

选择登录配置时，可先看[配置哪些登录，当前能用哪些功能](docs/campus-services.md#配置哪些登录当前能用哪些功能)：学校统一账号对应已适配的教务、MySTU 和宿舍报修；雨课堂、对分易、WebVPN 及第三方配置各有自己的功能范围，公开内容按条件免登录。同目录另列学校服务的入口和未接入项，不将“学校有这个系统”算成“MCP 已能使用”。

设置页、`stu-mcp status` 和 MCP `get_capabilities` 使用同一份功能目录，告诉你配置后能做什么、哪些服务还没接入。学校统一账号输入一次，分别连接已接入的教务、MySTU 和宿舍报修；各业务仍独立保存会话，某项未完成会单独说明。

也可以记一下本地待办，或者告诉 agent 你的学院、专业和兴趣。它们都不是必填项，本地勾选“完成”也不会替你向学校提交作业。

查到的信息会带来源和缓存时间。想看最新消息时，让 agent 先刷新；没查到也可能只是这次没取全。狐友里是同学们的讨论，学校的正式要求还是要看 OA 或学校原文。[狐友怎么查](docs/huyou.md)

v0.7.8 明确了附件遇验证码后的交接：给你通知原文链接，结束这一附件的自动获取；缓存查询和来源刷新每次最多100条，默认仍为20条。具体约定见[Agent 使用说明](docs/agent-usage.md)。

本版包含充电查询，由本机 MCP 直接请求充电平台，按设备缓存，没有网站或自建服务器依赖。现有清单包含 15 台已核验设备，不代表全校完整清单；离线和旧数据会单独标记。[充电查询用法](docs/charging.md)

校园连接按服务处理：r和一网通办先查自身入口，宿舍报修需要时核实校园接入，SSO和ITS各协议独立判断。同属网络排障的两个工具保留各自范围：单服务诊断定位一个入口及其依赖，批量检测比较固定目录；校园入口普查并不会自动扩充运行时探测清单。普通读取复用连接，同批次暂时跳过连接失败的主机，继续读取其他来源，不自动改代理或接入远程隧道。[单服务诊断](docs/network.md) · [批量检测](docs/network-audit.md)

## 自己动手安装

先装好 [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/)，然后运行。这里以 Codex 为例：

```sh
uv tool install --python 3.12 https://github.com/0error0warning/stu-mcp/releases/download/v0.7.8/stu_mcp-0.7.8-py3-none-any.whl
stu-mcp connect codex --apply
```

第二行换成你用的客户端，比如 `claude-code` 或 `cursor`。其他客户端、豆包工作和 Skill 的接法放在[这里](docs/clients.md)。v0.6.1 起，运行 `stu-mcp update` 即可检查并升级；只想看有无新版用 `stu-mcp update --check`，也可以让 agent 调用对应更新工具。升级后，本机 stdio 重新加载 MCP；私有 HTTP 须重启宿主 MCP 服务。旧版首次升级见[安装说明](docs/install.md#从旧版升级)，支持范围见[更新说明](docs/updates.md)。

使用 DeepSeek Harness（DSH）时，可另装 [STU MCP 插件](https://github.com/0error0warning/stu-mcp/releases/download/v0.7.8/dsh-stu-mcp-0.1.1.tgz)，在左右侧栏查看账号状态、打开登录设置。校园查询照常在对话里完成，安装方法见 [DSH 说明](integrations/dsh/README.md)。

MCP 接入和技能安装分别处理。随包的[课表导出技能](docs/timetable.md)组织校历核对和文件转换。v0.7.1 加入教务本人理论课表读取，继续复用该技能和同一转换器；实验课、校历及作息另行核对。技能 ZIP 是可选资源包，生成后仍需按客户端支持的方式安装，不会自动让当前 agent 加载技能。

需要登录时，让 agent 打开设置页，或自己运行 `stu-mcp setup`。在自己的浏览器里配置学校统一账号、雨课堂、对分易、WebVPN 或一卡通，认证信息不经过 agent。WebVPN 可填写已有令牌密钥，由程序生成动态码并自动登录；不配置密钥也能手动输入当前动态码。喜欢终端可用 `stu-mcp login school` 等命令，完整用法见[认证说明](docs/authentication.md)。

本机 stdio 与个人服务器私有 Streamable HTTP 共用一套工具。CLI 与设置页共用 HTTP 认证核心，默认安装和 Docker 模板不需要桌面或 Chromium；无桌面服务器可以完整使用 CLI。会话及个人缓存加密保存，普通学校密码只用于本次认证。客户端到 MCP 和 MCP 到学校是两段网络，连上服务器不代表服务器能访问校园网。[服务器说明](docs/server.md) · [存储与隐私](SECURITY.md)

本版包含对分易后台和轻量本地网页：选课、启停监听、查询签到结果，微信回调可在宿主终端或本地网页完成。MCP 退出后后台继续运行，状态明确区分未启动、未登录、已暂停、监听中和查询异常。支持持续监听；电脑需保持运行和联网。新的课堂自动提交仍待实测。[安装与用法](docs/checkin.md)

宿舍报修使用独立 HTTP 会话填表，完整展示实际表单，等你明确确认后只提交一次。随后核对新增单据及详情，返回单号、处理状态和核对时间；结果未知时只读查单。草稿留在进程内存，登录会话独立加密保存。当前适配桑浦山学生社区；新版真实登录和填表预览已核验，正式提交仍由合成与回环测试覆盖，没有为验收额外建单。校园网报修是另一套入口。[使用与验证范围](docs/repair.md)

喜欢用终端的话，也可以直接查：

```sh
stu-mcp refresh oa --limit 20
stu-mcp query notice --source oa --search 竞赛
stu-mcp huyou search 选课
```

## 还在慢慢补

当前版本为 **[v0.7.8 学生预览版](docs/releases/v0.7.8.md)**，发布状态以 GitHub 发行页为准。[发行说明](docs/releases/v0.7.8.md) · [最近更新](CHANGELOG.md)

正式 HTTP 适配器已实测教务、MySTU 的身份与课程、ELC/Campus 的部分业务、雨课堂课程活动，以及报修登录和完整预览。WebVPN 的密码、动态口令和资源目录通过；受保护 OA 正文及自然过期续登尚未通过本轮验收。发行 CI 包含跨平台测试和默认镜像离线检查，容器内学校业务、跨机接入、更多账号和真实新报修提交仍分别待验，详见[验证记录](docs/verification.md)。

如果你用起来了，或者发现某个入口读不动了，欢迎开 issue 聊聊。告诉我用的版本、卡在哪一步就很有帮助，别把真实成绩、密码或登录凭据贴进去。

想自己改也可以：

```sh
uv sync --extra dev
uv run --extra dev pytest -q
uv run --extra dev ruff check .
uv run stu-mcp setup
uv run stu-checkin
uv build
```

[文档目录](docs/README.md) · [更新记录](CHANGELOG.md) · [代码结构](docs/architecture.md) · [代码来源](docs/provenance.json)

MIT 许可。个人折腾的小项目，和学校官方没有关系。

# DeepSeek Always-on

[Latest native-client, export and runtime verification](docs/V03_ENGINEERING.md) · **MVP Ready: false**

**v0.3 development candidate:** account-first Desktop/mobile onboarding, isolated account-to-Harness allocation, native event updates and operator deployment/recovery tooling are implemented in this repository. [Implementation and release gates](docs/V03_ACCEPTANCE.md) · [Operator handoff and user flow](docs/V03_HANDOFF.md) · [Baseline audit](docs/V03_AUDIT.md). **No production sign-in service, physical iPhone release or MVP Ready claim.** v0.2 and the published v0.1 Web alpha records remain below.

**v0.2 development is in progress:** a managed Harness device gateway, paired native Desktop panel, independent React Native / Expo app and durable native-push outbox are implemented. Existing task scheduling, memory, Inbox and Run Ledger are reused. **No production hosted URL or real-phone/model/push release acceptance is claimed.**

See [managed runtime](docs/V02_PHASE2.md), [native mobile](docs/V02_PHASE3.md), [shared devices](docs/V02_PHASE4.md), [native notifications](docs/V02_PHASE5.md) and [release gates](docs/V02_PLAN.md). The original Web/PWA alpha remains available below; it is not the v0.2 native phone delivery.

[Native preview setup and current blockers](docs/V02_QUICKSTART.md) · [Security scope](docs/V02_SECURITY.md)
[v0.2 acceptance and artifacts](docs/V02_ACCEPTANCE.md)

[简体中文](README.zh-CN.md) · [Development plan](PLAN.md) · [Acceptance evidence](docs/ACCEPTANCE.md)

A native **DeepSeek Harness / Cordis plugin** for persistent personal tasks, consented memory, a shared Inbox and Web Push. One cloud Host serves your phone and computer. Harness owns the model, chat, tools, Sessions and scheduling; this plugin does not implement an Agent loop.

**Status: 0.1.0-alpha.2 — engineering acceptance passed; production validation pending, not MVP Ready.** No hosted service, DeepSeek API credit or npm publication is included in this repository. GitHub Actions is a test runner, not a continuously running Host.

## Legacy v0.1 Web alpha developer installation

The following commands configure the original Web alpha. They are not the v0.3 ordinary-user onboarding flow. The v0.3 account service and signed physical-phone release are still blocked; see the handoff above.

Requires pnpm on PATH, Node **24.9+** and exactly **`@deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.2-rc.3`**. Preview APIs are version-sensitive; see [compatibility](docs/COMPATIBILITY.md).

```bash
git clone https://github.com/abwoo/-DeepSeek-Always-on-Personal-AI-Agent-Plugin.git
cd -- -DeepSeek-Always-on-Personal-AI-Agent-Plugin
npm install -g pnpm@11.28.5
npm ci
npm run check
npm pack
npx --package @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.2-rc.3 dsh plugin --profile web add "$PWD/abwoo-deepseek-always-on-0.1.0-alpha.2.tgz"
npx --package @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.2-rc.3 dsh web --no-open --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8080
```

Open the launch URL locally to authenticate. Configure your DeepSeek model and credentials through Harness Settings. On a server use an authenticated HTTPS gateway; read [deployment](deploy/README.md) before exposing any endpoint. Phone and desktop must access **the same Host URL**. A local Harness Desktop installation is a different Host.

The **Always-on** sidebar entry contains Agent, Tasks, Memory and Inbox. Create a once, interval or daily task. Tasks have dedicated Harness Sessions and default to 30 lifetime runs, 8 model steps per run a 180-second timeout, a 2,048-token per-request output cap and a 50,000 reported-token per-run budget. The total-token threshold stops the next request after provider accounting arrives; one request can overshoot it. Missing accounting stops further model steps. Only explicitly selected built-in `web_search` / `web_fetch` tools plus the plugin's report/retrieval tools are permitted during an unattended run. No shell, outbound writes, purchasing, publishing or email dispatch is admitted. Unsupported actions remain interactive Harness work.

## Memory and notifications

Add a memory in the panel and explicitly consent to cross-session use. Chat's `always_on_memory_propose` tool proposes a memory; it becomes retrievable only after you confirm it in the panel. Search is keyword-based; approved memories form a small dynamic system-prompt section. Deletion stops future retrieval and prompt assembly; it does **not** erase historical model requests, backups, or provider records.

The Inbox is the authoritative notification record. Optional Web Push needs `VAPID_SUBJECT`, `VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY` and `VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY` in the Host environment. Generate a key pair on the server with `npx web-push generate-vapid-keys`; never commit private keys. Enable notifications with a user gesture in Inbox. On iPhone install the Harness Web App on your Home Screen first (iOS 16.4+). Revocation and provider failures do not remove Inbox results. Lock-screen payloads contain a generic update only.

## Reliability contract

- Native Schedule delivery is **not completion**. A run becomes completed only after `always_on_report`, a successful native `turn/end`, and successful Session flush.
- A unique task/occurrence pair prevents the same occurrence from being admitted twice. SQLite transactions persist run admission before model work.
- A crash before final confirmation marks the run interrupted on restart. This alpha never automatically replays interrupted work. Inspect the Session, then explicitly start a new occurrence if appropriate.
- No-change checks stay in run history without notifying. Repeated source sets are suppressed across runs.
- Disabling the plugin pauses its owned schedules on graceful teardown. Stored native reminders contain only a trigger, never the underlying task instruction, so an absent plugin cannot disclose the task to an uncoordinated turn.
- This is **not exactly-once execution**. The model's acknowledgment is a reported business outcome, not an independently verified external-world guarantee.

SQLite WAL state lives in `ALWAYS_ON_DATA_DIR` or the profile's `always-on/` directory. Keep the entire Harness profile and plugin data on durable, private storage. One writer Host per profile is supported. See [operations](docs/OPERATIONS.md).

## Development

```bash
npm ci
npm run check
# Installs the bundle in a disposable test profile:
DSH_HOME="$PWD/.artifacts/dsh" npx dsh plugin --profile web add "$PWD"
npx playwright install chromium
npm run test:e2e
```

E2E launches the published real Harness Web profile, installs this bundle, exercises authenticated API access, mobile UI, cross-device state and Host restart. It does not spend API credits or claim real iPhone push delivery. CI uploads the npm tarball, browser reports and screenshots. [Acceptance status](docs/ACCEPTANCE.md) separates component, native integration, browser and real-device evidence.

MIT licensed. This is an independent community plugin, not an official DeepSeek product.

Exported dist/host/index.js and dist/client.js are absent in the fixed archive; prepack runs the build and npm is absent. Built release correspondence is unresolved. No candidate code or lifecycle hooks were executed; runtime safety and compatibility are unproven.

# DeepSeek Always-on — Desktop native plugin

Development candidate for DeepSeek Harness **0.2.2-rc.3**, Cordis **4.1.0**. The package runs inside the official Desktop Profile and provides Personal Agent. Local Harness workspaces and hosted Personal Agent conversations remain separate.

## Graphical installation

Open **Plugins → Add plugin**, enter the operator-published npm package/version or supported tarball address, confirm installation and enable the plugin. This is third-party distribution, not an official DeepSeek endorsement. Production publication is blocked until a real service and release gates are verified; do not mistake this private development candidate for a live service.

The pinned official Plugins page supports disabling/enabling and removal. For third-party upgrades its UI instructs uninstall/reinstall; use the operator's immutable supported package version. Removing the plugin does not delete hosted tasks or memory. Reinstall and sign in to recover the same account's authority. Background cloud work is controlled in Tasks or the account service; disabling the local presentation plugin does not stop its independent hosted Agent.

No public production URL, provider credit, Apple signing or physical-phone certification is included. See repository docs/V03_ACCEPTANCE.md for current implementation and exact gates.

# DeepSeek Always-on

[Latest native-client, export and runtime verification](docs/V03_ENGINEERING.md) · **MVP Ready: false**

**v0.3 development candidate:** account-first Desktop/mobile onboarding, isolated account-to-Harness allocation, native event updates and operator deployment/recovery tooling are implemented in this repository. [Implementation and release gates](docs/V03_ACCEPTANCE.md) · [Operator handoff and user flow](docs/V03_HANDOFF.md) · [Baseline audit](docs/V03_AUDIT.md). **No production sign-in service, physical iPhone release or MVP Ready claim.** v0.2 and the published v0.1 Web alpha records remain below.


# dsh-id

给 AI Agent 用的账号执行层：**凭据值不落明文、不进日志、不进对话**，AI 却能自主用你的账号干活。

为 [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai) 生态写的，纯本地、无服务端、无遥测。

![dsh-id](docs/screenshot.png)

---

## 解决什么问题

AI 要用你的账号，只有三种做法：

| 做法 | 问题 |
| --- | --- |
| 把 token 贴进对话 | 之后每一次请求的输入里都有它，永久泄露 |
| 把 token 写进 `.env` | 任何同机进程 `cat` 一下就有 |
| 让 AI 每次找你要密码 | 你变成人肉 2FA，一天被打断十次 |

`dsh-id` 走第四条：**凭据只在该用的那一瞬间、只在该用的那个进程里解开**，其余时间磁盘上只有密文。

```bash
dsh-id exec github-pat https://api.github.com/user
```

这条命令执行完，明文就消失了。它不在命令行参数里（`ps` 看不到）、不在日志里、不在对话里。

---

## 五个能力

| 命令 | 干什么 |
| --- | --- |
| `dsh-id exec` | 按需注入凭据，发一次 HTTP 请求或跑一条命令，结束即失效 |
| `dsh-id session` | 网页登录态：**登录一次**存下 cookie/localStorage，之后直接是登录态（2FA 只过一次） |
| `dsh-id creds` | 凭据增删查测、改主密码、`panic` 一键吊销、`restore` 恢复、审计链校验 |
| `dsh-id guard` | 不可逆操作闸门：删除/转账/发布这类动作先记一条待批准 |
| `dsh-id` | 不带参数：一屏状态（凭据数、会话数、审计链、待审批） |

底层是五个独立可用的 CLI（`vault-cred` / `vault-session` / `vault-exec` / `vault-guard` / `vault-proxy`），`dsh-id` 只是统一入口，不改变它们的行为。

---

## 安装

### 方式一：当 DSH 插件装（推荐）

仓库根目录就是一个 DSH bundle（`package.json` + `cordis.patch.yml`）。在 DSH 里让 Agent 执行：

```text
plugin_manager install_bundle  github:AdgaiWalker/dsh-id
```

或手工装进 profile：

```bash
cd ~/.dsh/profiles/web
pnpm add github:AdgaiWalker/dsh-id
```

装好后在「设置 → 插件」里能看到 `dsh-id`。工具能力取决于机器上有没有装下面的 CLI。

### 方式二：只要命令行

需要：Linux / Python 3.10+ / `openssl`。

```bash
git clone https://github.com/AdgaiWalker/dsh-id ~/dsh-id
cd ~/dsh-id
./install.sh                 # 拷到 ~/.local/{bin,lib}，建数据目录
dsh-id                       # 看状态（首次会提示还没有凭据）
```

`install.sh` 只做三件事：拷文件、`chmod 755`、建数据目录。它不启动任何常驻服务。

### 目录结构

```text
package.json  cordis.patch.yml  lib/   ← DSH bundle 本体
cli/bin/  cli/lib/                     ← 五个命令行 + 两个 Python 库
docs/plugin.md                         ← 插件安装与工具清单细则
install.sh  test.sh                    ← 装 CLI / 冒烟测试
```

---

## 用法

### 存一个凭据

```bash
dsh-id creds add github-pat bearer --domains api.github.com
# bearer / basic / header / query 四种注入方式
# 交互输入值，不回显；写入后磁盘上是密文（0600）
```

### 用它发请求

```bash
dsh-id exec github-pat https://api.github.com/user
dsh-id exec github-pat https://api.github.com/repos/me/repo -X POST -d '{}'
# HTTP >= 400 默认退出码 22（便于判成败）；加 --allow-http-error 仍返回 0

# 也可以把明文注入子进程环境变量，跑任意命令
dsh-id exec run github-pat -- sh -c 'curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $VAULT_SECRET" https://api.github.com/user'
```

域名不在该凭据的白名单里 → 直接拒绝，退出码 4。

### 存一个网页登录态

```bash
dsh-id session save github --url https://github.com/login --ttl-days 30
# 开可见窗口，你手动登录完回车；默认 30 天
dsh-id session list                                          # 域名、保存时间、过期时间
dsh-id session use github --headless                         # 打开就是登录态
dsh-id session check github                                  # 探一次，判断是否还有效
```

### 出事的时候

```bash
dsh-id creds panic --dry-run    # 先看会做什么
dsh-id creds panic              # 停服务 + 禁用开机自启 + 隔离全部密文
dsh-id creds restore            # 一条命令回来（自动找最新隔离目录）
```

`panic` 不会删你的密钥文件——密文被挪进 `.panic-<时间戳>/`，随时可恢复。

### 账目与审计

```bash
dsh-id creds audit-verify       # 逐行重算哈希链，指出第几行被动过
dsh-id creds audit-report       # 每件凭据的健康度（多久没换、白名单、过期）
dsh-id guard check "删除生产库" # → require_approval / allow
```

---

## DSH 插件

仓库根目录就是 bundle，把上面这些能力包成工具交给模型：

- 8 个只读工具：账号/凭据/会话**元数据**、审批队列、审计链校验、边界说明
- 4 个执行工具：带凭据发请求、用会话开浏览器、浏览器操作、关浏览器
- 全部工具都不返回凭据值；截图只返回文件路径，不返回 base64

细则见 [`docs/plugin.md`](docs/plugin.md)。它与 CLI 解耦，不装插件也能用命令行。

---

## 安全模型：它挡什么，挡不住什么

**设计上做到的**

- 磁盘上永远是密文（`openssl enc` / AES-256-CBC），密钥单独存放、权限 600
- 明文只在目标进程的环境变量里短暂存在，不进 argv、不进日志、不进对话
- 每次操作写审计（每行带 `prev_hash` + `hash`）
- 域名白名单：凭据只能用在登记过的主机上
- `panic` 一条命令让 AI 立刻失去全部凭据能力
- 会话文件加密存储，权限 600

**做不到的（请当它是「限制」，不是「隔离」）**

- **同用户的其他进程仍可读密钥文件**。这不是安全沙箱，是防手滑和防日志泄露的工程措施。真要隔离，得换用户/容器的边界。
- **审计哈希链防不住同权限重写整条链**，也发现不了尾部截断。它能让「改一行」这种篡改留下痕迹，仅此而已。
- **`guard` 是关键词闸门，不是强制审批**。`approve --who` 由调用方填写，不能当作真实审批签名；模型也可以绕开它直接调用底层命令。
- **`panic` 只隔离本地密文**：它不会吊销上游已经发出的 token，也不会终止别人已经打开的网页会话。真要止血，还得去平台后台 revoke。
- **会话「过期时间」是本地 TTL**，不代表站点侧真的还有效。`session check` 是启发式探测，结果是参考不是保证。
- 机器绑定自动解锁意味着：**能在这台机器上以这个用户身份跑代码的人，就能解密**。这是刻意的取舍（AI 要自主干活），不是疏忽。

这些边界在 `dsh-id creds status` 和插件的 `*_security_boundary` 工具里也如实标着。

---

## 现状与未完成

- 主密码默认关闭，用机器绑定自动解锁（`creds passwd` 可开启，作为可选加强项）
- 插件是「只读状态 + 执行能力」MVP，不是登录执行器；设置卡片是否可视化取决于 DSH 版本
- 只做了 Linux；`vault-session` 依赖 Chromium/Playwright
- 没有做多用户、没有做远程同步、没有做团队共享

---

## 兼容性

- Python 3.10+（标准库 + `openssl` 命令行，无第三方依赖）
- 插件针对 DSH `0.2.2-rc.1` 开发，devDependencies 见根目录 `package.json`
- 在 Arch Linux / Omarchy 上实测

---

## License

MIT，见 [LICENSE](LICENSE)。安全问题怎么报见 [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md)。

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# dsh-botplugin

把 Telegram / 微信变成 DSH 的聊天入口的插件。三大功能：**Telegram 入口、微信入口、handoff 记忆接续**，外加语音转文字。

> 🔰 **第一次接触、想知道"这东西到底能干什么"** → 先看 [功能说明.txt](功能说明.txt)（大白话版，不用懂技术）。
> 装的时候怎么填、怎么启动 → 看 [使用说明.txt](使用说明.txt)。下面这份是给要自己动手的人的完整文档。

## 环境要求

- Node ≥ 18
- 机器上装好 DSH（有 `dsh` 命令；没装的话先跑下面第 0 步）
- 一个 Telegram bot token（在 Telegram 里找 @BotFather 发送 `/newbot` 新建，不要和其他 bot 共用）

> 安装分成两件事，一个脚本管一头，互不越界：
> `setupdsh` = 升级（Git、Node、DSH 本体，外加已经装过机器人的工作区里的插件：装 + 升级）；
> `setupbot` = 建/选工作区、首次装插件、绑 TG / 微信、生成工作区里那 5 个文件（英文名，双击或终端里跑都行）。
> 机器上没有 `dsh` 时 `setupbot` 会自己把 `setupdsh` 跑一遍，所以顺序不用记。

## 安装方式一：在线安装（两条命令，推荐）

0. 先装/升级本体（Git、Node、DSH 一起办，可重复跑）：

   ```
   curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aitcmhk-web/DSH-bot/main/setupdsh.sh | sh
   ```

1. 再装机器人 —— 把下面这条整段贴进终端，回车：

   ```
   curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aitcmhk-web/DSH-bot/main/setupbot.sh | sh
   ```

   它自己列出/新建工作区、自己把插件装好，然后**只问你三件事**：
   工作区叫什么（直接回车就叫 `mybot`）、Telegram token（@BotFather 那串）、微信怎么绑（可选）。
   每样都是「输个编号」或「粘一下回车」，不用你编辑任何文件。

2. 跑完它会把两个词装进 PATH —— **以后升级（本体 + 插件）敲 `setupdsh`；
   重新绑 TG、重新绑微信敲 `setupbot`**：

   ```
   setupdsh
   setupbot
   ```

3. 启动：照着它最后打出来的那行，或者跑 `~/DSH/<工作区名>/start.command`
   （同目录里另有 `stop.command`、`restart.command`、`install-autostart.command`、`uninstall-autostart.command`）。

> 那五个文件**名字一律英文**：有桌面双击，没桌面（云主机 / 只有终端）就
> `cd ~/DSH/<工作区名> && ./start.command`。中文文件名在纯终端里得切输入法，太别扭。

## 开发者：本地安装（用你手上这份源码）

已经有一份源码（比如你自己 clone 下来的、或者要改着调试的），就用 `file:` 指向**那个目录**：

```
dsh plugin --profile mybot add file:/绝对路径/dsh-botplugin
```

例如源码在 `~/DSH/botplugin`：

```
dsh plugin --profile mybot add file:$HOME/DSH/botplugin
```

> ⚠️ `file:` 后面**不能写 `~`** —— 它不会展开波浪号，会当成字面路径找不到。用 `$HOME/` 或完整绝对路径。

> 用 `file:` 装出来的是**软链** —— 改完源码不用重装，重启 profile 就生效。
> 调试的时候用这个；平时用上面的 git 方式。**两种选一种，别都装**
> （会装出两份同名插件，加载哪份不好说）。
>
> ⚠️ 路径必须是**绝对路径**，且指向**含 `package.json` 的那一层**（也就是仓库根），
> 不要指到 `src/` 或上一层。

## 安装方式二：下载安装包（不想敲命令的）

1. 下载安装包：[dsh-mybot-安装包.zip](dsh-mybot-安装包.zip)（在本页文件列表里，点它再点 Download / Download raw）。
2. 解压，双击里面的 `安装-mybot.command`。
3. 接下来和在线方式**完全一样**：问你工作区名字（直接回车就叫 `mybot`）→ 粘 token → 微信要不要绑。
   窗口最后会停住等你按回车，结果不会一闪而过。
4. 以后每次使用：跑 `~/DSH/<工作区名>/start.command`（`stop.command` / `restart.command` / `install-autostart.command` / `uninstall-autostart.command` 是同一个目录里的另外四个文件）。
   想重新绑 TG / 微信：把 `安装-mybot.command` 再双击一次（或在终端敲 `setupbot`）。
   想升级（Git / Node / DSH 本体 / 已经装过机器人的工作区里的插件）：在终端敲 `setupdsh`（安装包里也带了这个脚本）。

> 两种方式装出来的是同一个插件，跑的是同一个 `setupbot.sh`，选一种就行。
> 安装包方式适合完全不想碰命令行的人；在线方式第一次要粘两条命令，之后也只剩 `setupdsh` / `setupbot` 两个词。

## 怎么确认装对了

脚本跑到最后会打「✅ 复核通过：配置已经生效」—— 看到这句就是装对了，它紧接着会给你启动命令。

没看到这句、或者它报「插件没装上」= 没装成，插件不会生效（而且**不报错**，只会静默什么都没发生）。

## 配置项速查

| 配置 | 说明 |
|---|---|
| `telegramToken` / `telegramApiRoot` | TG 必填；apiRoot 指向代理时改 |
| `telegramAllowedUsers` | 允许的 TG 用户 ID；空 = 首个发消息者认领为主人 |
| `weixinToken` / `weixinApiRoot` / `weixinAccountFile` | 微信入口（通常用扫码登录，不用填 token） |
| `routes` + `defaultRouteKey` | 手工指定模型档位；留空 = 自动跟随 web 端「设置 → 模型」 |
| `cwd` | 模型的工作目录 |
| `memoryDir` / `memoryScript` | handoff 记忆接续：**默认开启**（`<工作目录>/memory` + 插件自带的记账程序），不用配；要关闭把 memoryDir 设成空串 |
| `restartCommand` | 重启用的启动器 .command 路径；不填默认找工作目录里的 `start.command`（兼容老的 `启动-<工作区名>.command` / `启动-mybot.command`） |
| `turnTimeoutMs` | 单轮超时，默认 **90 分钟**（2026-10-20 由 30 抬上来：满 30 分钟就判超时并把这一轮答案丢掉） |
| `asrBackend` / `asrWhisperBin` / `asrPythonBin` | 语音转文字。默认 **sensevoice**（阿里 FunASR，中文准），不填路径就自动找 `/opt/homebrew/bin/python3.11`；本机没装时，安装收尾和发语音都会回一条可粘贴的安装命令（⛔ 不自动装）。`whisper` 中文差，只有显式填 `asrBackend: whisper` 才用 |
| `llmBudget` | 模型流量闸：滚动 60 秒内请求数与 token 数封顶（默认 **50 次 / 90 万 token**），超了排队等，别撞供应商的 TPM 限额。字段：`enabled`（默认 true，关掉=不限流）/ `tpm` / `rpm` / `输出预留`（每次先占多少输出 token，默认 8000）/ `最长等待毫秒`（默认 10 分钟，等满就放行并打告警） |

## 模型流量闸（每分钟限额，2026-10-19 加）

一回合里跑工具、开子代理都会**反复**发模型请求，一分钟里的累计很容易顶到供应商的
TPM/RPM 限额（撞上就是 429）。插件在宿主 llm 的 `llm/stream` 上挂了一道闸
（`src/llm-budget.js`）：**滚动 60 秒窗口内 请求数 ≤ `rpm`、token 合计 ≤ `tpm`**，
快满时让下一次调用**排队等**到窗口腾位，⛔ 不丢请求、⛔ 不改流里的内容。

- **记账口径**：调前按请求体的可读字符量**预估**（中文 1 token/字、其余 1/4，另加输出预留），
  流里收到宿主 `usage` 块后换成**实际用量**（替换，不叠加）；失败/中断的那次仍按预估留在账上（保守）。
- **fail-open**：单次最多等 `最长等待毫秒`（默认 10 分钟），等满仍无额度就**放行一次并打告警**——
  宁可偶尔超一次，也不让整台 bot 卡死。
- **子代理与工具循环一样算**：它们都走同一条 waterfall，所以一处就管住全机流量。
- **默认口径**：`rpm` 50 次 / `tpm` **90 万 token**（2026-10-19 定的最终值）。供应商（百度千帆）的
  **TPM 限额是 100 万**，90 万是留一成余量。一条请求就带十几万 token（整段历史重发），所以一分钟
  大约放六七发 —— 这是硬约束，要更快只能少发请求，⛔ 不能靠抬闸。
  ⛔ 历史上曾抬到 300 万（当时误判「供应商限的是请求密度、不是 token 量」），拿到实数后已收回。
- **关掉**：配置里 `llmBudget.enabled: false`（出问题时可一键停，不影响启动）。

## 会话压缩口径（随版本下发，2026-10-19 加）

插件作为 profile 层装上时，会顺手把**会话压缩**的口径打进 profile：本包的
`cordis.patch.yml`（`package.json` 的 `dsh.bundle.patch`）多打一行 `compaction-basic`。
宿主代码默认 `thresholdRatio 0.8` —— 在百万窗口上等于 **80 万 token 才压缩**，
正常对话根本触发不到，历史只能近乎全量重发，越聊越慢。

本包一律下发**比例制**（两个数都随窗口缩放，任何窗口都自洽）：

| 键 | 值 | 作用 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `thresholdRatio` | `0.15` | 窗口的 15% 触发压缩（百万窗口 = 15 万 token） |
| `retainRatio` | `0.08` | 压缩后按窗口留约 8%（百万窗口 ≈ 5 万 token） |
| `headroomTokens` | `8192` | 预留空间。出厂默认 65536 比小窗口本身还大，会把压力预算算成负数 |

⛔ **不要再用 `retainTokens`（绝对保留量）**：它是绝对值、不随窗口缩放，宿主会校验
「保留量必须小于触发线」，小窗口模型（如 6.5 万窗口）配上几万的绝对值会被判非法并抛
`TargetPressureConfigError` —— 压缩整个失效、历史无限增长，直到上下文溢出。

补丁顺序是「出厂 → 本插件 → 用户 profile 的 `cordis.patch.yml`」，最后一个写的人赢，
所以用户 profile 想改仍盖得住本包，这里只是把合理默认变成**可分发**的东西。

## 远程审批（手机点按钮，不用守着电脑）

DSH 的审批服务用 waterfall 广播 `approval/request`，插件把它桥接到 Telegram——
推一张和 web 端审批面板**同口径**的卡片（`等待审批 / 已允许 / 已拒绝 / 已取消 / 已超时`
+ 命令、工作目录、原因），下面挂两个内联按钮【✅ 允许一次】【❌ 拒绝】。
点完卡片收成终态并去掉按钮。

> 桥是**只读旁路**：卡片渲染失败、编辑失败、按钮超时，统统只记日志，
> **绝不影响审批本身的结果**（该通过的照常通过）。
> 行动端入口在 `src/approval-bridge.js`，默认超时 10 分钟。

## 多端互通（TG ⇄ 微信，同一个大脑）

`src/hub.js` 是所有端点的唯一交汇点，纯逻辑、零依赖。两条规则，都是「同步到所有」：

| 方向 | 行为 |
|---|---|
| 端点到 hub | 同步给 ① DSH ② **其他所有端点** |
| DSH 到 hub | 同步发到**所有端点** |

新增端点 = 加一个数组项（O(n)），**不是**两两镜像（O(n²)）。
微信消息并入**主人的 TG 会话**，所以两边聊的是同一段上下文，
在微信里 `/new`、`/model` 操作的是同一个会话。

> ⛔ 这里刻意**不做去重/合并**：TG 和微信各进来一条就是两次真实输入，进来几条算几条。

## 指令

`/whoami` `/status` `/model` `/new`（新会话） `/restart`（重启进程，先留档） `/help`

> `/model`（含菜单按钮与微信编号）＝**当场切档**：往当前会话日志追加一条档位记录，下一条消息就用新档，句柄与历史都不动；手选结果记进 `.botplugin-state.json`（记忆位），重启后照旧生效。会话在用期间，刷新⛔ 拿旧记忆盖回在用档（v1.1.11 修：此前表现为「点了没反应」；v1.1.12 修到模型本身——此前只重建句柄，恢复后仍按日志里记的旧档发请求）。

> `/restart` 与老 bot 同路：先把进展写进 handoff，再由**进程外的接力脚本**延迟几秒杀掉宿主并重新拉起（有 `start.command`（兼容老的 `启动-<工作区名>.command` / `启动-mybot.command`）就重开终端窗口；没有就按原始命令行后台拉起）。两者都没有时退化为只重开会话。重启完成后发条消息，新会话自动带上刚才的记忆。

## 记忆（流水账 + handoff）

默认开启，什么都不用配：

- **流水账**：每轮对话原文追加到 `<工作目录>/memory/conversation-cache/raw/ledger/`，按月一个文件，只增不删。
- **handoff**：`/new`、切换模型（本次会话满 20 条才写，调试期反复切不会覆盖）、`/restart`（无条件）和启动补写时，把最近 20 条进展落盘到 `<工作目录>/memory/handoff/handoff.md`。
- **冷启动注入**：新会话的第一条消息会自动带上最近一次 handoff，模型直接接着上段干，不用你复述上文。
- 记账程序随插件自带（`vendor/conversation-cache/`），不依赖机器上是否装过 DSH 的其它项目。
- 想换位置或关闭：配置里写 `memoryDir`（自定路径；**空串 = 关闭**）、`memoryScript`（自定程序路径）。

## 微信入口（扫码绑定）

1. 运行（本目录下）：

   ```
   node weixin-login.mjs --out 你的账号文件路径
   ```

2. 手机微信扫终端二维码（约 2 分钟过期，自动刷新；备用链接发到手机微信里点开）。
3. 凭据写入账号文件（0600）→ 在配置里加 `weixinAccountFile: 那个路径` → 重启即启用。
4. 扫码的这个微信就是主人，只有它能和 bot 对话。

## ⚠️ 三条硬注意事项

1. **一个 token 只能一个进程**。两个进程抢同一个 token，先启动的会 409 冲突。
2. **Telegram 游标在内存里**：重启后从当前时刻开始拉消息，不补发离线期间的旧消息。
3. **409 冲突时插件只停自己的轮询并打日志**，不会拖垮宿主；原因要去启动日志里看（通常是同一个 token 另有进程在用）。

## 已知限制

- 微信扫码工具用 macOS 原生 CoreImage 渲染二维码（零依赖），Windows/Linux 机器上会退化为只打印链接。
- **回答由节点（hub）广播到所有端点**（2026-10-19 定）：大模型 → 节点 → 广播，**含来源通道本身**，出口只有一个。
  进度占位消息**只报进度**，⛔ 收尾不在它上面写「✅ 已回复」（2026-10-20 起：回答进窗口后**把气泡删掉**），⛔ 不再承载最终回答 —— 同一条消息上出现两个写者
  （进度编辑 / 收尾回答）时，迟到的进度编辑会把回答盖回去，而且日志里看不出任何异常（2026-10-19 线上丢件的成因）。
- **Telegram 限流（429）不丢答案**：发消息这一层（`sendRich`）照 Telegram 给的 `retry_after` 排队重发
  （单次最多等 90s、一轮最多 3 分钟，等待总预算可用 `DSH_BOTPLUGIN_RATE_LIMIT_BUDGET_MS` 调整，默认 180000）；
  回答广播到 TG 失败时，整篇回答落盘到 `DSH_BOT_DIR/未送达/`（可用 `DSH_BOTPLUGIN_UNDELIVERED_DIR` 指定别的目录），
  同时把占位消息改成「❌ 回答未送达…已存到 <路径>」——旧版遇限流会留下永远的「⏳ 正在处理…」并丢掉答案。
- **进度消息只显示「正在做什么」**（2026-10-18 口径，同日修订）：正文里带 `[进度] …` 标记的行，加工具的中文动作标签，
  标签后面接**具体在干什么**——如「🏃 跑命令：grep -rn notes src/index.js」「🛠 改文件：服务.mjs」
  （只留文件名，不带目录）。模型思考（reasoning 块）一律不上屏；口令类字面量自动打码
  （`PGPASSWORD=***`、`Bearer ***`）。抠不出细节的工具只留标签、不编占位词；认不出的工具原样给个 `🔧 名字`。
  工具标签可用 `DSH_BOTPLUGIN_PROGRESS_TOOLS=0` 关掉，只留进度行。
- 进度占位消息的版式（2026-10-19 定）：**顶行 ＝ 我最新说的那句话**——它顶掉原来「⏳ 正在处理…」那几个字，
  我还没开口时才显示那句占位语；⛔ **不显示已耗时**。底下滚动的是**操作**（工具标签、📌 进度行，最近 3 条），
  与顶行互不影响。**只在我出新话（或新操作）时编辑一次**，⛔ 不做定时刷新（旧版每 2s／4s 刷一次，
  秒数一变就编辑，内容其实没变，白撞限流）。吐字速度小尾巴跟**回答**走，气泡上不重复显示。
  **上面顶行出全文、底下三条操作行照旧掐字**（2026-10-25 先定「你的输出不要截断 120 字、出全文」，
  同日再厘清「底下那三条操作提示不变」）：顶行那句走 `顶行_MAX = 0`＝**不掐**（`truncate(text, max)`
  见 `max ≤ 0` 即原样返回）；📌 进度行与工具提示仍各自掐到 120／90／60／80／40 字
  （`操作行_MAX = 120` ＋ `摘要()` 里那几个数）——两个常量各管一路：同日早些时候那次「一律出全文」
  把操作行也放开了、版式被撑散，故拆开；要收更紧就改 `操作行_MAX` 与那几个数。
  **收尾不写那一行「✅ 已回复」**（2026-10-20 起）：回答进窗口后**把气泡删掉**；没送达才保留气泡并改标「未送达」。
  收尾前先等「已经在飞」的那次进度编辑落地，⛔ 不让它回头盖掉进度文本。


## 等待上限 90 分钟（2026-10-20 起；进度哨兵已删）

- **为什么抬**：原来是 30 分钟。`turnTimeoutMs` 一到就判「等待回复超时」，**这一轮的答案当场丢掉**，
  主人只会看到一句 `❌ 等待回复超时（30 分钟）` —— 白干一轮。老板 2026-10-20 定：抬到 **90 分钟**。
- **等久一点 ≠ 让你多等**：它只是「最多等多久才放弃」的上限；活干几分钟就是几分钟。
- **配置**：`turnTimeoutMs`（毫秒，默认 `90 * 60 * 1000`）。超时那句话跟着实际值现算
  （`runtime.js`：`等待回复超时（${Math.round(timeoutMs / 60000)} 分钟）`），⛔ 不再写死「30 分钟」。
- **回退**：改回 `30 * 60 * 1000` 即回到旧行为。
- ⛔ **进度哨兵已删除**（2026-10-20 老板定「哨兵不起作用，删除哨兵」）：旧版在进程外放一个 `哨兵.mjs`，
  每 20 分钟用主 bot 令牌代报一句「还在干活」。老板判定它不起作用，改走「抬等待上限」这一条路 ——
  模块 `src/progress-sentinel.js`、四项配置（`sentinelEnabled`／`sentinelScript`／`sentinelStateFile`／
  `sentinelIntervalMinutes`）、自测件 `test-progress-sentinel.mjs`，以及项目根的 `哨兵.mjs`／`哨兵状态.json`
  全部删除。**回退办法**：装回 `v1.1.2`。

## 发版规矩（2026-10-19 定）

- **版本号末段最多到 99**：第 100 版起**直接进位** —— `1.0.99` → `1.1.1`，⛔ 不再出现 `1.0.100` 这种末段三位数。
- 升版本号必须**同一个 commit** 里一起改**三处**：`package.json` 的 `version`、`package-lock.json`（两处）、`setupdsh.sh` 的 `BOTPLUGIN_SPEC` 默认 tag。本仓 pre-commit 闸（`.githooks/发版对账.sh`）会拦「只改一边」与「末段 > 99」。
- 发完把提交与 `git tag v<版本>` 一起推到 `origin`；装到本机用 `npm install github:aitcmhk-web/DSH-bot#v<版本>`（⛔ 别用裸 `npm install`：旧锁文件会把版本带回上一个 tag）。

## 许可

MIT License（全文见 [LICENSE](LICENSE)）：可以自由使用、修改、再发布，保留版权声明即可；软件不提供任何担保。

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# coursework-author

Author a structured, module-based self-study course on any technical topic: a
`syllabus.md` blueprint, one `README.md` per module in a fixed anatomy, and two
verification gates — a memory-less logic review and a literature survey — that a module
must clear before it is marked `✅ verified`.

Ships one skill: `skills/coursework-author/SKILL.md`. Works with Claude Code, Codex,
Gemini and DSH; the `lib/` + `cordis.patch.yml` pairing is DSH's mounting glue only.

Consumed by [`explainer-video-from-coursework`](https://github.com/akshayDev17/ai-explainer-video),
which vendors this skill at release time so that installing the video pipeline also gives
you the authoring half. That is a soft pairing: authoring a course never requires video,
and video work never requires this package to be installed separately.

# my-skills-package

A shelf of skill plugins — **one npm package per skill**, each installable on Claude Code,
Codex, Gemini/Antigravity and DeepSeek Harness. Adding a skill means adding a directory under
`packages/`; it does not touch its neighbours, and each package carries its own version.
Plugins that only Claude Code can run live under `plugins/` instead. They are delivered
straight from this repo, with no npm package.

| package | what it does |
|---|---|
| [`coursework-author`](./packages/coursework-author) | Author a structured, module-based self-study course on any topic: syllabus blueprint, one README per module, a fixed module anatomy, then two verification gates (a memory-less logic review and a literature survey). |
| [`@akshaydev17/portfolio-app`](./packages/portfolio-app) | Bootstrap a sub-app of the personal site in one command: its Cloudflare Access app for the path, its D1 database id, and its GitHub `production` secrets. With `--public`, a sub-app meant for everyone gets its D1 database, R2 bucket, its one `<prefix>*` Worker route and secrets with no Access step. With `--public-path` (repeatable), a sub-app that is signed in by default also gets a Bypass-for-Everyone Access app on exactly the named public paths. Plans by default and applies on `--apply`. Also ships `verify`, a token-free login check that deploy jobs run first. Not yet published to npm. |
| [`graph-notes`](./plugins/graph-notes) (Claude Code only) | Read and edit your graph-notes graphs (knowledge graphs kept as Obsidian canvases) as notes and links. Bundles the graph-notes MCP server, which uv runs and which signs in through cloudflared, and a skill on editing graphs well. |

## Install

Every host installs the **same** npm package and reads only its own manifest surface out of it.
The marketplace catalogue that lists these packages lives in this repo, because Claude Code
accepts npm as a *plugin* source but not as a *marketplace* source.

**Claude Code**

```sh
claude plugin marketplace add akshayDev17/my-skills-package
claude plugin install coursework-author@akshaydev17-skills
```

**Codex**

```sh
codex plugin marketplace add akshayDev17/my-skills-package
codex plugin add coursework-author@akshaydev17-skills
```

**DeepSeek Harness**

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add coursework-author
```

**Gemini / Antigravity**

```sh
agy plugin install https://github.com/akshayDev17/my-skills-package
```

`graph-notes` is Claude Code only, and comes from this repo rather than npm:

```sh
claude plugin marketplace add akshayDev17/my-skills-package
claude plugin install graph-notes@akshaydev17-skills
```

Verify what actually loaded, rather than trusting the install:

```sh
claude plugin details coursework-author@akshaydev17-skills     # component inventory
claude plugin list                                             # version + enabled
```

## The pair is optional, in both directions

`coursework-author` is also shipped *inside*
[`explainer-video-from-coursework`](https://github.com/akshayDev17/ai-explainer-video): that
plugin vendors a copy of this skill so one install gives you both — author the coursework, then
turn it into videos. The copy is generated (`scripts/sync-coursework-author.mjs` over there) and
gated in that repo's CI, never hand-edited.

Neither direction is forced. Installing the video plugin does not install this package, and
installing this package does not pull in the video toolchain. You get the pairing by choosing
the video plugin; you get a standalone authoring skill by choosing this one.

## Layout

```
packages/<skill>/                 one npm package per skill
  package.json                    dsh.bundle.patch → cordis.patch.yml
  plugin.json                     Agent Plugins manifest (Codex, Gemini/Antigravity)
  .claude-plugin/plugin.json      Claude Code manifest
  cordis.patch.yml + lib/index.js the DSH bundle plugin (serves this package's skills/)
  skills/<skill>/SKILL.md         the skill itself
plugins/<plugin>/                 Claude-only plugins, delivered by path (no npm package)
  .claude-plugin/plugin.json      Claude Code manifest
  .mcp.json, skills/, ...         whatever the plugin ships
.claude-plugin/marketplace.json   Claude Code catalogue
.agents/plugins/marketplace.json  Codex / Antigravity catalogue
scripts/                          version bump, release helpers, CI gates
```

Both catalogue files pin the version a host installs from npm (`source: npm`, `version: ^x.y.z`)
for every package under `packages/`. A plugin under `plugins/` is listed only in the Claude
catalogue, with its path as the source (`"source": "./plugins/<plugin>"`), and
`scripts/check-path-plugins.mjs` checks it.
`scripts/bump-package.mjs` rewrites the pin during a release and
`scripts/check-marketplace-pins.mjs` fails CI when a pin disagrees with its package — a
hand-maintained range rots without a symptom, which is exactly what happened in the video repo.

## Releasing

Nothing publishes on a merge. (A plugin under `plugins/` has no npm package: merging a change to
it is its release.) A release is a manual dispatch of `release.yml`, one package at a
time, with an independent version and a `<package>@<semver>` tag — see
[`RELEASING.md`](./RELEASING.md).

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# @akshaydev17/portfolio-app

Set up a new sub-app of the personal site in one command, and check from CI that its path is
behind Cloudflare Access before every deploy. A sub-app meant for everyone can instead be set up
as a public app with `--public`, which skips Access and gives it an R2 bucket and the Worker
route `<domain>/<prefix>*`.
A sub-app that is signed in by default but has a few public paths is a mixed app: name each
public path with `--public-path`, and it gets a second Access app whose destinations are exactly
those paths. A path listed without a final `/*` is meant to be public on its own, so its Allow
app also gets a narrowing `<path>/*` that keeps the paths under it behind sign-in, and they are
checked to still ask for it.

Ships one skill (`skills/portfolio-app/SKILL.md`) and the script it drives
(`skills/portfolio-app/scripts/portfolio-app.mjs`), which is also the package's `portfolio-app`
bin, so it runs with or without an agent. Works with Claude Code, Codex, Gemini and DSH; the
`lib/` + `cordis.patch.yml` pairing is DSH's mounting glue only. Node 20+, no dependencies.

## `bootstrap`

```sh
portfolio-app bootstrap --repo <owner/name> --path /<prefix> [--public | --public-path <path>…]
                        [--d1 <name>] [--clone <dir>] [--apply]
```

A prefix may have several segments (`/work/election-atlas`). Without `--public`, three steps,
each one only filling in what is missing:

1. **Cloudflare Access.** Find or create one reusable *allow* policy named
   `portfolio-app sign-in` that includes the config's `allowedEmails`. Then find or create a self-hosted Access
   app whose destinations are exactly `<domain>/<prefix>` and `<domain>/<prefix>/*`, attached to
   that policy. With `--apply`, it then waits until the path redirects (3xx) to
   `<team>.cloudflareaccess.com/cdn-cgi/access/login/…`, and stops before touching D1 or GitHub
   if it never does.
2. **D1.** Find the database by name or create it, then write its id into the clone's
   `backend/wrangler.jsonc`, replacing the `REPLACE_AFTER_d1_create` placeholder (comments are
   preserved). The commit is left to the repo's normal delivery path. `--clone` defaults to the
   current directory, and its `origin` must be `--repo`. `--d1` defaults to the `database_name`
   of the entry that holds the placeholder.
3. **GitHub.** Create the repo's `production` environment and set `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` (the
   narrow deploy token) and `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID` through `gh`. Secret values go to `gh` over
   stdin, never in argv.

### `--public`: an app anyone can reach

Only `--public` makes an app public: there is no config default and nothing is inferred from
the repo or the path. The plan's header says `(public: no Access sign-in)` and its first line
says the two destinations will be reachable by anyone. The steps, in apply order:

1. **No Access.** No policy and no Access app are created, and apply does not wait for a
   login redirect. If an Access app already guards either destination, or the path already
   redirects to an Access login (a wider app such as `<domain>/work/*`), the plan is a
   conflict: the tool never removes protection.
2. **D1**, as above.
3. **R2.** Find the bucket by name or create it. The name is the single `bucket_name` in the
   clone's `r2_buckets` (several names are a conflict; none means no R2 step).
4. **Worker route.** Exactly one, `<domain>/<prefix>*`, pointing at the Worker named by `name`
   in the clone's `backend/wrangler.jsonc` (why one route and not `<domain>/<prefix>` +
   `<domain>/<prefix>/*`, and what the Worker must do with it: see
   [The Worker route and its pass-through](#the-worker-route-and-its-pass-through)). A route
   can only name a deployed Worker (see the research notes), so before the first deploy the
   plan says so and creates nothing here; re-run after that deploy to add the route. With
   `--apply`, whenever the route exists or this run creates it, it waits until the route check
   passes, and stops before GitHub, deleting nothing, if it never does (a route this run created
   stays in place). The check, signed out: `/<prefix>?portfolio-app-verify=1` must answer with
   the status `/<prefix>` answers with, or redirect to `/<prefix>` or a path under `/<prefix>/`
   on the same host, with neither answer from the origin nor a redirect to an Access login; and
   `/<prefix>portfolio-app-verify` must come from the origin. "From the origin" means the answer
   carries GitHub Pages' `x-github-request-id` header. A query probe from the origin means the
   Worker route misses `/<prefix>?<query>`; a sibling probe without the header means the Worker
   serves paths outside its prefix; an Access login redirect means nothing about the route can
   be told signed out. An app bootstrapped
   before this change holds that same Worker's exact pair `<domain>/<prefix>` +
   `<domain>/<prefix>/*`: the plan shows each as a `-` line, and apply deletes them only after
   `<domain>/<prefix>*` exists and the check passes. Both point at the same Worker, so the app
   answers throughout.
5. **GitHub**, as above.

`verify` fails by design on a public path, so a public app's deploy job does not run it.

### `--public-path`: signed in by default, with named public paths

A mixed app is a private app (all of the above) plus a list of public paths given on the
command line, one `--public-path` per path. Nothing is inferred: a path is public only when it
is listed. Each path is one of:

- `/<prefix>` itself;
- `/<prefix>/`, the prefix's trailing-slash path, exactly, and only alongside `/<prefix>` (see
  below);
- an exact path under it, such as `/graph/public.txt`;
- a directory under it with a final `/*`, such as `/graph/_next/*`.

A path without a final `/*` is meant to be public on its own, not with what is under it:
`/graph/public` does not make `/graph/public/x` public. Cloudflare lets a sub-path inherit its
parent path's rule, so on its own an exact Bypass destination opens its children too (seen on
the live account; see the research notes). So the Allow app gets a **narrowing destination**
`<path>/*` for each such path: `/graph/public` adds `<domain>/graph/public/*`. It is more specific
than the inherited `<domain>/graph/public`, so the children ask for sign-in while the path itself
stays public. None is added for the bare prefix, whose children are the Allow app's own
`<prefix>/*` already, nor for a path whose children another listed `/*` path makes public. The
tool still requests a child of each exact public path and requires the Access login; if one
answers signed out, `--apply` stops and `verify` fails, naming that child. To make the children
public too, list `<path>/*` as well.

The leading `/` is optional. Refused before anything is read: a path outside the prefix,
`/<prefix>/*` (the whole app; that is `--public`), a `*` anywhere but a final `/*`, empty, `.` or
`..` segments (the one exception is `/<prefix>/` itself: `/<prefix>//`, `/<prefix>/x/` and
`/<prefix>//x` are refused), queries, and `--public` together with `--public-path`.

**The trailing-slash path `/<prefix>/`.** `/time-track` and `/time-track/` are two request paths,
and Access tells them apart: with `time-track` public and `time-track/*` behind sign-in, the first
answers signed out and the second asks for sign-in (seen on the live account). Listing
`/<prefix>/` makes exactly `<domain>/<prefix>/` a public destination. It gets no narrowing
destination: that would be `<prefix>/*`, which the Allow app already holds. But it is the parent
of every page under the prefix, and an Access destination covers its subpaths too; the docs do
not say whether `<prefix>/` or the Allow app's `<prefix>/*` is the more specific for
`<prefix>/<child>` (see the research notes). So the plan says the children are meant for the
Allow app and that a child is checked, and `--apply` probes `<prefix>/portfolio-app-verify` and
`<prefix>/api/portfolio-app-verify`, which must still redirect to the login. If this run added
`<prefix>/` and they answer signed out, or the check fails in any other way, apply takes
`<prefix>/` out of the public app again (step 5 below). A run that does not add it (a re-run
after it is in place) only reports a failed check and removes nothing, and the plan's line for
the children says which of the two applies.

`/<prefix>/` is accepted only alongside `/<prefix>`. Listing `--public-path /<prefix>/` without
`--public-path /<prefix>` is a plan conflict (`✗`, exit 2, nothing applied), whether the public
app is new or already exists. That way the public app always holds the bare prefix, so taking
`<prefix>/` out again always leaves it a destination to keep, and the tool never has to delete
an app.

```sh
# time-track: everything signed in except the landing page and its static assets
portfolio-app bootstrap --repo owner/time-track --path /time-track \
  --public-path /time-track --public-path '/time-track/_next/*' --clone ../time-track

# graph-notes: its Allow app and D1 came first; a first mixed run on such an app adds the
# public app, and the narrowing destinations for its three exact public paths to the Allow app
portfolio-app bootstrap --repo owner/graph-notes --path /graph \
  --public-path /graph/public --public-path /graph/public.txt --public-path '/graph/_next/*' \
  --public-path '/graph/icons/*' --public-path /graph/manifest.webmanifest \
  --public-path '/graph/api/public/*' --clone ../graph-notes
```

Both apps are set up on the live account now, so re-running either command plans zero changes.
graph-notes' Allow app already holds its three narrowing destinations (the owner approved adding
them on 2026-11-15) and its public app matches the list; its Access section reads:

```
  ✓ reusable policy "portfolio-app sign-in" exists
  ✓ Access app "graph-notes (/graph)" guards example.com/graph + example.com/graph/* + example.com/graph/public/* + example.com/graph/public.txt/* + example.com/graph/manifest.webmanifest/*
  ✓ Bypass app "graph-notes (public)" lets anyone reach example.com/graph/public + example.com/graph/public.txt + example.com/graph/_next/* + example.com/graph/icons/* + example.com/graph/manifest.webmanifest + example.com/graph/api/public/*
  · who answers (…): one line per destination, as below
  ✓ /graph already redirects to <team>.cloudflareaccess.com, and its public paths answer signed out
…
nothing to create — already bootstrapped
```

time-track's only exact public path is the bare prefix, so it has no narrowing destination:

```
  ✓ reusable policy "portfolio-app sign-in" exists
  ✓ Access app "time-track (/time-track)" guards example.com/time-track/*
  ✓ Bypass app "time-track (public)" lets anyone reach example.com/time-track + example.com/time-track/_next/*
  · who answers (…)
  ✓ /time-track already redirects to <team>.cloudflareaccess.com, and its public paths answer signed out
…
nothing to create — already bootstrapped
```

Signed out, `/time-track/` (with the slash) still asks for sign-in, because only the exact
`time-track` is public. The owner's fix is the same command with that path listed too:

```sh
portfolio-app bootstrap --repo owner/time-track --path /time-track \
  --public-path /time-track --public-path '/time-track/_next/*' --public-path /time-track/ \
  --clone ../time-track
```

It plans one change, to the public app only:

```
  ✓ Bypass app "time-track (public)" lets anyone reach example.com/time-track + example.com/time-track/_next/*
  + add public destination(s) example.com/time-track/ to Bypass app "time-track (public)" (anyone, no sign-in)
  · who answers (…):
  ·   example.com/time-track → "time-track (public)" — Bypass, anyone
  ·   example.com/time-track/_next/* → "time-track (public)" — Bypass, anyone
  ·   example.com/time-track/ → "time-track (public)" — Bypass, anyone
  ·   example.com/time-track/* (the rest) → "time-track (/time-track)" — Allow, sign-in
  ·   example.com/time-track/<child> → "time-track (/time-track)" (by example.com/time-track/*) — Allow, sign-in; example.com/time-track/ covers its subpaths too and the docs do not rank it against example.com/time-track/*, so apply checks a child and takes example.com/time-track/ out again if one answers signed out
…
1 change(s) planned
```

`verify` for time-track then takes the same three `--public-path` flags.

The Cloudflare Access step, in apply order:

1. **The Allow app**, as for a private app, on `<domain>/<prefix>` and `<domain>/<prefix>/*`,
   plus a narrowing `<domain><path>/*` for each exact public path (above). If `/<prefix>` itself
   is public, that destination is left out, so time-track's Allow app holds only
   `<domain>/time-track/*`. An existing Allow app that holds the base destinations and some or
   none of the narrowing ones is reused, and the plan shows
   `+ add narrowing destination(s) … to "<app>"` for the missing ones. That is the one change the
   tool makes to an existing Allow app, and it only shrinks what is public (the other change it
   makes to an existing app is adding newly listed paths to the public app, step 3). Apply reads
   the app again, refuses if its destinations changed since the plan, and sends it back with
   `PUT` (which replaces the whole app) carrying every current setting, the same policies by id and
   precedence, and only the missing destinations added. It never removes or alters any other
   destination, policy or setting. This comes before the Bypass app, so no child is ever public.
2. **The Bypass policy.** Find or create one reusable policy named `portfolio-app public`, with
   decision *bypass* and the single include rule *Everyone*. If a policy by that name exists and
   is anything else, the plan is a conflict; the tool does not rewrite it.
3. **The Bypass app** `<repo name> (public)` (graph-notes gets `graph-notes (public)`), whose
   destinations are exactly the listed paths, attached to that policy. An existing app holding
   exactly those destinations, all of whose policies are Bypass for Everyone, is reused under
   whatever name it has. An existing `<repo name> (public)` that holds only some of the listed
   paths and nothing else, is Bypass for Everyone and can take a plain `PUT` (self-hosted, its
   paths in `destinations`, all public hostnames) gets the missing ones added, the same way as
   the narrowing destinations: the plan shows `+ add public destination(s) … to Bypass app
   "<app>"`, and apply reads the app again, refuses if it changed since the plan, and sends it
   back with only those destinations added. So a re-run with one more `--public-path` adds only
   that destination.
4. **Wait for both answers.** With `--apply`, it waits until every private probe redirects to
   the Access login and every public path answers signed out (see `verify` below), and stops
   before D1 or GitHub if that never happens. The private probes include a child of each public
   path listed without a `/*`, so a run whose exact public paths open their children despite
   the narrowing destinations stops here, with both Access apps already in place; nothing is
   removed for you (the one exception is a run that added `<prefix>/`, step 5).
   The two apps start answering at different moments, so the first round in which every probe
   passes may hold private answers taken before the Bypass app was live. That round is run
   again at once, and apply goes on only when the second run passes too. If the second run
   fails, the wait carries on like after any failed round, until a round and its second run
   both pass or the attempts run out.
5. **Take `<prefix>/` out again, if this run added it and the wait fails.** This applies only
   to a run that added the trailing-slash destination `<domain>/<prefix>/`, to an existing
   Bypass app or as part of one it created; no narrowing destination protects that path's
   children, so a failed check may mean they are public. Apply reads the Bypass app again and
   sends it back with only `<domain>/<prefix>/` taken out. Everything else the app holds stays,
   no app is deleted, and nothing that existed before the run is removed. Then it runs the
   wait again with the other public paths, and reports all three: the original failure, what
   it removed, and whether the site passes the check without `<prefix>/`. It exits 1 either way,
   and D1 and GitHub are not touched. The error reads `Rollback: removed <domain>/<prefix>/
   from Bypass app "<name>", which keeps …`, naming what the app still holds; the bare
   `<domain>/<prefix>` is always among it, because `/<prefix>/` is planned only alongside
   `/<prefix>`. It ends with `Without /<prefix>/ listed, the site passes the check` or the
   probes that still fail.
   The same removal runs when the write that adds `<domain>/<prefix>/` to an existing Bypass
   app fails, because a `PUT` can go through and still fail (a lost response, or an answer
   that does not list the destination as sent). Apply reads the app again and sends a removal
   only if the app holds `<domain>/<prefix>/` under exactly that name. Otherwise the error says
   `does not hold <domain>/<prefix>/, so nothing was removed`, lists what the app guards, and
   asks you to check it in the dashboard now. If Cloudflare answers the removal with the
   destination still there, the error says `tried to remove … but it still holds it`.
   A failed create of a new Bypass app that would hold `<domain>/<prefix>/` gives no app id to
   work with, so that error says the app may exist all the same and must be checked in the
   dashboard now.
   Before such a run adds `<domain>/<prefix>/`, apply records which private probes ask for
   sign-in. If one of those answers signed out during the wait, the run has made it public, so
   the wait stops at once and the destination comes out, instead of staying public until the
   attempts run out.
   Every other mixed run that fails the wait stops with `Access is not answering for <prefix>: …`
   and leaves the apps it created in place for you to look at.

D1 and GitHub follow as for a private app. Each step only fills in what is missing, so a mixed
run on an app that already has its Allow app, D1 and secrets adds only the narrowing
destinations it lacks, and the Bypass policy and app (or the public destinations its Bypass app
lacks).

**Which app answers which path.** When several Access apps match a request, the one with the
most specific matching destination applies, and within one app Bypass policies are evaluated
before Allow. A listed destination under the prefix is more specific than the Allow app's
`<prefix>/*`, so the Bypass app wins there; a public `/<prefix>` is left out of the Allow app, so
only the Bypass app holds it. The paths under an exact public path would inherit its Bypass, so
its narrowing destination, more specific again, sends them to the Allow app. Everything else
under the prefix goes to the Allow app's `<prefix>/*`. A public `<prefix>/` is the exception: the
paths under it are meant for `<prefix>/*` too, but which of the two wins there is not documented,
and no narrowing destination can decide it, so the plan adds a line saying so. A child of each
exact public path is still probed and must ask for sign-in. The plan prints the intended answer
per destination:

```
  · who answers (the app with the most specific matching destination wins; Bypass lets anyone in, Allow asks for sign-in):
  ·   example.com/time-track → "time-track (public)" — Bypass, anyone
  ·   example.com/time-track/_next/* → "time-track (public)" — Bypass, anyone
  ·   example.com/time-track/* (the rest) → "time-track (/time-track)" — Allow, sign-in
```

and, for graph-notes, after its six Bypass lines:

```
  ·   example.com/graph → "graph-notes (/graph)" — Allow, sign-in
  ·   example.com/graph/public/* (narrowing) → "graph-notes (/graph)" — Allow, sign-in
  ·   example.com/graph/public.txt/* (narrowing) → "graph-notes (/graph)" — Allow, sign-in
  ·   example.com/graph/manifest.webmanifest/* (narrowing) → "graph-notes (/graph)" — Allow, sign-in
  ·   example.com/graph/* (the rest) → "graph-notes (/graph)" — Allow, sign-in
```

A `/*` destination does not cover its own base: `/graph/_next/*` makes `/graph/_next/a.js` public,
not `/graph/_next`.

### Plan, apply, exit codes

Without `--apply`, the command prints the plan and changes nothing: planning makes Cloudflare
`GET`s (with the setup token read from the keychain), `gh` reads, `git remote get-url`, and an
*existence* check on the deploy-token keychain entry only. Exit codes: `0`
ok, `1` a step failed, `2` usage error or a conflict in the plan.

**What it refuses or leaves alone.**

- **Refused prefixes:** an empty prefix, `/`, and anything under ai-chat-archive's site-wide
  `/api`, `/_next` or `/vendors`. Also refused: wildcards, dots, queries and uppercase.
- **Conflicts (`✗`), where nothing is applied:**
  - an existing Access app that overlaps the two destinations without matching them exactly
    (for a mixed app: one holding anything beyond the base and narrowing destinations, such as a
    narrowing destination for a path no longer listed);
  - with `--public-path`, an existing Allow app that lacks a narrowing destination but cannot take
    one by a plain `PUT`: one that is not self-hosted, holds its paths in the deprecated
    `self_hosted_domains`, holds a destination that is not a public hostname, or has a Bypass
    policy (a destination added to it would not ask for sign-in);
  - with `--public`, any Access app on the destinations, or a path that already redirects to
    an Access login;
  - with `--public-path`: an app other than the public app that already holds a listed path (a
    destination is never moved from one app to another); an app named `<repo name> (public)`
    that holds anything beyond the listed paths, or only some of them but is not Bypass for
    Everyone or cannot take a plain `PUT`; an app holding exactly the listed paths
    that is not Bypass for Everyone; a Bypass app that opens more of the prefix than the list
    (say `<domain>/graph/api/*` when only `/graph/api/public/*` is listed); a
    `portfolio-app public` policy that is not Bypass for Everyone; and `/<prefix>/` listed
    without `/<prefix>`;
  - a clone of a different repo;
  - placeholder entries that name more than one database; with `--public`, `r2_buckets` that
    name several buckets, an entry with no `bucket_name` or an invalid one, or a
    `wrangler.jsonc` with no `name` for the routes;
  - a Worker route that reaches into the prefix and is not the app's own: one owned by another
    Worker or by none (another Worker's `<domain>/<prefix>*`, `<domain>/<prefix>` or
    `<domain>/<prefix>/*` included), or one of the app's Worker that also matches paths outside
    the prefix and is not `<domain>/<prefix>*` (`<domain>/work/*` for `/work/election-atlas`);
  - with `--public`, a setup token that may not read R2 buckets, the zone, its Worker routes
    or the Worker scripts (the line names the permission; see the keychain table);
  - a missing deploy-token keychain entry.
- **Reported but left alone (`!` or `·`):**
  - a policy whose emails differ from the config;
  - an exact-match Access app that is not attached to the policy;
  - a broader route of another Worker, such as the home site's `<domain>/*`: the app's longer
    pattern is more specific, so Cloudflare sends the prefix to the app;
  - a route on a sibling path that `<domain>/<prefix>*` also matches, such as
    `<domain>/work/election-atlas-old/*`: it is more specific, so it keeps its paths;
  - with `--public-path`, a Bypass app above the prefix (such as one on `<domain>`): the app's
    own destinations are more specific, so it does not reach the private paths.

  Changing who can sign in is a decision for the Zero Trust dashboard, not for a re-run.

## The Worker route and its pass-through

Cloudflare matches a Worker route against the whole request URL, **query string included**, and
a route pattern cannot contain a query; its only wildcards are a leading `*` on the host and a
trailing `*` on the path. So the exact route `<domain>/<prefix>` never matches
`/<prefix>?<query>`, and `<domain>/<prefix>/*` needs the slash: `/graph?g=rag` matched no
route and went to the zone's origin, GitHub Pages, which answered 404 (seen for every sub-app
on 2026-11-15). The only pattern that matches it is **`<domain>/<prefix>*`**, so that is the one
route every app's Worker gets: from `bootstrap --public`, and in the app's own
`frontend/wrangler.jsonc` for the others:

```jsonc
"routes": [{ "pattern": "akshayprabhakant.com/graph*", "zone_name": "akshayprabhakant.com" }],
```

More specific routes still win under it (`/graph/api/*` on the API Worker, `/_site/*` on
site-shell). But `<prefix>*` also matches every sibling path that starts with the prefix:
`/graphfoo`, `/graphs`, `/graph.html`, `/graph-x/y`. **The app's Worker must pass each of those
to the origin untouched**, returning `fetch(req)` for any path that is neither `/<prefix>` nor
under `/<prefix>/`. A Worker's subrequest to its own zone goes to the origin and does not
re-enter the Worker, and `fetch(req)` forwards the incoming request itself (method, headers,
body; a 3xx comes back as is). At the top of the Worker's `fetch`, after any `/_site/*` forward
(under `wrangler dev` the Worker stands in for site-shell's route), with `PREFIX` the app's
prefix as a pattern such as `/^\/graph(?=\/|$)/`:

```js
const u = new URL(req.url);
const ours = PREFIX.test(u.pathname);            // /graph or /graph/…, not /graphfoo
u.pathname = u.pathname.replace(PREFIX, '') || '/';
if (u.pathname.startsWith('/_site/') && env.SHELL) return env.SHELL.fetch(new Request(u, req));
if (!ours) return fetch(req);                     // /graphfoo etc.: the origin, untouched
```

Then `/<prefix>?<query>` reaches the app. Whether it serves that in place or redirects to
`/<prefix>/?<query>` (keeping the query) is the app's choice: redirect only when `/<prefix>` and
`/<prefix>/` have the same Access (both signed in or both public) and the app's canonical URL
has the trailing slash; otherwise serve in place (so a mixed app with `--public-path /<prefix>`
but not `/<prefix>/` serves in place). To redirect, test the request's own path: after the
rewrite above, `u.pathname` is `/` for both `/graph` and `/graph/`:

```js
const { pathname, search } = new URL(req.url);
if (pathname === '/graph' && search) {
  return new Response(null, { status: 308, headers: { location: `/graph/${search}` } });
}
```

**Access does not change.** An Access app keeps exactly `<domain>/<prefix>` and
`<domain>/<prefix>/*`: Access already matches `/<prefix>?<query>` with the `<prefix>`
destination (signed out, `/graph?x=1` redirects to the login like `/graph`), and widening it to
`<prefix>*` would put `/<prefix>foo` behind sign-in. Those sibling paths stay public, as before.
They now count as Worker requests (the free plan allows 100,000 a day); they are 404s nobody
links to.

## `verify`: the login check for deploy jobs

```sh
portfolio-app verify --path /<prefix> --domain <host> [--team <team>] [--public-path <path>…]
```

Requests `https://<host>/<prefix>` and `https://<host>/<prefix>/portfolio-app-verify` without
following redirects. It exits `0` only when both answer 3xx to
`<team>.cloudflareaccess.com/cdn-cgi/access/login/…`. If `--team` is omitted, any
`*.cloudflareaccess.com` login host is accepted. It needs no token and no config (with `--domain`
given), so it can be the first step of a GitHub Actions deploy job:

```yaml
- name: Refuse to deploy unless the path is behind Cloudflare Access
  run: npx -y @akshaydev17/portfolio-app@0.1.0 verify --domain akshayprabhakant.com --team shiny-moon-6b37 --path /quiz
```

Until the package is published to npm, run the script from a checkout of this repo instead:
`node packages/portfolio-app/skills/portfolio-app/scripts/portfolio-app.mjs verify …`.

**A mixed app** passes the same `--public-path` list it was bootstrapped with, and then the check
goes both ways. The probes run in this order:

1. The private probes, each of which must redirect to the Access login: `/<prefix>`,
   `/<prefix>/portfolio-app-verify`, `/<prefix>/api/portfolio-app-verify`, then
   `<path>/portfolio-app-verify` for each public path listed without a `/*`, in the order
   listed. Any of these that a listed public path covers is left out (`/<prefix>` when it is
   public, a child when `<path>/*` is listed too), and one that appears twice is requested once.
2. The public probes, in the order listed, each of which must answer without a redirect to any
   Access login: an exact path as itself, a `<dir>/*` path as `<dir>/portfolio-app-verify`. The
   app's own 404 counts as an answer.

For graph-notes' six paths that is `/graph`, `/graph/portfolio-app-verify`,
`/graph/api/portfolio-app-verify`, `/graph/public/portfolio-app-verify`,
`/graph/public.txt/portfolio-app-verify` and `/graph/manifest.webmanifest/portfolio-app-verify`
as private, then the six public probes. The three children pass only because the Allow app holds
their narrowing destinations. For time-track, the child of the public `/time-track` is
`/time-track/portfolio-app-verify`, which is already a private probe, and so is the child of
`/time-track/`. With `/time-track/` listed, time-track's probes are
`/time-track/portfolio-app-verify` and `/time-track/api/portfolio-app-verify` as private, then
`/time-track`, `/time-track/_next/portfolio-app-verify` and `/time-track/` as public. Without
`--public-path`, `verify` behaves exactly as before.

**Limit:** a public path that answers a bare `401` or `403` fails the check. Access can answer
that way, and so can Cloudflare's bot protection when it refuses an automated client; from a
signed-out request without a browser the two look the same, so the line says to open the path in
a private browser window. The private probes need a real 3xx to the login, so a bot-protection
`403` can never pass a private pat
