# Português (`@automagik/locale-pt-br-dsh`) Brazilian Portuguese for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (DSH). DSH 0.2.2 ships Portuguese itself, as **Português** (`pt`); this client plugin adds the part DSH does not carry — the Bot team's own `omni-ui` strings — under that same entry. It adds no language: Settings › General › Language keeps exactly **one** Portuguese row, DSH's. Supported runtime: **DSH 0.2.2-rc.2 or later** (`engines.dsh` is `>=0.2.2-rc.2 <0.3.0-0`). Earlier DSH series have no `pt` to register under; this pack requires rc.2 or later. ## One Portuguese entry The pack used to add its own **Português (Brasil)** entry with a corrected copy of four DSH namespaces (date order, thousands separator, the plan hint and several mistranslations). A pack cannot override a namespace DSH already registers for `pt` — the second registration throws (`locale namespace "" already has locale "pt"`) — so those corrections required a second language, and therefore a second Portuguese row in the picker. That row is gone. The Language list shows DSH's **Português** alone, and DSH's `pt` copy serves the DSH screens. The pack's own strings are the Bot team's, and they belong to the Bot team's namespace: DSH does not have `omni-ui`. ## What it carries | Namespace | Keys | Why | |---|---|---| | `omni-ui` | all | The Bot team's namespace (`@automagik/bots-dsh`), which DSH does not have; registered under `pt` | `omni-ui` holds every Bot team key. A few keep their English text on purpose: brand and product names (`Omni`, `DSH`, `Automagik`, `DeepSeek`, `Claude`, `Codex`, `ChatGPT`, `OpenAI`, `Anthropic`, `Google`, `GitHub`, `Namastex`, `Kimi`, `WeChat`, `WeCom`, `DingTalk`, `Feishu`, `MCP`, `API`), code-like strings (`cookies.txt, JSON, storageState`, `MEMORY.md`, `GITHUB_TOKEN`, `~/.codex/pets`, `#rrggbb`, `@Name`, `/side`, `/feedback`), words Brazilian Portuguese uses unchanged (`Chat`, `Bots`, `Plugins`, `Admin`, `Site`, `Terminal`, `Endpoint`, `Feedback`, `Skill`, `status`, `tokens`, `Pets`, `Chats`, `Design`, `Beta`, `Cc`), and strings that are only a value (`{count}`, `{n}h`, `1 item`, `{percent}%`, `{label}: {version}`). `test/coverage.test.js` requires every Bot key to have an entry and at least 95% of them to differ from the English text. A plugin from outside this repository can add its own words to `omni-ui` through the Bot team's `addStrings`. `scripts/copy-check.mjs` lists in `OMNI_PLUGIN_STRINGS` a recorded fixture of the keys each one adds (their English text), under `test/fixtures/`: today `unfold-session-strings.json`, the model-menu messages of Unfold's session plugin, recorded at the hand-over commit when it left with the Unfold plugins (RFC 0020). Those keys are checked and covered like the Bot team's. The Bot team words a host message with any language pack's entry for it. The welcome (`@automagik/welcome-dsh`) keeps its own copy in its `welcome.team` namespace and registers it under DSH's `pt` as well, so the onboarding reads in Portuguese with this pack installed. ## Upgrading from the old pack, and removing it A profile that installed the pack before 0.2.2 has an older copy that registered a **pt-BR** language and its dictionaries. DSH replaces a plugin in place: when it loads this version it unloads the old one first, whose language and dictionary effects are disposed with it. This client adds no language at all, so it cannot leave a second Portuguese row behind; while the old copy is still mounted, it does not register over the dictionary the old copy holds (it waits for that copy's disposer), so nothing throws on a duplicate locale registration. A language choice saved as `pt-BR` under the old pack is an exact id to DSH's locale runtime, and DSH's entry is `pt`. On load the pack rewrites the stored choice through the runtime's only preference write (`setLocale`), before the choice is read, so a team that picked **Português (Brasil)** opens in Portuguese instead of falling back to English. A browser or home that never picked a language is left alone. To stop shipping the Bot team's strings, remove the plugin: `dsh plugin --profile remove @automagik/locale-pt-br-dsh` (or Settings › Plugins, then the Plugins page, which manages what the list only shows). DSH's own **Português** entry and everything DSH translates stay; only `omni-ui` falls back to its English text, and a saved `pt` choice keeps resolving. ## Install 1. Add the Automagik market to DSH's plugin market ([marketplace/README.md](../../marketplace/README.md) has the URL). 2. Install **Português (Brasil)** — the market title of this pack. If DSH asks for a restart, restart it. 3. Pick **Português** in Settings › General › Language (DSH's entry), or open DSH in a browser set to Portuguese. The client declares `inject: ['locale']` and loads in DSH's first boot phase (`immediately`). The host half does nothing. It needs no settings. ## Develop ```sh bun run harness # the pinned DSH release the tests and the linter run against bun run build # client.js from src/client; commit it with the sources bun run test # on Node: a fake locale service, then DSH's own LocaleRuntime bun run lint node scripts/copy-check.mjs # every pt-BR text against its English text and the copy rules ``` `src/client/locales/pt-BR/omni-ui.json` is keyed by the Bot team's English text. The copy check rejects a key the Bot team no longer has and every `{placeholder}` that does not match its English text. Its rules: Brazilian Portuguese, gender-neutral for the person, no article before Unfold, "clique" for a click, and "ambiente isolado" for a sandbox.

Automagik

A team of AI helpers that lives in your chats.

Automagik is superintelligence, in open building blocks: a team of AI agents in your chats,
and each part usable on its own once it ships; Cloud is still in design.

The film: our own GTM team. The team launching Automagik, at work. Music only, no voice-over.
Watch the film on automagik.si

⬇ Download for Mac  ·  ⬇ Download for Linux

Cloud is coming; no date yet. Join the Cloud waitlist on automagik.si

This repository, Genie and Omni are free and open source, Apache-2.0. Cloud is a private, paid service.
Mac with Apple silicon, macOS 13 or newer · Linux on a 64-bit PC · Windows is not supported yet

--- ## Two modes **Team mode** is the desktop app: a team of long-lived Bots, each with its own name, role, model and memory. They talk to you, to each other and in group chats, run scheduled tasks, and each drives a browser of its own. With an [Omni](https://github.com/automagik-si/omni) connected, your WhatsApp, Telegram, Slack and other channels sit in the same window, and the Bot you put on a chat acts when something happens there. The team runs on [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (DSH). **Code mode** is your code agents in the real [Herdr](https://herdr.dev) window, with the Automagik pack: a sidebar of spaces, Bots and workers across coding harnesses. Nothing in Herdr is rebuilt. The app's switch brings the Herdr window forward on the space for the current Bot's folder, and a button in Herdr brings you back. The app download alone does not set Code mode up: it needs Herdr and the pack, and [the pack's installer](herdr/README.md#install) sets up both. Team mode: the app's switch still says Work. ## The seven blocks Each block is usable alone. - **[Team mode (DSH)](apps/bots-dsh/README.md)**: the Bot team on DeepSeek Harness: long-lived Bots with their own name, role, model and memory, group chats, schedules and the Bot browser. - **[Code mode (Herdr)](herdr/README.md)**: your code agents in the real Herdr window with the Automagik pack; nothing in Herdr is rebuilt. - **[Genie](https://github.com/automagik-si/genie)**: a wish becomes a branch, a test run and a report you approve; `genie desktop` opens it on the team. - **[Omni](https://github.com/automagik-si/omni)**: the service that links your chat apps to Automagik, with its channels and canvases in the same window. - **[Pocket](apps/pocket/README.md)**: your coding agents on your Android phone, paired to your own machines. - **[The meter](meter/usagemeter/README.md)**: usagemeter, the Rust token meter that records usage and cost on the machine and answers `usagemeter query`. - **[Cloud](docs/rfcs/0024-automagik-cloud.md)**: one sign-in, organisations and hosted workspaces, with a rail that opens each. Cloud is designed and accepted, and is not live. When it ships it is a private, paid hosted service: not free and not open source. Only its contracts are public (RFC 0024). ## What makes it yours - **Your model.** Connect the AI account you already have, or an API key from a provider you use. Each Bot runs on the model you give it. - **Your files and memory, on your computer.** What the team keeps is in one folder, `.automagik` in your home folder. Each Bot keeps notes across its conversations, each group chat keeps its own, and the team shares one more. Your chats stay in your Omni. What your Bots read and write goes to the AI account you connected, under that company's terms. - **Secrets the Bots never see.** When a Bot needs an API key, a token or a password, it asks with a card in its own chat. You type the value; the Bot never sees it. - **It asks before it acts as you.** Before a Bot sends a message as you to a person, deletes something or disconnects a channel, it shows you exactly what it will do and asks first. The exceptions: your Main Bot and an Omni Bot read your chats and post to a group, a WhatsApp channel or your own chat with yourself without asking. Any other Bot reads and posts only where you allow: the first time it wants a chat it asks, and you answer **Once**, **Always** or **No**; after **Always** it posts to that group without asking again. ## Install The current release is always at [Releases](https://github.com/automagik-si/automagik/releases/latest). **Mac** (Apple silicon, macOS 13 or newer): 1. [Download Automagik for Mac](https://github.com/automagik-si/automagik/releases/latest/download/Automagik-Mac.dmg). 2. Open **Automagik-Mac.dmg** and drag the Automagik icon onto the Applications folder. 3. Open **Automagik** from Applications. **Linux** (64-bit PC): 1. [Download Automagik for Linux (.deb)](https://github.com/automagik-si/automagik/releases/latest/download/Automagik-Linux.deb) for Ubuntu or Debian. 2. Double-click it and choose **Install**, or run `sudo apt install ./Automagik-Linux.deb`. 3. Open **Automagik** from your apps. On another Linux, use the [AppImage](https://github.com/automagik-si/automagik/releases/latest/download/Automagik-Linux.AppImage). Windows is not supported yet. The app has two things to connect when you are ready: an Omni and an AI account. Both can wait. The full guide, updates, your data and uninstall are in [apps/desktop](apps/desktop/README.md). Code mode installs separately: [herdr](herdr/README.md#install). Pocket: [apps/pocket](apps/pocket/README.md#install). **For your code agent**: `npx skills add automagik-si/automagik --skill am` adds the skill that teaches it `am`, Automagik's one command. ## This repository Automagik's plugins for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (DSH), and the Automagik desktop app that runs them, with the Herdr pack (`herdr/`), Pocket (`apps/pocket/`) and the meter (`meter/`). | Folder | Package | What it is | |---|---|---| | [`apps/bots-dsh`](apps/bots-dsh/README.md) | `@automagik/bots-dsh` | The Bot team: long-lived Bots, group chats, memory, settings, scheduled tasks, the Bot browser. Omni's and Genie's plugins build on it. | | [`apps/welcome-dsh`](apps/welcome-dsh/README.md) | `@automagik/welcome-dsh` | The welcome: the octopus, the team step, and Connect AI through DSH's own sign-ins. | | [`apps/acp-dsh`](apps/acp-dsh/README.md) | `@automagik/acp-dsh` | Agents other than DSH's own, over ACP (Agent Client Protocol), as DSH models: the agent's tool calls show as DSH tool cards and ask through DSH's approval dialog (RFC 0003). | | [`apps/locale-pt-br-dsh`](apps/locale-pt-br-dsh/README.md) | `@automagik/locale-pt-br-dsh` | Português: the Bot team's Brazilian Portuguese under DSH's own Portuguese entry. Adds no language of its own, so Settings › General › Language keeps one Portuguese row; a pt-BR choice saved by an older pack moves to DSH's pt. | | [`apps/desktop`](apps/desktop/README.md) | (the app) | The Automagik desktop app: DSH of its own with the Bot team, the welcome and Omni's channels and canvases. `omni desktop` opens it with Omni preloaded, `genie desktop` with Genie. | Omni's own plugins (its channels and canvases) live with Omni, in [automagik-si/omni](https://github.com/automagik-si/omni) (`apps/omni-channels-dsh`, `apps/omni-canvas-dsh`), and carry Omni's version. ### Install into your own DSH - **The desktop app**: download it from [Releases](https://github.com/automagik-si/automagik/releases/latest), or run `omni desktop`. See [apps/desktop](apps/desktop/README.md). - **Into your own DSH**: add the Automagik market to DSH's plugin market and install from there: ``` https://raw.githubusercontent.com/automagik-si/dsh-marketplace/main/index.json ``` Every Omni also serves a market at `https:///api/market/index.json` with the release of these plugins it was tested with. Nothing here is published to npm. The plugins install as git sources pinned to a release commit, or from the tarballs each release carries (`plugins.json` lists their integrity). ### History `@automagik/bots-dsh` and `@automagik/welcome-dsh` were `@automagik/omni-dsh` and `@automagik/omni-ai-dsh` in automagik-dev/omni (`apps/omni-ui-dsh`, `apps/omni-ai-dsh`), and the desktop app was automagik-dev/omni-desktop. They moved here with their history. What did not change with the names: plugin ids (`omni-ui`, `omni-ai`), routes and browser-storage prefixes. From 3.12 the team's home is Automagik's own (`~/.automagik/bots`, or `~/.automagik/desktop/bots` in the app), and the app's identity is Automagik's (`ai.namastex.automagik`): an app from 3.11.x or before is installed afresh, not updated. - The Bot team's client bundle also answers to its former name, so channels and canvas plugins built before the rename keep working on it. - In your own DSH: install `@automagik/bots-dsh` from the market. With both installed, the newer one runs (they share the plugin id); remove `@automagik/omni-dsh` when you like. A settings row in your profile's `cordis.patch.yml` that names `@automagik/omni-dsh` needs its `name:` changed to `@automagik/bots-dsh` to keep applying. ### Versions and releases One version for the whole repository, `3.N` (semver `3.N.0`, N one above the last release: `scripts/version.ts`), above the 2.x builds omni-desktop released. Every merge into dev is a release: `release.yml` tags `v`, publishes the plugin tarballs and `plugins.json`, builds the desktop app into the same release (`desktop-build.yml`), lists the release in [`marketplace/automagik.json`](marketplace/automagik.json), and moves `main` to it. `follow-omni.yml` moves the desktop app to each newer Omni release and cuts a release with it. | Branch | What | |---|---| | `dev` | Integration: pull requests land here; releases are cut from it | | `main` | The latest release, moved by `release.yml` only | ### Develop Bun for the repository's own tooling; the plugins run on Node, as DSH does (`node --test`, esbuild), with Bun installing them; the desktop app uses npm for Electron. ```sh bun install && bun run check # versions, release tooling, market index cd apps/bots-dsh && bun install && bun run harness && bun run test cd apps/welcome-dsh && bun install && bun run harness && bun run test cd apps/desktop && npm ci && npm test node scripts/boot-check.mjs # boot the plugins with Omni's in headless Chromium ``` ### License This repository is Apache-2.0. See [LICENSE](LICENSE) and [NOTICE](NOTICE). [Genie](https://github.com/automagik-si/genie) and [Omni](https://github.com/automagik-si/omni) are Apache-2.0 in their own repositories. Automagik Cloud is not part of this licence: it is a private, paid service.

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# Omni AI for DSH

`@automagik/welcome-dsh` is the first thing a DeepSeek Harness (DSH) shows with Omni
installed: the Omni octopus says hello, then helps you connect an AI. It adds no provider
code. Every sign-in it offers is one DSH 0.2.1-rc.4 already ships, and every route it
writes goes through DSH's own settings and credential store.

## What it does

Two steps on DSH's `settings.onboarding` slot, shown once each on a fresh start (a new
chat with nothing in it), ahead of DSH's own steps:

| Step | Order | What it shows |
|---|---|---|
| `omni-welcome` | −300 | The octopus, a typewriter speech bubble and a glitch, on a starfield. |
| `omni-connect-ai` | −200 | Connect AI: one switch per AI, Continue and Skip. |

The Omni channels plugin (`@automagik/omni-channels-dsh`) adds `omni-connect` (−250) between them when it
is installed. DSH's `welcome-notice` (−100) and `deepseek-official` (0) follow.

Each step draws its own modal and makes `#root` inert while it shows. When you finish or
skip a step, the plugin records it in its own settings entry, `omni-ai`, in three live
fields (`welcomeDone`, `connectAiDone`, `connectOmniSkipped`), so the step does not come
back after a restart. A step whose flag is already set completes without showing.

Connect AI is a list of switches, and several can be on. What this computer already has
comes first, under **Found on this computer**: a key in DSH's store
or in the environment, a sign-in DSH already holds, Claude Code or Codex signed in, a
CLIProxyAPI route, Ollama answering on `127.0.0.1:11434`. **Add another** shows four more, then the rest on demand. Continue
needs one AI really on; Skip finishes the step either way.

Flipping a switch on turns on what is set up, or opens its setup in the row: a key field,
the provider's own sign-in in DSH, or, for a provider that takes both (Grok), a choice of the
sign-in or a key. Claude and ChatGPT sign in only through their CLIs (Claude Code, Codex; see
below): their setup offers the CLI's **Sign in**, and for Claude an Anthropic API key. Off
stops using an AI and keeps its key, sign-in or account:

| Kind | On | Off |
|---|---|---|
| Key | writes the pi-ai route that names the key | removes the route; the key stays |
| Sign-in | the route is written once the sign-in succeeds; with no sign-in, a key the row also takes | removes the route; the sign-in and the key stay |
| Claude, ChatGPT | signed in to the CLI: turns on acp-dsh's `claude` or `codex` switch; else (Claude) the Anthropic key's route | turns that switch off, for every Bot on that agent, and removes the key's route; the CLI's sign-in and the key stay |
| CLIProxyAPI | the gateway form writes its route | removes the route; the key stays |
| Ollama | lists its models into a local OpenAI-compatible route | removes the route |
| dsh-subscriptions | shows the vendor's models again | hides them in that plugin's picker settings; the account stays |

DeepSeek is DSH's own route: its row turns on with a key or a DeepSeek account, and its key
is removed in Settings → Models. Every other provider DSH knows stays one link away, in
Settings → Models.

Continue gives the companion and the Omni Bot their model. Both are made without one, so
joining the team sends nothing anywhere; once Connect AI finishes with an AI on, each gets
the team's default model and its held greeting goes out, without a further click. With no
model that can run (Skip, or only a provider that still needs its key), they keep waiting
and their chats offer the ways to set one up.

### The team step and the preload

The team step (`omni-team`) asks who joins the companion's team: Omni and Genie, each a card
with what it starts with. Omni's card starts asleep; its power button installs what a plain
DSH lacks (below), then looks for an Omni to connect. Genie has no DSH plugin yet, and
says so; it can still be added to the team.

The Automagik desktop app passes the product it was opened for (`omni desktop` →
`--preload=omni`, `genie desktop` → `--preload=genie`) to DSH as `AUTOMAGIK_PRELOAD`, which
`state` reports as `preload` (`src/host/preload.js`; anything but `omni`, `genie` or
`unfold` is none). That card comes first and starts chosen: Omni's powers on by itself, through the
same box and steps as a press, and Remove still sends it back to sleep; Genie's starts on
the team. The other card stays to add, then or later. Without a preload Omni comes first
and nothing is chosen.

Unfold's card is shown only in Unfold's own Automagik instance. Anywhere else the team step has
no Unfold card and `unfold-plugin-install` is refused, so the welcome installs no `unfold-*`
plugin. Unfold's own Automagik instance starts DSH with `AUTOMAGIK_HOST=unfold` or
`AUTOMAGIK_PRELOAD=unfold` (either one names it: `src/host/host.js`, the same rule as the Bot
team's and the Unfold Bot's). There Unfold's card comes first and is on the team from the start,
because the Unfold Bot is the instance's Main Bot, so the companion step is done (Unfold leads)
and no other Bot is made. `state` reports it as `host`, and Omni and Genie come with the
instance: Omni's card offers no new Omni of its own, and Genie's names the command line the
instance brought instead of the line that installs one.

### The power shortcut in the Bot team's sidebar

Where the Bot team runs, the welcome puts a power button in its sidebar, between the update
cloud and Search (and in the collapsed rail), through the Bot team's `sidebarTools`
registry: `@automagik/bots-dsh/client` is in `dsh.client.external` and in the build's
`external`, and is looked up only when the plugin applies, so a DSH without the Bot team
gets no button and no error. Its card has a row per product, in the team step's order
(Unfold only in its own instance, read-only), each led by the Bot team's own mark for that
product (its `BotMark`) and offering the one thing to do next: power it on or off, install
it (with a line on what that does, then its step and place, "Installing Genie · 2 of 3 ·
Bot team", from the host's install job), try again with the reason, add the Omni Bot back,
open Plugins, or choose where Omni lives (the Bot itself sits in the sidebar, so a row does
not open it). Powering off is the
team step's own (`powerOff`): it stops a run and puts the box to sleep, and undoes nothing
on the host (a linked Omni stays linked, no Bot is removed); Genie, once on the team, stays,
as on its box. Powering on runs the team step's own steps in a shared store
(`src/client/power-store.js`), so it keeps going when the card or the step closes. That store
lives in the page, so the button reads the host's `omni-plugins` and `genie-plugin` when it
mounts and each time the card opens: an install the host is running (its `install.phase` is
`installing`) that this window does not follow, after a reload or from another window, is
picked up where it is, without asking for a second install, and polled every `POLL_MS`
(900 ms) as the team step polls it, to On or to the reason with Try again. Choosing where Omni
lives, or "Open team setup", opens the team step on purpose: there Continue only closes it and
saves nothing, so the Main Bot keeps its name. Both show only when the Bot team passes the
shell's onboarding opener (`actions.openHarnessOnboarding`).

The team step follows the DSH language. Its copy is the `welcome.team` namespace
(`src/client/i18n.js`): the keys are the English text, registered in English and in Brazilian
Portuguese (`pt-BR`), and the rows the host sends are read through it too. A language pack that
adds `pt-BR` to DSH turns the step Portuguese; it registers no `welcome.team` dictionary of its
own, since DSH takes one per namespace and language. The other steps are English only.

### What the power button installs

The Bot team (`@automagik/bots-dsh`) is this repository's, at this plugin's version: from
the source this plugin came from, pointed at `apps/bots-dsh` (the same commit, or a linked
checkout), else that release's tarball. A release tarball is installed only after every
one about to be installed matches the `lane.json` on the same release, signed with a key
the plugin carries (`src/host/lane-keys.json`, a copy of `plugin-lane/keys.json`): the lane
for this version, each tarball's size, sha256 and sha512. One that does not match, or a
release without a signed lane, stops the install before anything is installed; the checked
tarballs are kept, 0600, under `<AUTOMAGIK_HOME>/welcome/tarballs`, where the profile
installs them from. A DSH that has the team under its former name,
`@automagik/omni-dsh`, has the team: it is switched on, not installed over. Omni's channels
and canvases (`@automagik/omni-channels-dsh`, `@automagik/omni-canvas-dsh`) are Omni's, at
Omni's version: they install as a git source from Omni's repository at the release
`package.json` pins under `automagik.omni`, the same one the desktop app carries
(`apps/desktop/omni.json`; `follow-omni.yml` moves both).

### One way to each AI

| AI | Through | Not offered |
|---|---|---|
| Claude | Claude Code's own sign-in (acp-dsh's `acp-claude`), or an Anthropic API key on pi-ai's `anthropic` route (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`) | DSH's Claude Pro/Max sign-in (`llm-pi-ai/anthropic`) |
| ChatGPT | Codex's own sign-in (acp-dsh's `acp-codex`) | DSH's ChatGPT sign-in (`openai-codex`) as a chat route |
| Kimi | DSH's sign-in (`kimi-coding`) | dsh-subscriptions' `kimi` |
| Copilot | DSH's sign-in (`github-copilot`) | dsh-subscriptions' `copilot` |
| Grok | DSH's sign-in (`xai`), or an `XAI_API_KEY` | dsh-subscriptions' `grok` |
| DeepSeek | DSH's key or account | pi-ai's `deepseek` route |
| Ollama | a local pi-ai route | dsh-subscriptions' `ollama` |

A pi-ai route still on DSH's own sign-in for Claude or ChatGPT (`openai-codex`, or `anthropic`
naming no key while DSH holds its Claude sign-in) is a duplicate of the CLI: the row says
*Also connected through DSH sign-in*, and once the CLI can answer, turning the row on (or
**Use only this**) removes that route, but only after the Bot team (bots-dsh's `omniTeam`,
`moveSubscriptionBots`) has moved the Bots on it to the CLI's route. While any Bot (its model,
or the model a pending switch goes back to) or the team's background jobs still run on it, or
the team cannot be read, the route stays and stays listed. Only the route: the sign-in record
stays, and so does any route that names a key. `signin-start` (and the other `signin-*`
endpoints) refuse `anthropic` and `openai-codex`: nothing here starts DSH's own Claude or
ChatGPT plan sign-in. Images and the companion's drawing on a ChatGPT plan go through Codex's
own sign-in (acp-dsh's `generateImage`); an `openai-codex` record an earlier version stored is
read as a last resort only when acp-dsh answers normally and declares a shared auth scope.
An OpenAI API key draws as before. dsh-subscriptions no
longer ships `claude` or `codex` (0.7.21-omni.1), so nothing stands for them.

The route earlier versions added for DSH's Claude sign-in did not retry a 429 (`retryPolicy`
without `RATE_LIMIT`). A route on an API key keeps DSH's default retries, also one such a
sign-in made before the key: saving the key drops the sign-in's policy (a policy set by hand
stays).

dsh-subscriptions keeps the vendors nothing else reaches (Cursor, Kiro, GLM, Qwen,
Perplexity, JetBrains, Cody, Replit and the rest). When an AI is turned on, the other ways
it is connected stop showing: their models are hidden, and no account or stored sign-in is
deleted. A row says when its AI is also
connected another way.

### Claude Code and Codex

With [`@automagik/acp-dsh`](../acp-dsh) in the DSH, Connect AI's Claude and ChatGPT rows are
these CLIs, and DSH's Settings (and the Bot team's) have a **Claude Code and Codex** page with
a row for each agent. Connect AI has no section of its own for them. Without acp-dsh, Claude
takes only its API key, ChatGPT is not offered a sign-in, and the Settings page says the ACP
agents plugin is not running. Each Settings row says (and a Connect AI row shows the same lines
while its CLI is missing, installing or failed, or signed in but not answering yet):

- for Hermes, Antigravity and omp (acp-dsh's native-ACP agents, off until switched on): the
  same row without a connector line, with what switching it on means while it is off, and with
  the terminal command that signs in instead of a Bot's chat (`hermes acp --setup`,
  `agy acp --login`, `omp login`); Automagik never installs these CLIs;
- whether the agent's CLI (`claude`, `codex`) is on this computer, as acp-dsh's own store has
  it: installing or updating it by itself, failed with its error and **Retry**, or found with
  its version; with its install link and **Check again** when it is missing;
- whether the CLI is signed in, as the CLI itself says (`claude auth status`, `codex login
  status`; only yes or no is read). Signed out, the row has **Sign in**, and the command to run
  in a terminal as the other way (`claude auth login`, `codex login`); not checked yet, it says
  so, with **Check again**;
- the connector acp-dsh installs in the background: installing, failed with its last error and
  **Retry**, or ready with its version;
- once ready and signed in, *Ready: pick Claude Code in the model picker*. The model appears
  without a restart; a DSH that has not loaded acp-dsh's routes says to restart instead.

**Sign in** (in Connect AI, **Sign in to Claude Code** or **Sign in to Codex**) opens the sign-in row in a Bot's chat (the selected Bot, or else the Main Bot), through
the Bot team's bridge (`Symbol.for('automagik.cli-login')`, [`@automagik/bots-dsh`](../bots-dsh)).
The row in the chat runs the CLI's own sign-in: a link to open on any device, then Codex's code
to type there or Claude's code to paste back in that row. This page only opens the chat: it starts
no sign-in, picks no model and never sees a link, a code or a credential. In Connect AI the step
steps aside while the chat is in front (a small **Back to setup** brings it back) and is not
completed by it; Settings closes its panel. Without the Bot team or a Bot the row says to run the
command in a terminal instead. While a sign-in waits, the busy file (`src/host/busy.js`, `AUTOMAGIK_BUSY_FILE`) counts it, so an
automatic plugin update does not restart DSH in the middle of it.

The switch is acp-dsh's own `claude` or `codex` setting, written through DSH's settings service,
and Connect AI's Claude and ChatGPT switches are that same setting: off there is off for every
Bot on that agent. An agent that can answer (CLI found, switched on, connector ready, no restart
pending, signed in) is an AI on: its row is on, it counts for Continue and for `aiConnected`.
A signed-out or still-installing CLI does not. Their copy is in the `welcome.team` namespace, in
English and pt-BR.

### Subscription sign-ins and vendor terms

A sign-in with a consumer plan is **personal use under the vendor's terms**: check that
provider's terms before you use a personal plan for work.

## Install into a raw DSH

The plugin needs DSH `>=0.2.1-rc.2 <0.3.0`. Add the Automagik marketplace index to DSH's
plugin market ([marketplace/README.md](../../marketplace/README.md) has the URL and the
steps) and install `@automagik/welcome-dsh` from it. DSH asks before it installs, then
applies the bundle patch (`cordis.patch.yml`), which adds one row, `id: omni-ai`, and
changes nothing else.

Restart DSH and start a new chat to see the octopus.

## The CLIProxyAPI route

[CLIProxyAPI](https://github.com/router-for-me/CLIProxyAPI) serves an OpenAI-compatible
API for the providers you sign into on it. The form asks for its address (for example
`http://localhost:8317/v1`; an address without a path gets `/v1`) and its API key. On
Connect, the host:

1. Checks the address is `http://` or `https://`, with no user name, query or fragment.
2. Lists the gateway's models with `GET {baseURL}/models` and `Authorization: Bearer <key>`,
   without following redirects. An empty list refuses the save.
3. Stores the key with `ctx.credentials.set('OMNI_AI_CLIPROXY_API_KEY', key)`.
4. Writes the route into pi-ai's settings entry with
   `ctx.settings.update('llm-pi-ai', patch, revision)`, the revision read from
   `ctx.settings.describe()`:

   ```yaml
   providers:
     cliproxy:
       displayName: CLIProxyAPI
       api: openai-completions
       baseURL: http://localhost:8317/v1
       apiKeyEnv: OMNI_AI_CLIPROXY_API_KEY
       models:
         - { id: <model id>, name: <model id> }
   ```

The key never enters a settings file, a reply or a log: the route names it by the
env-shaped credential reference, which DSH resolves for each request. Saving again
replaces this route's model list and keeps every other route. Use `https://` for a
gateway that is not on your own machine, since the key travels with each request.

The shape was read from DSH 0.2.1-rc.2:

- `dsh-llm-pi-ai`: `Config = z.object({ providers: z.dict(profile).default({}).volatile() })`,
  where a profile has `apiKeyEnv` (a credential reference), `displayName`, `api`, `baseURL`
  and `models: [{ id, name, … }]`. Its README: a route pi-ai does not ship needs `api`,
  `baseURL` and a non-empty `models` list. The base bundle mounts it as entry `llm-pi-ai`.
- `dsh-settings`: `update(ns, patch, expectedRevision)` deep-merges plain objects and
  replaces arrays, so other routes stay and this route's `models` is replaced.
- `dsh-credentials`: a reference matches `/^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$/`.

## Host endpoint

`POST /api/omni-ai` with `{ endpoint, payload }`, answered `{ ok: true, value }` or
`{ ok: false, error: { code, message } }`:

| Endpoint | Payload | Does |
|---|---|---|
| `state` | none | The flags; `deepseek` (a `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` or a DeepSeek account sign-in is stored); `piAiRoutes`; `aiConnected`; `preload` (`omni`, `genie`, `unfold` or null); `host` (`unfold`, only when set); `machine` (`{ os, remoteHint? }`: the OS family DSH runs on, `macos`, `windows`, `linux` or `other`, and `remoteHint: true` when DSH was launched over SSH; never the hostname, user or home). |
| `done` | `{ stepId, connected? }` | Sets the flag for `omni-welcome`, `omni-connect-ai` or `omni-connect`. Connect AI's Continue sends `connected: true`: the companion and the Omni Bot, made without a model, then get the team's default model (DSH's default model when it is served and has its key, else the first model that can run), and their held greetings go out. Skip sets nothing. |
| `cliproxy` | `{ baseURL, apiKey }` | The route above; answers `{ route, baseURL, models }`. |
| `ais` | none | Every row: `{ id, name, via, kind, ready, on, found, signIn?, keyUrl?, needs?, duplicates? }`, and dsh-subscriptions' accounts and hidden vendors. Names and states only. |
| `ai-switch` | `{ id, on }` | Turns a row that is set up on or off (table above). |
| `ai-dedupe` | `{ id }` | Stops the other ways that row's AI is connected. |
| `ai-subscription` | `{ provider, on }` | Shows or hides a dsh-subscriptions vendor's models. |
| `provider-key`, `signin-*` | see `src/host/providers.js` | A key, or a sign-in run through DSH's authorization service. |
| `omni-plugins` | none | The Omni plugins (`@automagik/bots-dsh`, `@automagik/omni-channels-dsh`, `-canvas-dsh`): each one's version and whether it is installed, `ready` once they run here, and the install in progress. |
| `omni-plugins-install` | none | Installs the missing ones in order through DSH's plugin manager (`installBundle`: the Bot team from this plugin's own source pointed at its sibling, else this release's tarball; Omni's from Omni's repository at the pinned release), switching on any that are off. Pressing Omni's power button in the team step calls it. |
| `acp` | `{ refresh? }` | Claude Code and Codex, from acp-dsh's `acpAgents` service: `{ available, agents: [{ id, key, name, on, cli: { found, installUrl?, state?, version?, updating?, error?, diagnostic?, logPath? }, connector: { state, version?, error? }, signedIn?, listed, restartNeeded }] }`. `refresh` looks for the CLIs again and asks each whether it is signed in. `{ available: false }` without acp-dsh. |
| `acp-switch` | `{ id, on }` | Writes acp-dsh's `claude` or `codex` setting in the entry its service names (`settingsEntry`, else `acp-dsh`) at the revision `describe()` gave. |
| `acp-retry` | `{ id }` | Starts a failed connector install again. |
| `bot-type` | `{ type: 'omni' }` | What the Omni Bot starts with, as groups: model and thinking (DSH's default), plugins with versions, tool groups with their switches, skills, folder and permissions. |

The host declares `inject: ['settings', 'credentials', 'connection']`; `connection` serves
the route. It reads DSH's `llm`, `authorization`, `pluginManager`, `agentDefaultModel`, `tools`, `skills`
and `permissionPresets` services when they are there, and acp-dsh's `acpAgents`.

## Develop

```sh
bun install          # esbuild, for the client bundle
bun run harness      # the pinned DSH release the tests and the linter run against
bun run test         # on Node, as DSH runs
bun run lint
bun run build        # rewrites client.js; commit it
node scripts/build-client.mjs --check
```

`client.js` is generated from `src/client` and committed, so git and `link:` installs need
no build step.

## Two modes

**Team mode** is the desktop app: a team of long-lived Bots, each with its own name, role, model and memory. They talk to you, to each other and in group chats, run scheduled tasks, and each drives a browser of its own. With an [Omni](https://github.com/automagik-si/omni) connected, your WhatsApp, Telegram, Slack and other channels sit in the same window, and the Bot you put on a chat acts when something happens there. The team runs on [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (DSH).

**Code mode** is your code agents in the real [Herdr](https://herdr.dev) window, with the Automagik pack: a sidebar of spaces, Bots and workers across coding harnesses. Nothing in Herdr is rebuilt. The app's switch brings the Herdr window forward on the space for the current Bot's folder, and a button in Herdr brings you back. The app download alone does not set Code mode up: it needs Herdr and the pack, and [the pack's installer](herdr/README.md#install) sets up both.

<sub>Team mode: the app's switch still says Work.</sub>

## The seven blocks

Each block is usable alone.

- **[Team mode (DSH)](apps/bots-dsh/README.md)**: the Bot team on DeepSeek Harness: long-lived Bots with their own name, role, model and memory, group chats, schedules and the Bot browser.
- **[Code mode (Herdr)](herdr/README.md)**: your code agents in the real Herdr window with the Automagik pack; nothing in Herdr is rebuilt.
- **[Genie](https://github.com/automagik-si/genie)**: a wish becomes a branch, a test run and a report you approve; `genie desktop` opens it on the team.
- **[Omni](https://github.com/automagik-si/omni)**: the service that links your chat apps to Automagik, with its channels and canvases in the same window.
- **[Pocket](apps/pocket/README.md)**: your coding agents on your Android phone, paired to your own machines.
- **[The meter](meter/usagemeter/README.md)**: usagemeter, the Rust token meter that records usage and cost on the machine and answers `usagemeter query`.
- **[Cloud](docs/rfcs/0024-automagik-cloud.md)**: one sign-in, organisations and hosted workspaces, with a rail that opens each.

<sub>Cloud is designed and accepted, and is not live. When it ships it is a private, paid hosted service: not free and not open source. Only its contracts are public (<a href="docs/rfcs/0024-automagik-cloud.md">RFC 0024</a>).</sub>

## What makes it yours

- **Your model.** Connect the AI account you already have, or an API key from a provider you use. Each Bot runs on the model you give it.
- **Your files and memory, on your computer.** What the team keeps is in one folder, `.automagik` in your home folder. Each Bot keeps notes across its conversations, each group chat keeps its own, and the team shares one more. Your chats stay in your Omni. What your Bots read and write goes to the AI account you connected, under that company's terms.
- **Secrets the Bots never see.** When a Bot needs an API key, a token or a password, it asks with a card in its own chat. You type the value; the Bot never sees it.
- **It asks before it acts as you.** Before a Bot sends a message as you to a person, deletes something or disconnects a channel, it shows you exactly what it will do and asks first. The exceptions: your Main Bot and an Omni Bot read your chats and post to a group, a WhatsApp channel or your own chat with yourself without asking. Any other Bot reads and posts only where you allow: the first time it wants a chat it asks, and you answer **Once**, **Always** or **No**; after **Always** it posts to that group without asking again.

## Install

The current release is always at [Releases](https://github.com/automagik-si/automagik/releases/latest).

**Mac** (Apple silicon, macOS 13 or newer):

1. [Download Automagik for Mac](https://github.com/automagik-si/automagik/releases/latest/download/Automagik-Mac.dmg).
2. Open **Automagik-Mac.dmg** and drag the Automagik icon onto the Applications folder.
3. Open **Automagik** from Applications.

**Linux** (64-bit PC):

1. [Download Automagik for Linux (.deb)](https://github.com/automagik-si/automagik/releases/latest/download/Automagik-Linux.deb) for Ubuntu or Debian.
2. Double-click it and choose **Install**, or run `sudo apt install ./Automagik-Linux.deb`.
3. Open **Automagik** from your apps.

On another Linux, use the [AppImage](https://github.com/automagik-si/automagik/releases/latest/download/Automagik-Linux.AppImage). Windows is not supported yet.

The app has two things to connect when you are ready: an Omni and an AI account. Both can wait. The full guide, updates, your data and uninstall are in [apps/desktop](apps/desktop/README.md). Code mode installs separately: [herdr](herdr/README.md#install). Pocket: [apps/pocket](apps/pocket/README.md#install).

**For your code agent**: `npx skills add automagik-si/automagik --skill am` adds the skill that teaches it `am`, Automagik's one command.

# @plannotator/dsh Plannotator for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (DSH). When the agent leaves plan mode, `exit_plan_mode` opens the plan in Plannotator instead of DSH's own review card. Annotate it, then approve, approve with notes, or send feedback to keep planning. `/plannotator-review`, `/plannotator-annotate` and `/plannotator-last` open code review and annotation without blocking the session. With the inbox tool on, the agent can also reach you through the Plannotator Inbox, and your replies wake its session. ## Requirements - DeepSeek Harness 0.2.1-rc.2 or newer, below 0.3.0. - The `plannotator` CLI: ```bash curl -fsSL https://plannotator.ai/install.sh | bash ``` ## Install From the Plugins page in DSH Web or Desktop, add `@plannotator/dsh`. Or from a terminal: ```bash dsh plugin --profile add @plannotator/dsh ``` For the Desktop app's profile, open Desktop once, quit it, then run `dsh plugin --profile desktop add @plannotator/dsh`. A new install loads without a restart; after updating the package, restart DSH. ## How it works - **Plan review.** DSH asks for the review through its user-questions waterfall. The plugin answers plan reviews only: it runs `plannotator dsh-plan`, waits for your decision, and answers DSH with Approve, or Keep planning with your feedback. Approve with notes approves the plan and then sends the notes to the agent as a message. Every other question goes to DSH as usual. - **Fallback.** If the CLI is missing, fails, or prints something unexpected, the plugin hands the review back to DSH's own card. Cancelling the turn closes the review. - **Plannotator Inbox.** With the inbox tool on, the agent gets a `plannotator_inbox` tool. It uses the tool to send you messages and questions in the [Plannotator Inbox](https://plannotator.ai/docs/reference/inbox/#deepseek-harness). When the session is idle, your reply arrives as a new turn. **Send now** steers it into the running turn. The tool is off by default, because DSH sends every tool's definition with each request. To turn it on for DeepSeek Harness alone, use the Inbox's **Settings → Agents**, or add `{ "inboxTool": { "dsh": true } }` to `~/.plannotator/config.json`, keeping its other keys. (`plannotator inbox` also turns it on when it finds this plugin, but it connects every other agent it finds too.) The tool appears only once the Plannotator Inbox has run on this computer, so if it never has, start it once with `plannotator inbox --background`. It applies when DeepSeek Harness next starts, so restart DSH. (`PLANNOTATOR_INBOX_TOOL=1` would turn the tool on for every agent and lock the switches in Settings, and DSH Desktop does not see it unless started from that shell.) Nothing is registered and nothing polls when the tool is off, before you have run the Inbox once, or in the `headless`, `sdk`, `sdk-minimal` and `acp` profiles. The plugin only connects out to the Inbox on `127.0.0.1`, and reads the Inbox's key from `~/.plannotator/inbox/inbox.json` for each request. It keeps no copy of the key, and never puts it in its config, a log, a tool result or a message. - **Review, annotate, last.** The plugin adds the commands `/plannotator-review [directory | PR URL] [--base ]`, `/plannotator-annotate [--gate] [--markdown]` and `/plannotator-last`. Each one opens Plannotator and returns at once. The agent is not busy while you review. When you send your feedback, it arrives in the session as a new turn. - **The `plannotator` tool.** With the tool on, the agent can open the same reviews itself, for example when you ask it to "open notes.md in Plannotator". The call returns once the page is open, and your feedback arrives later as a new turn. The tool is off by default, because DSH sends every tool's definition with each request. To turn it on, set `PLANNOTATOR_AGENT_TOOL=1` or add `{ "agentTool": true }` to `~/.plannotator/config.json` (this turns it on for every agent that has the tool), then restart DSH. - **Not in every profile.** The tool and the commands are not added in the `headless`, `sdk`, `sdk-minimal` and `acp` profiles. There, and from a DSH shell, Plannotator's skills in `~/.agents/skills` run the CLI as before. The CLI recognizes DSH shells (`DSH_SHELL`), labels the session DeepSeek Harness, and `plannotator last` reads the calling session's log under `$DSH_HOME/sessions`. ## Configuration Both keys are optional. Set them by overriding the plugin's row in your profile's `cordis.patch.yml`: ```yaml - id: plannotator config: binary: /Users/me/.local/bin/plannotator planReview: true ``` | Key | Default | Meaning | |---|---|---| | `binary` | `PLANNOTATOR_BIN`, then `plannotator` on `PATH`, then `~/.local/bin/plannotator` (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\plannotator\plannotator.exe` on Windows) | The Plannotator CLI to run. Set it when DSH cannot find the CLI, for example when DSH Desktop starts with a `PATH` that lacks the install folder. | | `planReview` | `true` | `false` leaves `exit_plan_mode` to DSH's own review card. | Plan prompts follow your Plannotator config: `prompts.plan` in `~/.plannotator/config.json`, with `runtimes.dsh` for DSH-only wording. ## Development ```bash bun run build:dsh # from the repo root; writes apps/dsh-plugin/dist/index.js bun test apps/dsh-plugin dsh plugin --profile add link:/absolute/path/to/apps/dsh-plugin ```

Everything you need to annotate and stay in the loop with your agents
Inbox Surface • Artifacts • Code Review
Annotate plans, specs, markdown, HTML, and other interactive artifacts. Review diffs and PRs. Send feedback to your agent.

                       

Plannotator Inbox · Official site · Code Review · Visual HTML Skills · Herdr Annotate · (Legacy) Plan Mode

# Plannotator **⭐️ NEW:** [Plannotator Inbox](https://plannotator.ai/inbox/) is the missing review layer between you and multi-agent work. It surfaces decisions, prototypes, variations, plans, and everything you need to stay in the loop. Works with all coding agents and personal assistants. Plannotator is a local, browser-based review surface for AI coding agents: Claude Code, Codex, Copilot CLI, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Kiro, Droid, Amp, DeepSeek Harness, and Pi. Plannotator Inbox also works with personal assistants (Grok Bot, Muse, Hermes, OpenClaw). **It plugs directly into your agent** through plugins, hooks and commands. When the agent proposes a decision, plan, html, or finishes working, the app opens in your browser and you mark it up, comment, and send feedback directly to the agent for it to act on it.
### Review documents, plans, and agent messages Annotate plans, specs, messages, html, then send the feedback to your agent.

Demo: Plan review with Pi
### Code Review Review local changes or remote PRs. Comment on diffs, suggest code. Your comments go back to the agent. Works with Git, GitButler, Jujutsu (`jj`), Perforce (`p4`), GitHub, and GitLab.

AI built in: ask AI about anything you're reviewing,
or launch AI reviews that post comments to the diff.

## Annotate HTML Artifacts

## Plannotator Inbox

The Plannotator Inbox is one local window where your agents leave you messages, questions, files, and guided reviews while they keep working. Answer a question with a click, annotate a file, and press Send when you can. Nothing holds an agent session open while you do, and your reply goes back to the session that asked. ``` plannotator inbox ``` Claude Code, Pi, and OpenCode connect through Plannotator's plugins, and your replies arrive as their next turn. Any other agent reaches it over MCP with `plannotator inbox mcp`, and `plannotator inbox --help` is the guide an agent reads. [Watch the demo](https://plannotator.ai/assets/inbox-film.mp4) · [More on the Inbox](https://plannotator.ai/inbox/) · [Docs](https://plannotator.ai/docs/reference/inbox/) ## Herdr Annotate: Plannotator in the Terminal

  

[Herdr Annotate](https://github.com/plannotator/herdr-annotate) brings Plannotator-style review to the terminal: annotate terminal text, review whole Markdown documents and your coding agent's replies inside [Herdr](https://herdr.dev), and send the feedback straight back to the agent as its next message. Works with Claude Code, Codex, Pi, Copilot CLI, and Droid replies. Annotations are saved in the Plannotator data directory, so terminal reviews and app reviews compound. ``` herdr plugin install plannotator/herdr-annotate ``` Prefer it standalone? [Plannotator TUI](https://github.com/plannotator/plannotator-tui) powers the document review and runs without Herdr: `brew install plannotator/tap/plannotator-tui`. --- ## Commands On Codex, swap the slash commands for `!plannotator …` (e.g. `!plannotator review`) or the `$plannotator-*` skills. ### Annotate ``` /plannotator-annotate README.md # Local markdown file /plannotator-annotate src/ # Browse and annotate files in a folder /plannotator-annotate https://docs.rs/… # Fetch and annotate any URL /plannotator-annotate report.html --render-html # Render HTML as-is instead of converting /plannotator-last # Annotate the agent's last message ``` Need a realistic document to try? Copy the [product requirements document template and filled example](https://docs.plannotator.ai/templates/product-requirements-document) as Markdown. ### Code review ``` /plannotator-review # Review uncommitted changes /plannotator-review # Review a GitHub pull request /plannotator-review # Review a GitLab merge request plannotator review --gitbutler # Review an active GitButler workspace plannotator review --patch-file reading.diff # Review a static caller-supplied unified diff ``` GitButler users can review the whole workspace, one stack, or one branch layer. See the [GitButler workflow guide](https://docs.plannotator.ai/open-source/workflows/gitbutler). ### Plan mode No command needed. Plan mode is wired in through each harness's hooks. Any time your agent creates a plan, the markdown review surface opens for you. ### CLI ``` plannotator sessions # List active Plannotator sessions plannotator sessions --open 1 # Reopen a session in the browser plannotator archive # Browse saved plan decisions read-only ``` --- ## Privacy and network behavior Plannotator does not collect usage telemetry or analytics. Plans, diffs, annotations, drafts, history, and configuration stay local by default. Each plan review, annotate, archive, share-portal, and code-review app surface checks GitHub for the latest Plannotator release when it loads. This sends no plan or review content and gives the Plannotator project owner no usage analytics, although GitHub receives an ordinary request. There is currently no opt-out setting for the release check. Local Git code review can also query the configured `origin` with `git ls-remote` to detect the default branch and a stale baseline; it does not send the local diff. That remote query runs when the review opens, when the page loads its diff, when you switch the diff type or base (including the "Diff out of date · Refresh" button), and when you press Fetch — never on a timer, so an idle review page makes no network calls. Turn it off entirely with `plannotator review --no-git-remote-check`, `PLANNOTATOR_GIT_REMOTE_CHECK=0`, or `{ "gitRemoteCheck": false }` in `~/.plannotator/config.json`; the compare target then comes from local refs only and the "behind GitHub" banner never appears. Content leaves the local workflow only when a network feature needs it: - URL annotation fetches the requested site, through Jina Reader by default for public pages or directly when Jina is disabled or unavailable. - GitHub and GitLab review uses your authenticated CLI and Git remote to retrieve PR or MR data. - Ask AI and review agents send the selected question and relevant plan, document, repository, or diff context to your configured provider. When Ask AI is answered by the agent session that opened Plannotator ("Ask this session"), the question goes to that session instead. - Sharing sends the complete link to whoever or whatever service you use to deliver it. Encrypted short links upload ciphertext to the paste service. - Workspaces is a separate hosted product, so the open source app's local-storage model does not apply to content placed there. The [privacy policy](https://plannotator.ai/privacy) documents these boundaries and the hosted website and waitlist data. --- ## Link sharing Open source asynchronous link sharing remains available for compatibility but is moving to deprecated support. Workspaces is the primary direction for team sharing. No removal date has been announced.

Legacy link-sharing demo: room.plannotator.ai

Share a plan with a teammate and they can annotate it themselves. Import their feedback and send it straight back to your agent. **Small markdown shares** are compressed into the URL fragment. The fragment is not included in the browser's request to the share portal, but it is not encrypted. Anyone or any messaging service with the complete link can read the shared content. The portal host still receives ordinary request metadata. **Large markdown and raw HTML shares** use a short-link service. The share payload is encrypted with AES-256-GCM before upload, the server stores only ciphertext, and the key is kept in the URL fragment rather than sent in the paste request. Anyone with the complete link can decrypt it. Hosted pastes expire after 7 days. Same model as [PrivateBin](https://privatebin.info/). The paste service is [self-hostable](https://docs.plannotator.ai/open-source/workflows/sharing). Sharing can be disabled entirely with `PLANNOTATOR_SHARE=disabled`. [Workspaces](https://plannotator.ai/workspaces) is the primary path for hosted team collaboration. --- ## Install One installer covers almost every agent. It installs the `plannotator` binary, auto-detects your installed agents, and configures hooks, skills, and slash commands for each: ```bash # macOS / Linux / WSL curl -fsSL https://plannotator.ai/install.sh | bash ``` ```powershell # Windows PowerShell irm https://plannotator.ai/install.ps1 | iex ``` The installer downloads the binary from GitHub Releases. A full install can also contact GitHub for release resolution and agent files, Ataraxy-Labs/sem for the optional `sem` sidecar, and npm for Pi, selected extra skills, or the managed agent-terminal runtime. Pinning `--version` skips only GitHub API release resolution, not the release download. See the [privacy policy](https://plannotator.ai/privacy) for the complete network boundaries. Want just the binary and nothing else? Pass `--minimal` (or export `PLANNOTATOR_MINIMAL=1`) to install only the `plannotator` binary to `~/.local/bin`, skipping every skill, hook, slash command, and per-agent config: ```bash curl -fsSL https://plannotator.ai/install.sh | bash -s -- --minimal ``` Then finish the step for your agent: | Agent | After the installer | Details | |---|---|---| | **Amp** | Copy [`plannotator.ts`](apps/amp-plugin/plannotator.ts) into `~/.config/amp/plugins/`, then `plugins: reload`. Workflows live in the command palette. | [README](apps/amp-plugin/README.md) | | **Claude Code** | `/plugin marketplace add backnotprop/plannotator`, then `/plugin install plannotator@plannotator`. Restart Claude Code. | [README](apps/hook/README.md) | | **Codex** | Nothing. Plan review is enabled automatically via Codex's experimental `Stop` hook (macOS/Linux/WSL; on native Windows, Codex hooks are experimental and the installer prints manual setup steps). `$plannotator-review`, `$plannotator-annotate`, and `$plannotator-last` skills included. | [README](apps/codex/README.md) | | **Copilot CLI** | `/plugin marketplace add backnotprop/plannotator`, then `/plugin install plannotator-copilot@plannotator`. Restart. Plan review activates in plan mode (`Shift+Tab`). | [README](apps/copilot/README.md) | | **DeepSeek Harness** | Add `@plannotator/dsh` on DSH's Plugins page, or run `dsh plugin --profile add @plannotator/dsh`. Plan review opens on `exit_plan_mode`. The plugin adds `/plannotator-review`, `/plannotator-annotate` and `/plannotator-last`, which open without blocking the session. | [README](apps/dsh-plugin/README.md) | | **Droid** | `droid plugin marketplace add https://github.com/backnotprop/plannotator`, then `droid plugin install plannotator@plannotator`. Commands only, no plan interception yet. | [README](apps/droid-plugin/README.md) | | **Gemini CLI** | Nothing. The hook, policy, and slash commands are configured automatically. Requires Gemini CLI 0.36.0+. | [README](apps/gemini/README.md) | | **Kiro CLI** | Nothing. Skills and an example agent are installed automatically. Try `kiro-cli chat --agent plannotator`. | [README](apps/kiro-cli/README.md) | | **OpenCode** | Add `"plugin": ["@plannotator/opencode@latest"]` to `opencode.json`. Restart OpenCode. | [README](apps/opencode-plugin/README.md) | | **Pi** | Skip the installer. Just `pi install npm:@plannotator/pi-extension`. Start Pi with `--plan`, or toggle with `/plannotator-plan-mode`. | [README](apps/pi-extension/README.md) | | **T3 Code** | For Claude threads in T3: run `plannotator t3 --help` and follow its two steps (sign in to T3 once, add the `--t3` MCP entry). Your Inbox replies then arrive in the thread as new turns. | [README](packages/t3-code/README.md) | **Updating:** run the installer again for the binary and slash commands. It also updates an installed Claude Code plugin when the `claude` command is on your PATH (opt out with `--skip-claude-plugin`); otherwise run `claude plugin marketplace update plannotator`, then `claude plugin update plannotator@plannotator`, then restart Claude Code (refreshing the marketplace alone does not update the plugin). Pi: `pi update --extensions` (a plain `pi update` updates only Pi). On Claude Code 2.1.287 or newer, plan review, code review and annotate don't make Claude wait: Claude ends its turn and your decision arrives later as a message. Set `PLANNOTATOR_CLAUDE_MOD=0` to go back to the classic flow. Full walkthroughs live in the [installation docs](https://docs.plannotator.ai/open-source/start/installation). ### Uninstall The safe default removes recognized Plannotator-installed components and keeps your local plans, history, drafts, guides, and settings: ```bash plannotator uninstall ``` Use `--purge` for a full removal of known local Plannotator data as well: ```bash plannotator uninstall --purge ``` Purge requires typing `purge` at the prompt and explains that the data is local-only: it is not stored on a Plannotator server and cannot be recovered. For automation, pass `--yes` (or `-y`); non-interactive removal refuses to run without it. Use `--dry-run` to preview recognized work without making changes. Host integrations are always part of uninstall. If a broken or unavailable host prevents safe cleanup, the command names the blocking plugin manager or configuration, gives exact manual cleanup instructions, and stops before deleting the binary. Complete that cleanup and rerun uninstall. It also keeps the binary when an agent's config file can't be read (another tool's too), or when a hook it did not install still runs Plannotator. The error names the file, the tool, and what to do. A `plannotator-inbox` entry you added yourself, or a Claude Code or Droid plugin installed for one project, is named with how to remove it and does not keep the binary. These mechanics keep the ordinary confirmation default-negative, make the irreversible outcome require a stronger explicit word, and still give package managers and scripts a conventional non-interactive flag. The command covers the conventional macOS, Linux, WSL, and Windows binary locations; the managed `sem` sidecar and agent-terminal runtime; installer skills, commands, hooks, policies, caches, and recognizable Amp/Kiro files; and detected Claude Code, Copilot CLI, Droid, Pi, and VS Code installations through their host CLIs. Shared JSONC settings are edited surgically, while strict JSON updates preserve the file's indentation, line endings, and trailing-newline style. Custom or unrecognized files, separately installed optional skills, project-local integrations, external plan-save locations, and invalid configs are preserved (malformed host config is a fail-safe error). If cleanup reports an error, the CLI remains available for a safe retry, and its Windows PATH entry is retained or restored when possible. If PATH restoration itself fails, the output gives the full CLI path for retry and asks for manual PATH repair. For safety, purge refuses filesystem roots, the home directory, the shared temporary directory, symlinked data directories, and non-directory data paths. Existing paths are compared by filesystem identity, so case aliases, symlinks, hardlinks, and bind mounts cannot bypass the root/home/ancestor checks. That identity and every containment guard are revalidated after awaited host commands, immediately before the synchronous data-removal block; a replaced data directory is refused without touching either the old or replacement data. If your dedicated data directory is symlinked, point `PLANNOTATOR_DATA_DIR` at its resolved target and retry. If you installed only the standalone Pi extension and do not have the `plannotator` CLI, use `pi remove npm:@plannotator/pi-extension`.
Claude Code: manual hook setup (without the plugin system) Add to `~/.claude/settings.json`: ```json { "hooks": { "PermissionRequest": [ { "matcher": "ExitPlanMode", "hooks": [ { "type": "command", "command": "plannotator", "timeout": 345600 } ] } ] } } ```
Pin a specific version ```bash curl -fsSL https://plannotator.ai/install.sh | bash -s -- --version vX.Y.Z ``` ```powershell & ([scriptblock]::Create((irm https://plannotator.ai/install.ps1))) -Version vX.Y.Z ```
### Try it The fastest way to see what Plannotator does is to invoke it yourself, right now, from your agent: ``` /plannotator-last # annotate the agent's last reply /plannotator-review # review your current diff, PR-style /plannotator-annotate report.html # annotate any file, folder, or URL ``` (Slash commands in most agents; `$plannotator-*` skills in Codex, command palette in Amp.) Plan review needs no command at all. The next time your agent proposes a plan, it opens in your browser automatically. --- ## How it works ### Plan review ``` Agent calls ExitPlanMode -> PermissionRequest hook fires -> Local server reads plan from hook input -> Browser opens with review UI -> You annotate and approve/deny -> Approve: agent proceeds -> Deny: structured feedback sent to agent -> Agent revises, plan diff shows what changed ``` ### Code review ``` You run /plannotator-review -> git diff captures changes (or PR fetched by URL) -> Browser opens with diff viewer -> Annotate lines, stage/unstage files -> Send feedback: returned to agent session -> Approve: "LGTM" sent ``` --- ## Integrations **VS Code**: Open plans in editor tabs, view diffs inline, add annotations from the editor gutter. Install from the [VS Code Marketplace](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=backnotprop.plannotator-webview). **Obsidian**: Auto-save approved plans to a vault with YAML frontmatter, tags from the plan title, and backlinks for graph connectivity. Configure in Plannotator's Settings panel. **Bear**: Save plans as Bear notes with nested tags and project metadata. **Notion**: Save plans as Markdown child pages under a shared Notion page. Set `NOTION_TOKEN` in the environment that starts Plannotator, then configure the parent page in Settings. **GitHub / GitLab**: Pass any PR or MR URL to `/plannotator-review` and review it with the full diff viewer, annotations, and file tree. --- ## Remote / SSH / devcontainer Plannotator auto-detects SSH sessions and switches to fixed port `19432`. For a different port, or in a devcontainer or Docker: ```bash export PLANNOTATOR_REMOTE=1 export PLANNOTATOR_PORT=9999 # forward this port ``` VS Code devcontainers forward the port automatically (check the Ports tab). For raw SSH, add this to `~/.ssh/config`, using your `PLANNOTATOR_PORT` value if you set one: ``` Host your-server LocalForward 19432 localhost:19432 ``` In remote mode the server listens on every interface (`0.0.0.0`) with no login, so anyone who can reach the port can use it, even when you use an SSH tunnel. Keep the port closed to networks you don't trust. --- ## Security Every released binary ships with a SHA256 sidecar. [SLSA provenance](https://slsa.dev/) attestations are available from v0.17.2. The current release workflow also attaches a CycloneDX JSON SBOM, evaluates it with a fresh Grype database before anything is attested or published, and creates a GitHub/Sigstore SBOM attestation for the shipped binaries and npm tarballs. The SBOM is intentionally labeled as a release-wide Syft inventory of the monorepo's locked build inputs and dependencies. It is not an exact per-binary runtime inventory: Bun standalone executables do not expose their bundled JavaScript package metadata to Syft. The canonical [installation and verification docs](https://docs.plannotator.ai/open-source/start/installation#pin-or-verify-a-release) cover the existing installer path; the exact new SBOM commands are included below and must be copied to that Mintlify page before the first SBOM-enabled release. The release gate rejects scanner-side ignored matches and treats unknown applicability conservatively as runtime when evaluating CISA KEV and fixable Critical findings. Its explicit Grype configuration, complete JSON results, database status, and repository policy decision remain available as workflow evidence. To verify a released Linux x64 binary, its existing provenance, and the new SBOM evidence directly: ```bash tag=vX.Y.Z version="${tag#v}" mkdi

# dsh-restart-win **A Windows-only, verify-before-you-stop restart engine for a DSH host.** It boots a throw-away instance in a temporary home on a free port, proves that this configuration can come up, and only then touches the instance that is serving you. The stop and the launch run from a detached supervisor or a scheduled task, so the host dying cannot take the executor with it. `@brainzombie/dsh-restart-win` · Windows 10/11 · Node ≥ 20 · DSH 0.2.x · MIT English | [中文](README.zh.md) --- ## 1. What this is A DSH host plugin that turns "restart safely" into five verifiable steps: 1. **Discover** — the authority for "which process is the host" is the port listener from `netstat -ano -p TCP`, not WMI/CIM and not command-line matching. 2. **Prove** — boot a real instance in an isolated home on a free port. Only `401`/`200` counts as ready (`404` means the port is bound but routes are not registered yet). 3. **Gate** — if the preflight fails, nothing moves: the old instance is untouched, the call returns a non-zero exit code with a reason. 4. **Stop and launch** — write the resume notice → stop the old instance → wait until the port is actually bindable → rebuild the environment block → launch → verify port ownership and the parent chain. 5. **Close out** — every outcome writes an audit record; if the abort happened after the stop, try one rescue launch. It is an engine, not a button. The four host tools and the CLI all drive the same PowerShell script, `scripts/dsh-restart.ps1`, and keep the old engine's parameters, exit codes, terminal words and state files. --- ## 2. How it differs from the restart plugins already out there Most restart options are "a button that restarts immediately" or "a watchdog outside the process that retries". These are the 13 projects that GitHub's `dsh-plugin` topic returned by stars in 2026-11: | Project | Shape | Relation to this plugin | |---|---|---| | `anweat/dsh-restart` (npm `dsh-restart`) | Configurable restart + post-restart prompt resume + watchdog | Overlapping (resume, watchdog); different package name | | npm `dsh-restart-guard` | Out-of-process watchdog, restarts and reports to This plugin only guarantees the notice is written **before** the stop. --- ## 3. Requirements | Item | Requirement | Notes | |---|---|---| | OS | Windows 10 / 11 | The engine targets Windows only; elsewhere there is no PowerShell and the tools fail with an explicit error | | PowerShell | `pwsh` 7.4+ | A verified restart needs `Start-Process -Environment`.
