# DSH WSL run mode English | [中文](README.zh.md) Lets DeepSeek Harness Desktop on Windows run tasks in WSL. For a task that runs in WSL, the agent, its commands, file access and plugins all run in a DSH inside WSL, while you keep using the Desktop window. > Beta. See [tested versions](#tested-versions) for verification scope and report problems on [GitHub](https://github.com/herenfor/dsh-wsl/issues). ![The new-task page: the sidebar lists Windows and WSL tasks together, the run location is picked under the input box; the desktop pet in the corner is a plugin installed in WSL](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/herenfor/dsh-wsl/main/docs/screenshots/home-en.webp) Screenshots from a test environment, for illustration only. The third-party plugins shown are listed under "Screenshot credits" at the end. ## Highlights - **Run location per folder**: switch between Windows and WSL under the input box; folders inside WSL run in WSL by themselves. - **One window for both sides**: the sidebar, scheduled tasks and the choices in Settings list Windows and WSL together. - **Linux plugins just work**: plugins installed in WSL, including ones that change the interface, work in the Desktop window, and have their own WSL tab on the Plugins page. - **Credentials stay out of WSL**: WSL tasks get model credentials from Desktop; nothing is written to the WSL disk. - **No official code changed**: built only from plugins and external components, starting and stopping with Desktop. ## Requirements - DSH Desktop 0.2.x on Windows 10 or 11. - WSL 2 with a Linux distribution: Ubuntu, Debian or whichever you have. If WSL is not installed yet, there is no distribution, or the distribution still runs on WSL 1, the setup window lists the commands to run in PowerShell. - A DSH in WSL whose version matches Desktop in its first two parts (for example both 0.2.x). Without one, the plugin lists the install commands; it can run them for you or hand them to the Windows DSH (step 3 below). ## Install **Install this package in Windows Desktop only. It deploys `dsh-wsl-agent` inside WSL automatically. If you installed the bridge inside WSL by mistake, remove it there; removing this package does not delete sessions or user files.** 1. Desktop → Plugins → Add plugin → Install a third-party plugin, enter `@herenfor/dsh-wsl` and install. 2. Quit Desktop completely (if it keeps running in the system tray, quit it there too), wait at least 5 seconds, then open it again. Until then the plugin does not start working, and the bottom of the sidebar says to restart Desktop. 3. On the new-task page, switch the run location under the input box to WSL. The first time, "Set up the WSL environment" opens; choose one way: - **Reuse your dsh**: offered when WSL already has dsh. Desktop shares data with the dsh you use in WSL yourself, so tasks show up on both; plugins follow your own dsh too (see "Installing plugins in WSL" below); updates update both. The plugin looks for `dsh` on your PATH (including a login shell's), in `~/.local/bin`, `/usr/local/bin`, `/usr/bin`, and in the global folders of nvm, fnm, pnpm, bun and `~/.npm-global`. If yours is somewhere else (installed into a project folder, or started by a script of your own), enter its location in the setup window: the command, the `@deepseek-ai/dsh` package folder or its `lib/bin.js`. - **A separate copy for this plugin**: installed in `~/.dsh-wsl/dsh` with its data in `~/.dsh-wsl/home`, leaving your own dsh alone. About 250 MB to download, about 900 MB installed. If Node.js or DSH is missing, the window lists the commands to run, and under "Where setup looked" which places were checked. After switching, tasks from the other way no longer show in the list; their data is not deleted. - Switch the distribution, when you have more than one. Sync failures distinguish the completed change in the current profile from a failed update to the source profile. Chinese and English wording are updated together. ## Tested versions Tested with DSH **0.2.2-rc.1, 0.2.2-rc.2 and 0.2.2-rc.3**. Browser fixtures drive plugin rows and sync failures, with screenshots checked in Chinese and English. The historical native Desktop record covers entry migration, connection and task mirroring after the first restart, with UI checked through code and state. ## Features in detail Reuse mode detects DSH on PATH and in common standalone install folders, so an entry usually needs no input. Manual entries are under “Advanced”. Saved pnpm version paths are repaired when the corresponding stable package entry is valid; check again after upgrading to pick up the new version. ### Run location and folders - **Choose where each folder runs**: on the new-task page, pick "Windows" or "WSL (distribution)" under the input box. The choice is kept per folder: new tasks in that folder run there from then on, and existing tasks stay where they are. Folders inside WSL (`\\wsl.localhost\…`) always run in WSL. - **Windows folders can run in WSL too**: WSL reads and writes them through paths like `/mnt/c/…`, which is slower than a folder inside WSL, and a note under the input box says so. The sidebar still shows it as one folder, with both sides' tasks under it. - **Add WSL folders**: when adding a folder, choose a Windows folder or a WSL folder. A WSL folder is picked by browsing the Linux file system right in Desktop. ![The run-location menu](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/herenfor/dsh-wsl/main/docs/screenshots/picker-en.webp) ### Tasks and the sidebar - **Both sides in one list**: the sidebar lists the folders and tasks of Windows and WSL together, with a small penguin on WSL ones. Approvals, questions, subagents and live titles work as in any task. - **Scheduled tasks together**: the scheduled tasks page lists both sides' scheduled tasks, and viewing, editing, running now and deleting one go to the side it lives on. A scheduled task that starts a new task is created on the side where the chosen folder runs. - **Starts and stops with Desktop**: the WSL side starts when Desktop opens and exits about 5 seconds after Desktop closes. ### Plugins - **WSL plugins on their own tab**: the Plugins page gets a "WSL (distribution)" tab to install, enable, disable and uninstall plugins in WSL, with a page per plugin showing its description and the state of each component. The official Installed tab still covers Windows only; the two sides do not affect each other. Plugins installed only in WSL, including ones that change the interface, work in the Desktop window too. To install them, see "Installing plugins in WSL" below. - **MCP servers set per side**: an MCP server's command, paths and environment variables differ between Windows and WSL, so they are not copied from Windows. Set up WSL's MCP servers at the bottom of the "WSL (distribution)" tab on the Plugins page; they serve only tasks that run in WSL. ### Settings and credentials - **Desktop's model credentials**: when a WSL task calls a model, it asks Desktop for the credentials; API keys and sign-ins are never written to the WSL disk. An API key you entered in WSL yourself takes precedence. - **Desktop's settings win**: settings you can change in Desktop (model, theme, language and so on) are copied one way into WSL. Settings of a plugin installed only in WSL show up on Desktop's settings page too, and changes made there are saved straight to WSL. - **Both sides' choices in one list**: where you pick one entry from a list (the default preset, the default permission preset, the search service, the model), the list shows both sides' entries, with " · WSL" on those only WSL has. When you pick one that only one side has, tasks on the other side use that side's own default, and the presets page says what the other side uses. - **Follows DSH's language**: Chinese and English for now; other languages show English. ## Installing plugins in WSL Desktop runs its WSL tasks in a profile of its own in WSL, `desktop-wsl`. Where its plugins come from depends on the run mode: - **Reuse your dsh**: plugins follow the `web` profile of your own dsh. Each time Desktop starts the WSL side, the plugins installed in `web`, whether they are on, and their settings are carried over; installing, uninstalling or switching a plugin in the tab below changes `web` too (your own dsh picks it up when it next starts); plugin settings changed in Desktop are written back to `web` at the next start, and when both sides changed one, `web` wins. Desktop's own settings (model, theme, language and so on) are never written to `web`. Plugins installed only in `desktop-wsl` before stay as they are, marked "This profile only" in the tab. "Follows web" means the plugin follows the `web` profile inside WSL; both labels describe WSL profiles. To follow another profile, add `"pluginProfile": ""` to `%USERPROFILE%\.dsh-wsl\config.json`. - **A separate copy for this plugin**: its plugins are its own, starting with the official ones. Install here: Plugins → "WSL (distribution)" → enter an npm package name, git URL or local folder path in the install box → Check → Install. Windows paths are turned into WSL paths. When it says a restart is needed, quit Desktop completely, wait at least 5 seconds and open it again. ![The WSL tab on the Plugins page](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/herenfor/dsh-wsl/main/docs/screenshots/plugins-en.webp) ![A WSL plugin's page](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/herenfor/dsh-wsl/main/docs/screenshots/detail-en.webp) ![DS Bot installed in WSL, with its own interface working in the Desktop window; the Bot runs a command in WSL to check the environment](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/herenfor/dsh-wsl/main/docs/screenshots/bot-en.webp) ## Updates - The plugin itself never updates in the background, which could cut off WSL tasks that are running. Check for and install updates under Plugins → Installed → WSL run mode, at a moment when no WSL task is running, then quit Desktop completely and open it again; until then the sidebar asks for the restart. The bottom of the setup window shows the installed version. - The DSH in WSL follows Desktop's version. After Desktop updates, the setup window offers to update the WSL side. A dsh you reuse that is not an npm global install (in a project folder, or installed with pnpm) is not updated by the plugin, which would put a second copy beside it: update it your own way. ## Uninstall 1. Desktop → Plugins → Installed → uninstall "WSL run mode", then restart Desktop. 2. Remove what is left in WSL by hand: - `~/.dsh-wsl`: connection files, logs, and in the separate-copy mode its DSH and data. - In the reuse mode also `~/.dsh/profiles/desktop-wsl`, the profile the plugin created. Task data lives in `~/.dsh`, shared with your own dsh: **do not delete all of `~/.dsh`**. ## When something goes wrong - When the bottom of the sidebar says the WSL side failed to start, click it to see the error. - When your dsh or Node.js is not found, the setup window lists where it looked. The full output of the last check is in `%USERPROFILE%\.dsh-wsl\setup-probe.log` on Windows. - If you chose to reuse your dsh and it is later not found (moved, removed), the WSL side stays off and the setup window asks for its new location; it does not switch to the plugin's own copy by itself. - The WSL side's log is `~/.dsh-wsl/run/desktop-wsl/daemon.log`. When the WSL side fails before it can write that log, the error is in `%USERPROFILE%\.dsh-wsl\bridge.log` on Windows. - Feedback: ## Known limitations - Desktop and the DSH in WSL must match in the first two parts of their versions; see [tested versions](#tested-versions) for verification scope. - In the separate-copy mode, WSL tasks are not shared with your own dsh, and tasks cannot be moved between the two ways yet. - Reusing your dsh runs its package directly with Node, with its data in `~/.dsh`. It does not go through launch scripts or wrappers of your own: environment variables, ports or a `DSH_HOME` set there are not applied. - When a WSL plugin's patch changes the configuration of an official component (rather than switching it off), that change does not apply in the Desktop window. - The interface of WSL plugins loads into the whole Desktop window, not only into WSL tasks. - Closing Desktop stops the WSL side as well; WSL tasks do not keep running in the background, and WSL's scheduled tasks run only while Desktop is open. - Referring to another task with @ works only within one side: a WSL task is offered WSL tasks, a Windows task Windows tasks. - The "All plugins" page in Settings lists Windows plugins only; WSL plugins are on the "WSL (distribution)" tab. ## Screenshot credits Screenshots from a test environment, for illustration only. Third-party plugins shown: the desktop pet [dsh-pet](https://github.com/PC2005-cloud/dsh-pet) (PC2005-cloud; code MIT, character art not for commercial use), [DS Bot](https://github.com/Fei2411/DS-Bot) (Fei2411, Apache-2.0), [Claude Code Style](https://github.com/Nwflower/dsh-claude-style) (Nwflower, MIT) and [dsh-runtime-tuning](https://github.com/herenfor/dsh-runtime-tuning) (MIT). Names and artwork belong to their authors. In the DS Bot screenshot, the replies come from a local stand-in model used for testing; the system details in the table are the real output of the command run in WSL. ## License MIT. The session ID field table is adapted from [dsh-ssh-workspaces](https://github.com/czp0312/dsh-ssh-workspace) (MIT); see `LICENSE` for its notice.
# dsh-wsl **Run DeepSeek Harness tasks in WSL from the Windows Desktop window** [![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/@herenfor/dsh-wsl?label=npm&color=cb3837)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@herenfor/dsh-wsl) ![DSH 0.2.x](https://img.shields.io/badge/DSH-0.2.x-4d6bfe) ![beta](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-beta-orange) [![MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-2ea44f)](LICENSE) English · [中文](README.zh.md)

The WSL tab on the Plugins page
DS Bot installed in WSL, with its own interface working in the Desktop window
## Quick start **Install `@herenfor/dsh-wsl` in Windows Desktop only. It deploys the WSL companion, `dsh-wsl-agent`, automatically; do not install a second bridge inside WSL.** 1. Desktop → Plugins → Add plugin → Install a third-party plugin, enter `@herenfor/dsh-wsl` and install. 2. Quit Desktop completely (in the system tray too), wait at least 5 seconds, then open it again. 3. On the new-task page, switch the run location under the input box to WSL and follow the "Set up the WSL environment" window. Reuse mode detects DSH on PATH and in common standalone install folders, so an entry usually needs no input. Manual entries are under “Advanced”. Saved pnpm version paths are repaired when the corresponding stable package entry is valid; check again after upgrading to pick up the new version. Needs DSH Desktop 0.2.x on Windows 10 or 11, and WSL 2. Feature details, other ways to install, updates, uninstalling, troubleshooting and known limitations are in the [plugin's README](experiments/mirror/mirror/README.md). ## This update The WSL plugin page now uses **“This profile only”** and **“Follows web”**, with hover explanations of the profiles inside WSL. Sync failures distinguish the completed change in the current profile from a failed update to the source profile. Chinese and English wording are updated together. ## Tested versions Tested with DSH **0.2.2-rc.1, 0.2.2-rc.2 and 0.2.2-rc.3**. The scope differs between records: | Verification | Plugin version | DSH version | Scope | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Current local candidate | **0.1.14** | **0.2.2-rc.3** | 64 unit tests; real manager and two isolated Hosts for wrong-location rejection, removal recovery, retained sessions and reinstall; Chinese/English label and sync-failure screenshots | | Latest use-side recovery record | **0.1.12** | Desktop / WSL both **0.2.2-rc.3** | Bridge and tuning loaded after configuration repair and restart; `web` was stopped, so creating a session there was not checked online | | Historical native Desktop entry acceptance | **0.1.12-dev.1** | Desktop / WSL both **0.2.2-rc.3** | Automatic discovery, persistent old pnpm entry migration, Host / daemon startup and first-restart connection and task mirroring | | Earlier compatibility work | Earlier releases | **0.2.2-rc.1, 0.2.2-rc.2** | Historical bridge, plugin-mirroring and installation checks | The current local setup uses two isolated Linux Hosts in the Desktop and WSL roles. Browser fixtures drive plugin rows and sync failures, with screenshots checked in Chinese and English. The historical native Desktop record covers entry migration, connection and task mirroring after the first restart, with UI checked through code and state. --- ## How it works ``` Windows WSL Desktop (DSH Host + page) DSH Host (profile desktop-wsl) └ plugin @herenfor/dsh-wsl └ plugin dsh-wsl-agent ├ per-task routing: WSL tasks go to WSL ├ reports WSL's page modules, routes and plugins ├ merges both sides' sidebar, modules, └ credential broker: asks Desktop when needed │ settings └ one wsl.exe connection ◄──────────────► resident daemon, exits 5 s after Desktop closes ``` - Transport: one multiplexed connection over `wsl.exe`'s standard input and output, with a resident process on the WSL side, the same approach as Claude Code Desktop's WSL mode. - Session IDs: WSL sessions and folders carry a `wsl:` prefix on the page; forwarded requests are rewritten by field and by value. - Credentials: never copied into WSL; the WSL side gets a credential broker that asks Desktop when it needs one. - Settings: copied one way into WSL. The rules and trade-offs are in [docs/cross-host-rules.md](docs/cross-host-rules.md) (Chinese). - Lists across both sides: scheduled tasks, presets, models and similar lists merge both sides; a call on one entry goes back to its side by its ID prefix. ## Repository layout | Path | Contents | |---|---| | `experiments/mirror/mirror/` | The Desktop-side plugin, the package published to npm: routing, merging, the setup window, the WSL plugins tab, page code in `client.js` | | `experiments/mirror/agent/` | The WSL-side plugin `dsh-wsl-agent`, carried into WSL by the Desktop-side plugin | | `experiments/transport/` | The `wsl.exe` connection: multiplexing (`mux.mjs`), the Desktop end (`client.mjs`), the WSL daemon (`daemon.mjs`) | | `experiments/mirror/tests/` | Unit tests | | `scripts/release.sh` | Releases a version (see below) | | `scripts/assemble.sh` | Copies transport and agent into the plugin package | | `.github/workflows/publish.yml` | Publishes to npm when a version tag is pushed | | `scripts/sync-windows.sh` | Development: assembles, then copies the package into a Windows test folder | | `dev/` | Test environment for development: a `dsh web` on Linux standing in for Desktop, a fake `wsl.exe`, screenshot tools; see [dev/README.md](dev/README.md) (in Chinese) | | `docs/` | Design and experiment notes (in Chinese) | | `CLAUDE.md` | For an agent taking over: status, entry points, rules (in Chinese) | ## Development ```bash node --test experiments/mirror/tests/*.test.mjs ``` ### Releasing ```bash scripts/release.sh 0.1.1 --dry-run # tests, assembles, checks the package contents; changes nothing scripts/release.sh 0.1.1 # then sets the version, commits, tags v0.1.1 and pushes ``` The pushed tag starts `.github/workflows/publish.yml`, which runs the tests, checks that the tag matches the version and that the package carries the current bridge files, and publishes to npm with npm trusted publishing (no npm token stored in GitHub). A version with a pre-release part (`0.2.0-beta.1`) goes to the npm tag `next`. Installed copies are updated by their users from the Plugins page; nothing updates in the background. The workflow publishes only once the package's trusted publisher is set on npmjs.com (settings of `@herenfor/dsh-wsl`: GitHub Actions, repository `herenfor/dsh-wsl`, workflow `publish.yml`). Until then, or to publish from your own machine, use `scripts/release.sh --local` after `npm login`: it publishes, waits until the version is live (approve it on npmjs.com if npm staged it for 2FA approval), then commits, tags and pushes. A failed run changes nothing and can simply be run again. `scripts/assemble.sh` copies the latest `experiments/transport` and `experiments/mirror/agent` files into the package; the release script runs it. `scripts/sync-windows.sh` is for development: it also copies the package into a Windows test folder you name, which a Desktop links to. For end-to-end tests the test environment in `dev/` is usually enough. ## Documents (in Chinese) - [docs/bridge-plan.md](docs/bridge-plan.md): the bridge (transport, deployment, per-session routing). - [docs/session-routing.md](docs/session-routing.md): per-session routing; each task runs in Windows or WSL, and the sidebar lists both. - [docs/plugin-management.md](docs/plugin-management.md): plugin management and the page mirror. - [docs/panel.md](docs/panel.md): the Plugins page (now separate Windows and WSL tabs). - [docs/credentials.md](docs/credentials.md): how WSL sessions use Desktop's credentials. - [docs/deployment.md](docs/deployment.md): first-run setup, version rules, plugin self-update, interface language. - [docs/cross-host-scan.md](docs/cross-host-scan.md) and [docs/cross-host-rules.md](docs/cross-host-rules.md): the scan for differences between the two sides, and the rules that settle them, compared with VS Code Remote and Claude Code. ## Screenshot credits Screenshots from a test environment, for illustration only. Third-party plugins shown: the desktop pet [dsh-pet](https://github.com/PC2005-cloud/dsh-pet) (PC2005-cloud; code MIT, character art not for commercial use), [DS Bot](https://github.com/Fei2411/DS-Bot) (Fei2411, Apache-2.0), [Claude Code Style](https://github.com/Nwflower/dsh-claude-style) (Nwflower, MIT) and [dsh-runtime-tuning](https://github.com/herenfor/dsh-runtime-tuning) (MIT). Names and artwork belong to their authors. In the DS Bot screenshot, the replies come from a local stand-in model used for testing; the system details in the table are the real output of the command run in WSL. ## License MIT, see [LICENSE](LICENSE). The ID field table in `experiments/mirror/mirror/ids.mjs` is adapted from [dsh-ssh-workspaces](https://github.com/czp0312/dsh-ssh-workspace) (MIT); its copyright notice ships with the plugin package (`experiments/mirror/mirror/LICENSE`).

The rules and trade-offs are in [docs/cross-host-rules.md](docs/cross-host-rules.md) (Chinese). - Lists across both sides: scheduled tasks, presets, models and similar lists merge both sides; a call on one entry goes back to its side by its ID prefix. ## Repository layout | Path | Contents | |---|---| | `experiments/mirror/mirror/` | The Desktop-side plugin, the package published to npm: routing, merging, the setup window, the WSL plugins tab, page code in `client.js` | | `experiments/mirror/agent/` | The WSL-side plugin `dsh-wsl-agent`, carried into WSL by the Desktop-side plugin | | `experiments/transport/` | The `wsl.exe` connection: multiplexing (`mux.mjs`), the Desktop end (`client.mjs`), the WSL daemon (`daemon.mjs`) | | `experiments/mirror/tests/` | Unit tests | | `scripts/release.sh` | Releases a version (see below) | | `scripts/assemble.sh` | Copies transport and agent into the plugin package | | `.github/workflows/publish.yml` | Publishes to npm when a version tag is pushed | | `scripts/sync-windows.sh` | Development: assembles, then copies the package into a Windows test folder | | `dev/` | Test environment for development: a `dsh web` on Linux standing in for Desktop, a fake `wsl.exe`, screenshot tools; see [dev/README.md](dev/README.md) (in Chinese) | | `docs/` | Design and experiment notes (in Chinese) | | `CLAUDE.md` | For an agent taking over: status, entry points, rules (in Chinese) | ## Development ```bash node --test experiments/mirror/tests/*.test.mjs ``` ### Releasing ```bash scripts/release.sh 0.1.1 --dry-run # tests, assembles, checks the package contents; changes nothing scripts/release.sh 0.1.1 # then sets the version, commits, tags v0.1.1 and pushes ``` The pushed tag starts `.github/workflows/publish.yml`, which runs the tests, checks that the tag matches the version and that the package carries the current bridge files, and publishes to npm with npm trusted publishing (no npm token stored in GitHub). A version with a pre-release part (`0.2.0-beta.1`) goes to the npm tag `next`. Installed copies are updated by their users from the Plugins page; nothing updates in the background. The workflow publishes only once the package's trusted publisher is set on npmjs.com (settings of `@herenfor/dsh-wsl`: GitHub Actions, repository `herenfor/dsh-wsl`, workflow `publish.yml`). Until then, or to publish from your own machine, use `scripts/release.sh --local` after `npm login`: it publishes, waits until the version is live (approve it on npmjs.com if npm staged it for 2FA approval), then commits, tags and pushes. A failed run changes nothing and can simply be run again. `scripts/assemble.sh` copies the latest `experiments/transport` and `experiments/mirror/agent` files into the package; the release script runs it. `scripts/sync-windows.sh` is for development: it also copies the package into a Windows test folder you name, which a Desktop links to. For end-to-end tests the test environment in `dev/` is usually enough. ## Documents (in Chinese) - [docs/bridge-plan.md](docs/bridge-plan.md): the bridge (transport, deployment, per-session routing). - [docs/session-routing.md](docs/session-routing.md): per-session routing; each task runs in Windows or WSL, and the sidebar lists both. - [docs/plugin-management.md](docs/plugin-management.md): plugin management and the page mirror. - [docs/panel.md](docs/panel.md): the Plugins page (now separate Windows and WSL tabs). - [docs/credentials.md](docs/credentials.md): how WSL sessions use Desktop's credentials. - [docs/deployment.md](docs/deployment.md): first-run setup, version rules, plugin self-update, interface language. - [docs/cross-host-scan.md](docs/cross-host-scan.md) and [docs/cross-host-rules.md](docs/cross-host-rules.md): the scan for differences between the two sides, and the rules that settle them, compared with VS Code Remote and Claude Code. ## Screenshot credits Screenshots from a test environment, for illustration only. Third-party plugins shown: the desktop pet [dsh-pet](https://github.com/PC2005-cloud/dsh-pet) (PC2005-cloud; code MIT, character art not for commercial use), [DS Bot](https://github.com/Fei2411/DS-Bot) (Fei2411, Apache-2.0), [Claude Code Style](https://github.com/Nwflower/dsh-claude-style) (Nwflower, MIT) and [dsh-runtime-tuning](https://github.com/herenfor/dsh-runtime-tuning) (MIT). Names and artwork belong to their authors. In the DS Bot screenshot, the replies come from a local stand-in model used for testing; the system details in the table are the real output of the command run in WSL. ## License MIT, see [LICENSE](LICENSE). The ID field table in `experiments/mirror/mirror/ids.mjs` is adapted from [dsh-ssh-workspaces](https://github.com/czp0312/dsh-ssh-workspace) (MIT); its copyright notice ships with the plugin package (`experiments/mirror/mirror/LICENSE`).

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# dsh-scheduled-message

Schedule the message you are already writing in the DSH composer — text, images and files — to be
delivered later by the **Host**. Because the timer and the store live in the Host, closing the tab or
the window does not cancel anything, and a message whose time passed while DSH was closed is sent at
the next start and marked **sent late**.

A **Scheduled** tab in the left sidebar then lists every scheduled message across all conversations,
in time order, and lets you edit the time, the text, the attachments and the destination, move a
message to another conversation (or to a new one), send it now, delete it, or retry a failed
delivery. Normal sending is untouched: Enter, Shift+Enter, Ctrl/Cmd+Enter and the Send button keep
exactly their current meaning.

![The Schedule message dialog: message preview, quick picks, date and 12-hour time, the "Sends …" summary and the Repeat row](docs/preview.png)

## What you get

| Surface | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| **Schedule** button | Orange pill beside Send in the composer tool row. Disabled while the draft is empty or the composer is busy. |
| **Alt+Enter** (Option+Enter on macOS) | Opens the same dialog. Registered as an editable-region shortcut, editable in Settings › Shortcuts. |
| **Dialog** | Date, hour 1–12, minute, AM/PM, quick picks, a "Sends …" summary, and an optional **Repeat** row. Backdrop/Escape close, focus returns to the composer. |
| **Scheduled tab** | Every scheduled message, across every conversation, grouped by day. Hover actions: **Send now**, **Edit**, **Delete**. Failed rows show the reason plus **Retry**. |
| **Editor** | Change the time, the text, images and files, and the destination — an existing conversation or a new one that is created when the message is due. Saves detect concurrent edits instead of overwriting them. |
| **Strip** | Above the composer: `2 scheduled · next Fri, 14 Nov, 9:00 am`, expandable to rows with **Send now**, **Change time**, **Cancel**, **Retry**, and a **View all** link to the tab. |
| **Repeat** | Creates a task in DSH's own Automation service and opens its task page. Blocked when the draft has images or files. |
| **Peak-price hint** | When the chosen time lands in DeepSeek's peak window and the session runs a DeepSeek model, the dialog adds one orange line naming the window in your own time zone. Weekends and off-peak hours are half price. |
| **Phone** | Bottom sheet under 640 px, 44 px targets, 16 px inputs (no zoom-on-focus), safe-area padding. |
| **Theme** | Host tokens for every surface and text colour; the accent orange is the only literal colour. English and Chinese dictionaries ship complete. |

## The Scheduled tab

The tab sits directly under **Automation tasks** in the sidebar and opens as a full page: one centred
column, a count under the title, then day groups — **Today**, **Tomorrow**, the weekday for the next
few days, then a full date. Grouping uses your browser zone, not the Host's.

- **Rows** show the send time, the message preview, the destination (`workspace › conversation`) and
  attachment chips — image thumbnails and file names with sizes. Hovering (or tapping, on a phone)
  reveals **Send now**, **Edit** and **Delete**; clicking the row opens the editor.
- **Failed** rows carry a red rule and the delivery reason, with **Retry** and **Edit**.
- **Sent** messages stay for 24 hours in a collapsed, dimmed group; a late one is labelled
  **sent late**.
- **Repeating** messages are listed read-only with a link to **Automation tasks** — they belong to
  DSH's Automation service, which delivers text only.
- **All / This workspace**: when a conversation is open, one small control narrows the list to that
  workspace. Without that mapping the tab simply shows everything.

### Editing one message

The editor opens as a side sheet on wide screens (the list stays visible), a centred dialog in the
middle, and a full-height bottom sheet on a phone. Top to bottom: **When** (the same quick picks,
date and 12-hour clock as the dialog, with the "Sends …" summary and the peak-price note), **Message**
(an auto-growing textarea), **Attachments** (chips with a thumbnail or file glyph, size and ×; add
files, drop them on the editor, or paste an image), **Send to** (a searchable picker of workspaces and
their conversations, plus **+ New conversation** per workspace), and the footer: **Delete** on the
left, **Cancel** and **Save** on the right.

Save sends only what changed and carries the record's `updatedAt`. If the message changed in another
tab meanwhile, the save is refused: your text stays, the record is reloaded, and a notice asks you to
review and save again. If the message was sent while you were editing, the editor closes and tells you
so.

A message can be moved to another workspace's conversation — its attachments travel with it, because
stored attachments are not tied to a conversation — or to **a conversation that does not exist yet**,
which is created in the chosen workspace when the message is due. That creation is written to the
record before the message is sent, so a crash cannot produce two conversations or two copies.

The list refreshes when the panel opens, after every action, on window focus, when the tab becomes
visible again, and once shortly after the next due time. There is no interval polling.

## Install

Published on npm as `dsh-scheduled-message`. The package is a normal DSH plugin bundle: a Host half
(`index.js`), a browser half (`client.js`), and one patch entry.

```sh
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add dsh-scheduled-message
```

Replace `<profile>` with the profile your host runs — `web` for a plain `dsh web`. DSH Desktop keeps
its own profile, so install there from **Settings → Plugins** instead of the command line.

The command forwards to pnpm in the profile directory and, because the package declares `dsh.bundle`,
adds it to `dsh.profile.bundles` as well. Then restart DSH.

The market card does the same thing in one click: **Plugins** → **Discover**, search *scheduled
message*.

Needs DSH `0.2.2-rc.2` or newer (`engines.dsh`).

### Without a package manager

Put the folder where the profile can resolve it, list it in that profile's `package.json`, and
restart:

```sh
cp -r dsh-scheduled-message ~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/node_modules/dsh-scheduled-message
```

```jsonc
"dependencies": { "dsh-scheduled-message": "file:./node_modules/dsh-scheduled-message" },
"dsh": { "profile": { "bundles": [ …, "dsh-scheduled-message" ] } }
```

With the plugin manager available, `install_bundle` with this directory as the target does the same
thing and reports `application: applied`.

Registering the row directly, without touching `dsh.profile.bundles`, also works — the bundle ships
`cordis.patch.yml`:

```yaml
- insert:
    - id: dsh-scheduled-message
      name: dsh-scheduled-message
```

### Upgrading from 0.2.x

Nothing to do. The stored records are version 1; the plugin writes version 2 and reads both, so
messages scheduled before the upgrade still deliver. Before the first 0.3.0 run the v1 storage unit
was copied to `.backup/` in this repository if you want a copy of the old file.

## Using it

1. Type the message and attach anything you want.
2. Press **Alt+Enter**, or click **Schedule**.
3. Pick a date and a time on the 12-hour clock, or use a quick pick.
4. Press **Schedule**. The draft and its attachments are cleared and the message appears in the strip.
5. Close the tab whenever you like. Delivery is the Host's job.
6. Open **Scheduled** in the sidebar to see everything that is waiting, change it, or move it.

Tick **Repeat** instead to create an Automation task: daily, weekdays, weekly on the chosen weekday,
or monthly on the chosen day. Monthly rules on the 29th–31st skip months that are too short.

## What it does not do

- **No repeating messages with attachments.** The Automation service delivers text only, so the UI
  and the Host validator both refuse that combination. Repeating tasks are edited in Automation tasks,
  never in the Scheduled tab.
- **No auto-retry.** A failed delivery is reported with its reason; **Retry** is a user action.
- **No polling.** The strip and the tab refresh on mount, after an action, on window focus, on
  becoming visible, and once shortly after the next due time.
- **No invented conversation names.** DSH's session list does not carry a title, so a destination
  shows the workspace name and a short conversation id unless the build exposes a title.
- **No attachment deletion.** Removing a chip drops the reference to the stored file; the bytes
  follow DSH's own attachment retention, because this build has no delete API.
- **No cross-zone surprise.** The browser's IANA zone is captured at create time and only used for
  display and for the 12-hour reading; the Host stores one absolute instant.
- **Disabling the plugin does not delete anything.** Pending records stay in storage and resume when
  the plugin is enabled again.

## Layout

```
index.js              Host half: durable store, thirteen /api routes, timer, delivery
client.js             browser bundle (generated — see scripts/build-client.mjs)
client.src.js         browser half source: composer button, dialog, strip, Scheduled tab, editor
lib/core.js           dependency-free shared logic: 12-hour clock, zone resolution, validation,
                      record schema v1→v2 migration, day grouping, RRULE text, retention
locale/en.json        English dictionary
locale/zh.json        Chinese dictionary
scripts/build-client.mjs   inlines lib/core.js + locale/*.json into client.js
scripts/check.mjs     static gates (bundle freshness, locale coverage, exports, registrations)
scripts/host-smoke.mjs     end-to-end Host test against in-memory services
test/*.test.mjs       node --test suites
docs/DETAIL.md        design notes, API evidence, and what is still unverified
```

## Development

```sh
npm run build     # regenerate client.js after editing client.src.js, lib/core.js or locale/*.json
npm test          # unit + bundle + Host smoke tests
npm run check     # static gates
```

## Status

`0.3.1`. 60 core tests, 20 client tests, one Host wrapper running 206 assertions, the static gates
and the standalone Host smoke test (206 assertions) all pass.

0.3.0 adds the **Scheduled** sidebar tab and its editor: every scheduled message in one list, with
the time, the text, the attachments and the destination editable, moves between conversations,
delivery into a newly created conversation, and read-only rows for repeating tasks. With it the
record schema moved to version 2 — the domain declares `compatibleVersions: [1]`, so records written
by 0.2.x still open and still deliver. 0.2.x added the DeepSeek peak-price hint; 0.1.1 fixed the
composer button so it enables as soon as you type.

0.3.1 fixes a blank panel: opening a scheduled message crashed the tab before its record had
loaded, because the editor tried to format a send time it did not have yet. `describeDue` now
answers an empty string instead of throwing, the editor only writes the summary once it has a real
instant, and `test/client.test.mjs` renders the editor's first paint so it cannot come back.

Verified: the two project gates, the Host end-to-end smoke test (including a v1 record opening
under the v2 schema and a `kind:'new'` delivery that creates exactly one conversation), the
bundle-freshness and dictionary-parity gates, the panel's two slot registrations structurally,
and the tab itself rendering in the live desktop GUI. Still a human look away: the editor's
sheet/dialog/bottom-sheet layouts, the destination picker against a real workspace list, and the
phone layout. Details are in [`docs/DETAIL.md`](docs/DETAIL.md#9-v2).

decision.reason: Static evidence chain reviewed. MIT, exact npm gitHead, patch, compiled client, host and lib/core.js agree with the frozen source. engines.dsh requires at least 0.2.2-rc.2. The host uses a versioned storage domain and authenticated connection routes to queue messages, manage attachment state and dispatch scheduled or repeating work. This can send messages after the current interaction. No candidate code or lifecycle hooks were executed; runtime safety and compatibility are unproven.

evidence.readmeExcerpt: # doubao-image — generate images with the local Doubao app > 面向：使用者 · 状态：stable · 最近核对：2026-09-20 Registers one tool, `generate_image`, that drives the **locally installed and logged-in Doubao (豆包) desktop app** to produce a picture, saves the full-resolution file, and sends it into the conversation. ``` plugins/doubao-image/ ├── package.json # type: module, dsh.bundle.patch, exports ├── cordis.patch.yml # bundle patch: the loader row ├── lib/ │ ├── index.js # cordis plugin: the generate_image tool │ ├── doubao.mjs # app launch, prompt submission, result harvest │ ├── cdp.mjs # dependency-free Chrome DevTools Protocol client │ ├── watermark.mjs # removes Doubao's own overlay, with a self-check │ ├── image.mjs # minimal PNG codec + raster helpers │ └── generate.mjs # CLI driver, for testing without spending a model turn └── test/ # node --test (no DSH, no app, no network) ``` ## Install ```bash # from npm dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-plugin-doubao-image # or from the repository root — the leading ./ matters: DSH anchors relative specs # against your current directory, otherwise pnpm would resolve it inside the profile dsh plugin --profile web add ./plugins/doubao-image ``` Then restart DSH (or reload the profile). The tool appears as `generate_image`. ## Use ```bash # exercise the whole path without going through the model node plugins/doubao-image/lib/generate.mjs \ --prompt "一只戴黄铜护目镜的橘猫，坐在双翼飞机驾驶舱里" \ --style "黏土质感 C4D 渲染，暖色夕阳光" \ --out ~/Pictures/doubao ``` The tool takes `prompt` (required) plus `style`, `composition`, `aspect`, `negative`, `count`, `dir`, and `reuseCurrentChat`. ## How it works, and why it is built this way Doubao ships a **full Chromium** (`Contents/Helpers/Doubao Browser.app`), and its launcher forwards unknown flags, so starting it with `--remote-debugging-port` yields a real CDP endpoint. That is the whole reason this works without the macOS Accessibility permission that `osascript` would need — which matters, because that permission is not granted on this machine. The findings each step depends on, all established by probing the running app: | Step | What is actually true | | --- | --- | | Launch | Doubao holds a **singleton lock**. A normally-launched instance never opens the debug port, and launching again just forwards to it. The app must therefore be quit and restarted — the first call costs ~10–40 s. | | Attach | `doubao-chat` is the real 1200×800 window. `doubao-launcher` is a 400×600 **sidebar that also accepts prompts** and renders results at 90 px, and `doubao-chat` is *additionally* served as an empty `hello` shell. Identification uses live window size plus the presence of the editor, never the URL alone. | | Type | The box is `div.tiptap.ProseMirror[contenteditable=true]`. `execCommand('insertText')` goes through the same `beforeinput` path a keystroke does, so the app's own state and send button update. Assigning `innerText` would not. | | Detect | The status sentence 「已生成 N 张候选图」 is the completion signal, not the image count — the grid mounts placeholders before the renders arrive. | | Harvest | The picture in the grid is a `cpreview_wm1` render behind an overlay, and its full-size sibling `` is a bare `data:image/svg+xml` **placeholder with no pixels**, so the bytes cannot be read from the grid. Instead the tool clicks each thumbnail to open the image viewer and uses the app's own `[data-testid=edit_image_download_button]`, which writes the file to `~/Downloads`; the tool then moves it to `dir`. | `dsh-doctor`-style checks live in the unit tests: the output schema must stay in sync with `execute`, because a tool that returns a value without a declared schema is refused at registration and takes the **whole plugin tree — and every DSH boot, the desktop app included — down with it**. ## The watermark Doubao stamps 「豆包AI生成」 into the bottom-right of every saved picture. It is an overlay the app composites on, not part of the artwork, which is what makes removal a solved problem instead of an inpainting guess. All of this was measured, not assumed: | Property | Measurement | | --- | --- | | Position | Anchored to the bottom-right corner; a glyph mask from one image correlates with an unrelated image's corner at **NCC 0.949** (inverse control −0.949, exactly symmetric) | | Scale | Proportional to the image's **short side**, not its width: 2048²→321×69 box, 1365×2048→214×46 box, both giving width/short ≈ 0.1567. Verified on a second sample per shape | | Blend | Plain alpha composite `C = a·W + (1−a)·B`, fitted at **a = 0.638**, W = 234.4, RMS residual 6.3/255 | | Soft edge | Glyph interiors measure a = 0.63 while the antialiased rim ramps to 0 — which is why a hard 0/1 mask left a visible outline | Removal inverts the composite per pixel, and estimates the artwork behind the mark by coarse-grid interpolation that excludes masked pixels. The output PNG is encoded losslessly (round-trip delta verified 0). **Self-check.** The `verifyOnFlat` helper turns "does it look clean?" into a number: on a flat-background sample the artwork behind the mark is a constant, so any residual offset inside the glyph area *is* the watermark that survived. Measured on a flat 2048² sample: **residual 46.3 → 0.0 (100% removed)**. On a photograph the same metric would be meaningless, so it detects a non-flat frame (background IQR > 8) and says so instead of printing a flattering zero. **Scope.** This targets this one overlay, at this one anchor, with this one calibrated blend. It is not a general watermark remover. It exists for internal reference material — animation reference, storyboards, internal review. Doubao's official API (Volcengine Ark) returns images with no watermark at all, and that is the right channel for anything published or commercial. **Stripping is off by default** (owner's decision, 2026-09-25): an image comes back with Doubao's own 「豆包AI生成」 badge unless the caller explicitly asks for `stripWatermark: true`. Keeping the badge is the safe default — it is what makes a picture traceable to the tool that made it — and the capability stays here for the internal-reference case described above. ## Known limitations - **Generation consumes the user's Doubao quota** (the app reports 「本次生成将 消耗每日免费额度」). Exactly one generation is issued per call; if the plugin cannot confirm a submission it stops rather than retrying, because a blind retry is what once produced duplicate generations. - **The app window is closed and reopened** on the first call, and Doubao must stay running-and-instrumented for the harvest to complete. - The harvest depends on Doubao's own UI markup (`image-box-grid`, `edit_image_download_button`). A Doubao redesign breaks it; the selector surface is deliberately kept to those two names. - The watermark pass only re-encodes PNG. # dsh-plugin-mobile-link

[![DSH plugin](https://img.shields.io/badge/DSH-plugin-4D6BFE)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness)
[![listed in awesome-deepseek-harness](https://img.shields.io/badge/listed%20in-awesome--deepseek--harness-4D6BFE?logo=awesomelists&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Dominic789654/awesome-deepseek-harness)
[![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/dsh-plugin-mobile-link)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-plugin-mobile-link)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](../../LICENSE)

> 面向：使用者与实现者 · 状态：stable · 最近核对：2026-09-20

**The computer half of [DSH Mobile](https://github.com/jayantTang/DSH_Mobile): it
dials a relay over WSS, so the native iOS client reaches this DSH instance even
though the computer has no public IP.**

```
iPhone App ──WSS──▶ Relay（公网，只鉴权与转发）──WSS──▶ this plugin ──HTTP+WS──▶ 127.0.0.1:<port>
```

The connector always talks to the local DSH as `127.0.0.1:<port>`, so the host's
authority and its trust fence are unaffected: no `--trusted-host`, no rewritten
`Host`, no new listening port on this machine.

```
plugins/mobile-link/
├── package.json          # type: module, dsh.bundle.patch, bin: dsh-mobile-link
├── cordis.patch.yml      # bundle patch: the loader row + config reference
├── lib/
│   ├── index.js          # cordis plugin: starts the agent, registers 5 routes
│   ├── link.js           # the DLP agent transport: identity, socket, heartbeat, reconnect
│   ├── router.js         # frames ⇄ local DSH mux streams, per-device `$events`
│   ├── dlp.js            # DLP v1 frame codec (shared with the relay)
│   ├── files.js          # phone → computer file transfers (`_link/file*` methods)
│   ├── enroll.js         # open enrollment (no invite code), writes ~/.dsh/mobile-link/agent.json
│   ├── journal.js        # lifecycle journal: why a relay link was dropped, after the fact
│   ├── routes.js         # status, enroll, pair-code, pair-code/regenerate, devices/revoke
│   ├── qr.js             # dependency-free QR SVG
│   └── cli.js            # dsh-mobile-link: enroll / mint-pair-code
└── test/                 # node --test, 100+ tests (no DSH, no network)
```

## Install

The connector runs in whichever host runs your DSH. There are two supported hosts today —
**the official desktop app** and **the command-line web host** — and each keeps its own
profile, so you install the plugin into the one you actually use. The connector discovers
the local DSH by itself in both (the host hands it the authenticated loopback address);
you never type an address or a token.

**Command-line web host**

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-plugin-mobile-link
```

**Official desktop app** — install through the app's own plugin page, or with the CLI that
the app ships (`…/Resources/runtime/cli/bin/dsh`, installable from its settings). The npm
`dsh` refuses this profile on purpose (`profile "desktop" is managed exclusively by the
Electron application`). Two prerequisites matter in practice: let the app start once so it
initializes its profile, and **quit it completely** before installing — otherwise the
profile is locked.

```bash
# quoting the app's bundled CLI; see docs/ONBOARDING.md for the section titles
"<DeepSeek Harness.app>/Contents/Resources/runtime/cli/bin/dsh" \
  plugin --profile desktop add dsh-plugin-mobile-link
```

Then restart the host (or reload the profile). From a checkout the same command takes
a path — the leading `./` matters, because DSH anchors a relative spec against
your current directory instead of resolving it inside the profile:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add ./plugins/mobile-link
```

## Use

1. Register this computer with a relay (once). Open the **移动端连接** panel at the
   bottom of the DSH sidebar: the relay address is prefilled (editable) from the
   installation default; click **登记**. The connector derives the computer name
   automatically, writes `~/.dsh/mobile-link/agent.json` and reconnects in place —
   no terminal and no DSH restart. Open enrollment is the default; the relay
   rate-limits by source. If an installation has no panel (headless, CI), the CLI
   still works:

   ```bash
   dsh-mobile-link enroll --relay wss://<你的站点>/dsh-link
   ```

   …or register it on the relay host with `dsh-relay admin agent-register
   --write-config ~/.dsh/mobile-link/agent.json`.

2. The same panel shows the pairing code and its QR once the relay link is up.
   The CLI can still mint one directly:

   ```bash
   dsh-mobile-link --mint-pair-code        # prints JSON: code + relay + agentId
   ```

   The code is persistent: it stays valid until you click 重新生成. Each paired device
   has a quiet 撤销 action; revoking one device leaves the code and other devices alone.

3. Scan it in the iOS app. The code can be claimed again for another phone, a reinstall
   or a new device; only 重新生成 revokes it (already-paired devices stay connected).
   After that the phone reconnects on its own — nothing else has to be run by hand.

`GET /mobile-link/status` reports whether the link is up, which devices are
attached, and whether this computer is registered yet. Its `enroll` block also
carries `panel` (this connector can enroll from the DSH panel), `relayPrefill`
and `relayLocked` (the address to prefill and whether it came from config).
`POST /mobile-link/enroll` performs that enrollment (open enrollment; no invite code); it returns the agent id and
name, never `agentSecret`, and is behind the same DSH request fence as pairing. `GET /mobile-link/devices` lists the full paired roster (including offline) for the panel, and
`POST /mobile-link/devices/revoke` revokes one paired device by `deviceId` through the relay; both are behind
the fence and authenticated with the agent secret. Its `journal` block carries
the current process's newest lifecycle events (link opened/closed with the reason,
device attached/detached); the counters in it reset when the plugin hot-reloads, so
the full history — across restarts — is the JSONL file at `journal.path`.

## Configuration

All optional; the defaults are what a stock deployment needs. Set them in the
plugin's config block (`cordis.patch.yml`), not by editing this file.

| Key | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | `true` | `false` stops the outbound link without uninstalling |
| `relayUrl` | from `agent.json` | Relay base URL; a bare deployment dials `<relay>/link/agent`. Pinning a real value here outranks the enrolled identity and makes the panel field read-only |
| `defaultRelayUrl` | empty | Form-only default: prefills the panel's relay input, but never outranks the enrolled identity. Official installs set this so users can still edit it |
| `agentId` / `agentSecret` | from `agent.json` | Override the enrolled identity |
| `stateFile` | `~/.dsh/mobile-link/agent.json` | Where the identity lives |
| `journalFile` | `~/.dsh/mobile-link/link-events.jsonl` | Lifecycle journal (rotated once at 256 KiB); `false` keeps it in memory only |
| `slowRequestMs` | `2000` | A slower single request gets its own `request.slow` entry; `0` disables those (per-attach `device.summary` is still written) |
| `diagnostics` | `true` | `false` refuses the phone's phase uploads; the phone ignores the refusal and stays connected |
| `dshUrl` | discovery | Explicit local DSH base URL (usually unnecessary — the host hands the connector its own address) |
| `heartbeatMs` | `20000` | DLP ping interval |

The connector does **not** read an endpoint handoff file any more: discovery happens inside
the host process (`ctx.inject(['webServer','connection'])`), which is what makes one npm
package work on both the desktop app and the command-line host. It **writes** one instead —
`$DSH_HOME/mobile-link/endpoint.json`, mode 0600 — for tools that run *outside* the host
(our dev/test scripts and the iOS integration helpers).

Address resolution order: this config block, then `DSH_RELAY_URL` (or
`DSH_MOBILE_LINK_RELAY`), then the enrolled identity file, then the repository
placeholder `wss://relay.example.com/dsh-link` — the placeholder being the
"nothing configured yet" sentinel rather than a real address.

## Design notes

- **No required services.** `inject` is empty and the routes are attached through
  `ctx.inject([...])`, so a future DSH that renames or drops `webServer` /
  `connection` cannot make the tunnel fatal on boot.
- **Protocol-transparent.** Nothing outside `lib/` is imported and no DSH
  business API is touched: the connector forwards frames, it does not interpret
  sessions. The relay has the same property.
- **Disable** by removing the row from the profile's `cordis.patch.yml`, or by
  setting `enabled: false`.

## Test

```bash
cd plugins/mobile-link && npm test    # zero dependencies
```

The wire protocol is specified in
[`docs/RELAY-PROTOCOL.md`](https://github.com/jayantTang/DSH_Mobile/blob/main/docs/RELAY-PROTOCOL.md).

# dsh-plugin-send-image

> 面向：使用者 · 状态：stable · 最近核对：2026-09-20

**Lets the agent put a picture into the conversation.** A screenshot, the
clipboard, or a file — the host normalizes and persists the bytes, every DSH
client renders it inline, and the user can open it full screen.

Why a plugin is needed at all: DSH's model adapters declare **text-only output**,
so the agent cannot emit an image in its answer. The bytes reach the client
through the Host's attachment service (`ctx.attachments.saveImage`, which
normalizes and persists them) and the returned reference rides on this tool's
**result**, as an image content block — so every client draws the picture inside
the agent's own turn.

Submitting it as a prompt instead — which is what this plugin used to do — is
wrong twice over: a prompt is a **user message**, so the picture looked like
something the user had sent, and it **started a turn**, so the agent answered its
own screenshot. `send-image.mjs --via-prompt` keeps that path for a client that
cannot render tool-result images; nothing here uses it.

```
plugins/send-image/
├── package.json          # type: module, dsh.bundle.patch
├── cordis.patch.yml      # bundle patch: the loader row
├── lib/index.js          # cordis plugin: registers the send_image tool
└── test/                 # node --test, 19 tests (no DSH, no network)
```

The tool is a thin shell around
[`skills/send-image/send-image.mjs`](https://github.com/jayantTang/DSH_Mobile/blob/main/skills/send-image/send-image.mjs),
which owns the capture quirks (`screencapture`, `pngpaste`, the screen-recording
permission message) and prints one JSON descriptor. Standalone it only
*prepares* — the publishing half needs the Host context this plugin has:

```bash
node skills/send-image/send-image.mjs --screenshot        # prints the descriptor
node skills/send-image/send-image.mjs --file ./out/render.png
node skills/send-image/send-image.mjs --clipboard         # needs pngpaste
```

## Install

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-plugin-send-image
```

Then restart DSH (or reload the profile). From a checkout a relative spec works
too — the leading `./` matters, because DSH anchors it against your current
directory instead of resolving it inside the profile:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add ./plugins/send-image
```

## Use

The agent calls `send_image`. Exactly one source per call:

| Argument | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `file` | Path to an image (absolute, or relative to the working directory) |
| `screenshot` | `true` captures the whole screen — the picture contains everything on it |
| `clipboard` | `true` sends the image on the clipboard (needs `pngpaste`) |
| `caption` | Text shown with the picture |

Passing none or several is a readable tool error rather than a schema failure:
source exclusivity is a runtime rule here, so the model is told what to fix.

### You can also take the screenshot yourself

Inside the DSH window, `⌥⌘S` (or the button at the left of the composer) starts a drag-select; the
selected rectangle is **attached to the current conversation as a draft** — you decide whether to send
it. The shortcut only works while the DSH window has focus (no system-wide hotkey), and it can be
rebound under Settings → Shortcuts. `Esc` cancels without leaving a file, and a missing Screen
Recording grant prints where to enable it and which program to restart.

Both supported hosts (the official desktop app and the command-line web host) run the same client
half, shipped in this package. The plugin is hot-pluggable: enabling or disabling it adds or removes
the shortcut, the composer button and its styles in place — no host restart, no page reload.

## Test

```bash
cd plugins/send-image && npm test    # 14 tests, zero dependencies
```

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# davinci-console（0.11.0 · DEMO）

![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/davinci-console-demo?label=npm)
![demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-DEMO-orange)

仓库：<https://github.com/JiangXingchen4210/Davinci_MCP_DSH_Demo>

DaVinci Resolve 的调色 / 剪辑控制台，作为 DSH Web 插件运行：在浏览器面板里完成「素材 → 还原 → 调色/风格 → 交付」的完整流程，所有动作通过 **Resolve MCP** 驱动本机 DaVinci Resolve Studio。

> ⚠️ 这是 **Demo 版（0.11.0）**：核心链路已可用，擦除（erase）等实验功能明确标记 DEMO/禁用；请在真实交付前自行复核画面。

## 功能

- **工程预检**：项目设置、色彩科学、离线素材一次性体检；缺素材会拦住风格与渲染
- **灰片还原**：先判断是否 LOG（画面统计）→ 读元数据识别机型/曲线 → 在 DaVinci 自带/官方库按曲线匹配；库里没有时给厂商官方页面，可粘贴直链自动下载安装（如 OPPO O-Log 已验证），或上传 `.cube`
- **三层 15 节点调色图**：每节点一个工具（还原/白平衡/曝光/对比/曲线/色相/饱和/分离色调/肤色键/背景键/风格 LUT/质感），`grade.nodeReport` 逐节点说明作用
- **风格库（10 个，带出处）**：青橙、漂白旁路、矩阵绿、银翼杀手 2049、夜魔侠暗黑、韦斯·安德森粉彩、月光蓝、疯狂麦克斯·铬版、教父琥珀、柯达 2383；一键应用，配方逐组写入并读回校验
- **质感**：黑柔/白柔（Fusion Glow）、颗粒意图、可选胶片模拟 LUT
- **局部**：抠像、面部跟踪、遮罩校验、透视跟踪、擦除（DEMO）
- **交付**：先选长宽/帧率/码率生成方案，**用户确认后才渲染**
- **调试日志**：面板内逐条中文显示「阶段 / 节点 / 工具 / 目的 / 参数」

## 环境要求

| 依赖 | 说明 |
|---|---|
| macOS | 当前仅支持 macOS（`osascript`/`sips`/预编译助手） |
| DaVinci Resolve Studio | 建议 21.2；需可被 Resolve MCP 连接 |
| Resolve MCP | 工具名 `resolve_*`（DSH 中启用对应 MCP 插件） |
| ffmpeg / ffprobe | `brew install ffmpeg`，用于分析/抽帧/导出 |

面板启动时会自动检测以上依赖，缺什么会在顶部提示。

## 安装

```bash
# DSH 市场/包安装
npm install davinci-console-demo@0.11.0
# 或在 DSH 的插件管理中按包名安装后启用
```

## 使用（三步）

1. **素材交接**：粘贴素材路径或选择文件，导入后自动体检色彩管线
2. **还原**：点「判断/匹配还原 LUT」；灰片才需还原，库里有同曲线多条时由你选；缺 LUT 按官方链接下载/上传
3. **调色/风格 → 交付**：在标签页调色或点「一键风格」，再到「交付」选参数并确认渲染

详细说明见 [USER_MANUAL.md](./USER_MANUAL.md)。

## 版本

- 0.11.0（Demo）：还原决策链路、15 节点图、风格库、交付审批、调试日志、依赖自检、内置 LUT 支持库（清单随包，LUT 本体因授权不随包发布）

## License

MIT


## 反馈 / 报错

- 面板底部「调试日志 → **反馈/报错**」：自动把环境（MCP/ffmpeg/Resolve 路径）、最近日志打包进预填 Issue，并保存一份到插件 data 目录；
- 也可以直接开 [Issue](https://github.com/JiangXingchen4210/Davinci_MCP_DSH_Demo/issues/new/choose)，附版本号与日志；
- 支持邮箱：2504836725@qq.com

## Star / 使用反馈

如果这个 DEMO 对你有用，欢迎 Star 仓库；遇到问题请提 Issue（附日志），我会按报错优先级修复并记录在 CHANGELOG。

# @local/dsh-lazy-plugins

按需加载市场插件的 Host 插件（v3.14.4）。本地没有的插件，在任务需要时由 agent 从市场索引解析、安装、**当场可用**；用完可以卸载移除。
默认激活方式为 `proxy`：插件真正生效，但它的工具**不进模型可见的 tools[]**，因此不会打碎提示词前缀缓存。

## Claude 式形态（v3.14）

常驻只注入一句（152 字符 / ≈38 tokens），细节在注册的 **skill** 正文里，模型需要时才加载：

- `skills/lazy-plugins/SKILL.md`：frontmatter（name/description/whenToUse）+ 正文（何时用、三个动作、判定规则、示例、注意）；
- 插件 apply 时读文件并 `ctx.get("skills").register({ name, description, whenToUse, content, invocation, provider, source: "runtime" })`；
- 实测：工具描述 **936 → 152 字符（234 → 38 tokens）**，skill 出现在模型技能目录并能按需加载（`advise.skill = ["lazy-plugins:runtime"]`）。

## 工具（模型可见面）

只有一个工具 `lazy_plugin`：

| 动作 | 含义 |
|---|---|
| `ensure` | **给一句需求**，自动挑出最匹配的插件并在判定明确时直接安装（默认走 proxy） |
| `suggest` | 任务句 → 候选排序（IDF 加权，可翻页） |
| `search` | 关键词检索（可翻页，去重 + 隐藏装不上的条目） |
| `resolve` | 看一个包的版本、安装目标（npm / git）、兼容性 |
| `load` | 安装指定版本并激活（已装则只做启用） |
| `reload` | 停用→启用，让新版本模块生效（不重启 dsh） |
| `unload` | 停用但保留安装 |
| `release` | 停用并移除 |
| `uninstall` | 直接移除 |
| `list` | 已装清单、懒加载记录、常驻判定与使用分、索引缓存状态 |
| `refresh` | 立刻刷新索引（条件请求）并预热常驻插件 |
| `advise` | 体检：工具面 tokens、缓存命中率、使用分、隐藏工具、建议 |
| `invoke` | 调用被 proxy 隐藏的工具（`{tool, arguments}`） |

## 模型调用准则

1. **有需求先 `ensure`**：一句话描述要做什么，它负责挑；判定不明确时才回候选让人选。
2. 想自己挑就用 `suggest` / `search`，按「描述最匹配」优先，其次热度；可 `offset` 翻页。
3. **优先最新版本**：不传 `version` 就是索引默认（最新）版本。
4. **一次装一个**，用完 `release`，不要囤。
5. `load` 回 `installable:false` 说明该条目任何 registry 都装不上（索引里有这类幽灵条目），换候选，别重试同一个。
6. 没有 `force` 参数：base bundle 一律拒绝停用/移除，常用插件只提示不阻断。

## 激活方式与提示词缓存

工具是 API 独立字段 `tools[]`、按名字排序，缓存断点在最后一个工具，所以**可见工具集一变，前缀就重建**。

| `activate` | 当场能用 | 前缀缓存 | 做法 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `proxy`（默认） | ✅ | ✅ 不变 | 插件激活，工具被 **per-agent `tools.restrict`** 藏起来，经 `invoke` 调用 |
| `now` | ✅ | ❌ 重建一次 | 工具原生进入 `tools[]` |
| `session` | ❌ | ✅ | 只安装，之后 `load` 一次启用（无下载，约 0.1–0.5 s） |

`invoke` 之所以能调用隐藏工具：`tools.execute()` 在 host 作用域执行，而 `restrict` 只作用于 agent 作用域（实测：`visibleForAgent: false` / `visibleGlobally: true` / `executeWithoutAgent: ok`）。
屏蔽落盘在 `hidden.json`，启动时重新打上；插件卸载后失效名字会自动剔除；插件异步注册的工具由 1.2 s / 3.5 s / 7 s 三次补扫兜住。

## 检索与自动选取

- **候选池**：`limit × 3`，先按相关性排序，再 `enrich`、过滤不可装、按安装目标合并近重复（`dsh-voice-7` / `dsh-voice-13` → `dsh-voice`，带 `variants`）。
- **IDF 加权**：`idf = ln(1 + N/(1+df))`，命中按 `idf × 字段权重`（name 3 / title 2 / description 2）累加，`dsh`/`plugin` 这类全库词不再决定排序。
- **自动选取守卫**：`ensure` 只在 `top ≥ autoSelectScore(40)` **且** `top ≥ 第二名 × autoSelectMargin(1.5)` 时才装，否则回 `needs-choice` + 候选；`auto:false` 只报告不装。
- **阈值是实测校准出来的**（31 条真实需求语料）：`40/1.3` 的自动安装精度只有 **0.636**（11 次装错 4 次），`40/1.5` 提升到 **0.80**（recall 0.367→0.167）；没有参数组合能到 0.90，所以默认偏保守，模型多看候选是更便宜的错误。
- **git-pinned 条目**（当前占 52.5%）判为可装、不走 npm 探测；`source` 字段直接回 `npm` / `git`。

## 常驻（resident）怎么算

三路来源（社区做法见 CREDITS.md）：

| 来源 | 判定 | 效果 |
|---|---|---|
| `base` | `availability !== 'profile'` 且**当前启用**的 bundle | 硬拒绝 `unload/release/uninstall` |
| `explicit` | `config.resident` | 只加提示，不阻断 |
| `auto` | `score >= residentScore(3)` | 只加提示，不阻断 |

```
score = 1.0·Σ_loads + 0.3·Σ_manualEnables + (base ? 1000 : 0)   每项 × 0.5^(Δ/14天)
```

只写本机 `~/.dsh/cache/dsh-lazy-plugins/usage.json`，不联网、不上报。

## 索引与缓存

- **拉取**：单次尝试只等首字节 3 s，失败转镜像；源顺序 = profile 索引 → `indexMirrors`。
- **缓存优先**：磁盘副本直接返回，后台条件请求热更新（304 = 0 字节）；断网时旧副本仍可用。
- **描述表**：索引自身描述覆盖率 ≥80% 时**直接投影**（零额外请求）；否则按 `descriptionSources` 拉 sidecar/旧文档。
- **刷新触发**：启动一次、**打开插件面板一次**（client 半调用 `GET /lazy-plugins/refresh?src=panel`，60 s 节流）、每天保底一次、手动 `refresh`。
- **client 半**：`client.js` + `package.json` 的 `dsh.client{platform:web,immediately:true}` + `exports['./client']`，用 `window.__ModuleLoader__.load({id, factory})` 形态（无需构建）。页面挂载即调 `GET /lazy-plugins/refresh?src=mount`，点进插件面板再调 `?src=panel`，页面侧 60 s 节流 + `sessionStorage`，失败只 `console.debug`。
- **自愈（重要，给后续维护者）**：`link:` 安装的包在**主机进程启动早于 `dsh.client` 声明**时，会被上游 `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-modules` 的 `ClientModuleRegistry.pkgMeta` 缓存成 `null`（该缓存**没有任何失效路径**，`set_bundle false/true` 命中缓存、不够）。本插件在**启动后 `bootDelayMs` 自动一次**、以及显式 `POST /lazy-plugins/repair-client`（或 `GET /lazy-plugins/state?repair=1`）时自愈：删掉陈旧 `null` → 强制 `reconcile` 报变更 → `flush()`（内部 `compose()` + 通知）→ 图里出现本行。`GET /lazy-plugins/state` 本身**纯读、无副作用**。
- **自愈返回值**：`repair.attempted:false` + `why:"already in graph"` 是**幂等 no-op（已在图中，不是失败）**；真正的失败看 `repair.errors` 或 `repair.compose.error/failures`。
- **自愈的退出条件（必须遵守）**：这是**上游缺陷的 workaround**，不是本插件的功能。一旦 `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-modules` 让 `pkgMeta` 的 key 带上 `package.json` 的 mtime/size、或暴露 `invalidate()`、或 `flush()` 前对 dirty 行强制重解析 —— 就**整段删除** `ensureClientRow` 及其三个触发点（启动定时器、`POST /lazy-plugins/repair-client`、`GET /state?repair=1`），此 README 对应段落一并删除。依据与建议修法见 `_tmp/panel-trigger/UPSTREAM-ISSUE.md`；`clientHalf.lastRepair.upstream` 字段也带同一句提示。
- **验证计数**：`state.panelPings`（过闸执行的刷新数）、`clientRequests`（含被节流的客户端调用）、`browserPings`（带 `Sec-Fetch-Mode`+浏览器 UA 的调用，`curl` 伪造不了）+ `lastBrowserPingFingerprint`、`lastBrowserPingSource`（`mount`/`panel`），以及 `clientHalf{inGraph,rows,graphRev,url,clientPath,lastRepair}`。
- 索引现状（2026-11-07 实测）：10,559 条、99.96% 带 zh 描述、52.5% git-pinned、166 个后缀名条目。

## 装前探测与别名

- npm 条目：并行 HEAD `<registry>/<name>/<version>`（命中 26–230 ms）；全 404 直接回 `installable:false`；超时/网络错判为未知，不挡安装。
- 别名：索引把重名条目改名成 `dsh-voice-8`，真实包名在 `title`。`load` 用 `title` 作第二候选，探测通过就装真名并回 `installedAs`。

## 可配置项

`cordis.patch.yml`（全部有默认值）：`defaultActivate`、`autoSelectScore`、`autoSelectMargin`、`autoSelectEnabled`、`resident`、`halfLifeDays`、`residentScore`、`fetchTimeoutMs`、`bodyTimeoutMs`、`refreshIntervalMs`、`dailyRefreshMs`、`panelThrottleMs`、`bootDelayMs`、`indexMirrors`、`descriptionSources`、`descriptionTtlMs`、`descriptionSearch`、`enrichDescriptions`、`enrichTimeoutMs`、`enrichRegistries`、`verifyInstall`、`probeFastMs`、`probeTimeoutMs`、`deferLoading`、`diskCache`、`cacheTtlMs`。

## 性能（本机实测）

| 场景 | 耗时 |
|---|---|
| 已装再 `load`（快路径） | 75–490 ms |
| 冷装小包（含探测+安装+激活） | 1.9–2.6 s |
| 冷装大包 / registry 抖动 | 3–5 s（个别 38 s，属上游 installBundle 抖动） |
| git-pinned 安装（`@lbxc/dsh-voice-input`） | 5.07 s |
| 索引冷拉 | ~1.0–1.7 s（gzip 约 300 KB–1 MB，随版本变化） |
| 索引 304 热更新 | 0.5–1.1 s / 0 字节 |
| 索引磁盘命中（新进程） | 42 ms |
| `search` / `suggest`（本地 10,559 条，含 IDF 扫描） | 10–30 ms |

`load` 结果带 `phases`（lookup/resolve/probe/install）与 `ms`；`advise.cache` 有命中率计数。

## 失败恢复

`reload` 是「先停用再启用」，启用失败会停在停用态 → 现在失败自动重试一次并回传 `diagnostic` + 修复提示（最常见成因：`cordis.patch.yml` 里 `@scope` 未加引号）。

## 数据边界

只做三件事：读市场索引、调 profile 的 `pluginManager`、返回结果。不写日志文件、不上报、不采集会话内容。

## 出处

见 `CREDITS.md`。

# dsh-market · DSH 插件市场索引（自动爬取）

为 DeepSeek Harness（DSH）的「插件 → 发现」提供一份**自动生成、格式合规**的索引源。

- 主源（GitHub Pages，实测最稳）：`https://jingjiangze.github.io/dsh-market/index.json`
- 品牌域名（Cloudflare Pages）：`https://dsh.jiangjiangze.icu/index.json`
- 两个地址内容同源：都来自本仓库 `site/`，由 CI 生成后提交

## 加进 DSH

「插件 → 发现 → 添加索引源」，两个都加（互为主备）：

```
https://jingjiangze.github.io/dsh-market/index.json
https://dsh.jiangjiangze.icu/index.json
```

> 为什么主源选 GitHub Pages：2026-11-02 本机直连实测 **3/3 成功，0.61–0.81 s**；同一份索引走 Cloudflare Pages 自定义域名时 **3 次里 1 次卡在 25 s 只收到 538 B**、其余 3.8–17.5 s（CF 边缘境内无节点，直连不稳；走代理 2/2 成功 1.9–2.9 s）。DSH 的 fetch 超时是 15 s，所以把 Pages 当人读站点、把 GitHub Pages 当机器源，两边都不丢。

## 它是什么 / 不是什么

- 是：从 **npm 公共源**爬到的、**声明了 `dsh.bundle.patch`** 且 `engines.dsh` 满足当前运行时的包的元数据清单（分类、多语言描述、图标直链、精确版本）。
- 不是：不是代码托管，不镜像任何包，不对任何插件背书。装什么、跑什么，以包本身为准。
- 索引里**只有元数据**：`source.type = npm`，安装走你本机 pnpm + 你自己的 registry 配置。

## 爬取与准入（`crawler/crawl.mjs`，零依赖）

```
node crawler/crawl.mjs --selftest     # 门禁自测（正例 + 反例）
node crawler/crawl.mjs                # 爬取并生成 dist/
```

两段式，先便宜后贵：

1. **发现**：`registry.npmjs.org` 关键词检索（`keywords:dsh-plugin`、`keywords:deepseek-harness`、`keywords:dsh`）。
2. **初筛**（每包 1 次 `/<name>/latest`）：必须声明 `dsh.bundle.patch`；不得含 `preinstall`/`install`/`postinstall`。
3. **定版**（入选包再取完整 packument）：取**最新稳定版**且满足 `engines.dsh`；未声明 `engines.dsh` 的一律**不收**（不猜"应该能跑"）；发布不足 `MIN_AGE_DAYS`（默认 3 天）的不收（pnpm 的 `minimumReleaseAge` 会扣住它们，写进索引用户也装不上）；许可为空或 `NOASSERTION`/`UNLICENSED` 的不收。

产出：

| 文件 | 内容 |
|---|---|
| `dist/index.json` | format 1 索引（DSH 唯一读的东西） |
| `dist/index.sidecar.json` | format 1 装不下的东西：`dist.integrity`、provenance、体积、生效的门禁 |
| `dist/rejections.json` | 每个被排除的包 + 原因（可复盘，不静默丢） |
| `dist/stats.json` | 候选数 / 初筛数 / 收录数 / 拒绝原因分布 / 索引字节数 / 耗时 |

环境变量：`NPM_REGISTRY`、`SEARCH_REGISTRY`、`DSH_RUNTIME_VERSION`、`MIN_AGE_DAYS`、`MAX_PLUGINS`、`MAX_CANDIDATES`、`CONCURRENCY`、`SEARCH_QUERIES`。

### 已知的爬取坑（踩过）

- **npmmirror 不支持 `keywords:` 语法**：`registry.npmmirror.com/-/v1/search?text=keywords:dsh-plugin` 返回 `total=0`，而 npmjs 返回约 11.9k。所以**发现阶段固定用 npmjs**；manifest 阶段可换镜像加速。
- **不能信 latest**：一个包可能同时有多个兼容版本，`latest` 未必兼容当前运行时，所以定版要读完整 packument。
- **未声明 `engines.dsh` ≠ 兼容**：DSH 的安装侧会用真实包的 `engines` + `peerDependencies` 再判一次，索引里谎报兼容比不收更伤口碑。

## 站点（`site/`）

- 首页第一屏是**索引源卡片**（渐变描边 + 外发光，纯 CSS）：「由 DSH 制作」徽章、**全部 / 国内 / 国际**三个索引源切换、源地址 + 一键复制。
- `index.html` 690 B；`style.css` / `app.js` 为**同源**资源（Pages 直接提供，部署即生效）。第三方图标仍走 jsDelivr 的 npm 直链（npm 版本不可变，不存在缓存问题）。
- 页脚：交流 QQ 1689170897。
- **多语言**：右上角切换 中文 / English / 日本語 / 한국어 / Русский；ja/ko/ru 由 CI 里的 Google Translate 生成（`crawler/translate.mjs`，按内容哈希缓存，失败即跳过不发布）。
- 卡片**点击打开详情**：中英对照 + 类别/版本/作者/发布/来源/包名 + 安装命令一键复制；卡片本身不再放「主页」按钮（链接在详情里）。

## 索引源：一个链接就够了

| 索引源 | 内容 | 国内实测 |
|---|---|---|
| **`index.zh.json`** | 全部 1 万余条，中英双语（推荐加这一个） | 4.3 MB，**gzip 后 1.08 MB / 1.8 秒** |
| `index.<lang>.json` | en / ja / ko / ru，同一份目录的其它语言 | 各 4.3–4.8 MB |
| `index.json` | 五语合并文档（站点与工具用，最大） | 11.6 MB，gzip 2.2 MB / 24 秒 |

**关键事实（实测）**：GitHub Pages 对 JSON 走 `Content-Encoding: gzip`，所以 4.3 MB 的文件实际只传 1.08 MB。用不带 `Accept-Encoding` 的 `curl` 测会得到「40–88 秒」的假象。

不建议、也不需要的做法（都验证过不可用）：
- ModelScope 数据集 URL：`/resolve/` 与 API 都 **302 → cdn-lfs-cn-1**，DSH 的加载器拒绝重定向；
- 品牌域 `dsh.jiangjiangze.icu`：国内被限速到约 4 KB/s；
- jsDelivr 镜像：该路径返回 **403**；
- 分片（多链接）：能满足速度，但配置要写 6 条，已撤掉；
- Cloudflare Worker：明确不使用。

## 双语与分类

- 每个插件都有 `{en, zh}` 标题与简介，并被归到一个声明过的类别（9 类：safety / ui / media / integrations / memory / models / automation / devtools / other）。
- 中文来源优先级：**包自带 `locale/zh.json`** → **本仓库 `data/zh-overrides.json`**（可按 `version` 钉版）→ 兜底英文并标 `zh-fallback`（当前 0）。当前 38/38 双语：`zh-native` 13 + `zh-override` 25。
- 标签写明来源（`zh-native` / `zh-override` / `zh-fallback`），数量统计进 `dist/stats.json`。
- 分类规则在 `crawler/crawl.mjs` 的 `CATEGORY_RULES`，**必须带词边界**——裸子串会把 `inspired` 命中 `ide`、把主题插件误判成开发工具。
- 不编造翻译：没有机器翻译，全部来自作者 locale 或仓库内人工整理。
- **不在本机跑任何服务**：爬取、校验、发布都在 GitHub Actions；本地 `node crawler/crawl.mjs --dry-run` 只是一次性脚本。

## CI（三段流水线）

| 工作流 | 触发 | 做什么 |
|---|---|---|
| `crawl.yml` | 每 3 小时 + 手动 | 三分片采集 → 合并目录 → 生成多语言/浏览分片/资源 → **离线 + 在线发布门禁** → Git Data API 提交 `main` → 显式触发 `deploy` |
| `ci.yml` | 每次 push / 每个 PR | 门禁自测 → 官方 `@deepseek-ai/dsh-plugin-market-index` 校验 → 页面预算与引用检查 → registry 回查 → `--dry-run` 冒烟（守住 main 与人工 PR） |
| `deploy.yml` | main 的 `site/**`、`dist/**` 变化，或由 crawl 派发 | 双端发布：GitHub Pages + Cloudflare Pages（`wrangler`） |
| `dependabot.yml` | 每周 | GitHub Actions 版本升级 PR（人工审） |

**发布纪律**：`crawl` 和 `translate` 共用 `catalog-publish` 并发组，避免两个写入者同时基于旧 `main` 创建提交；完整发布门禁在写入 `main` 前执行，push 触发的 `ci` 作为发布后回归检查。

**两个必须知道的 GitHub 行为**（都已在代码里绕过）：

1. **用仓库 `GITHUB_TOKEN` 写入 `main` 不会触发其它 workflow**（防递归）→ 所以 `crawl` 提交后显式 `gh workflow run deploy.yml`，不指望 push 事件。
2. 当前 `crawl` 走 Git Data API 直接写 `main`，不再创建 crawl PR；因此发布门禁必须在写入前执行，不能依赖 push 后才运行的 `ci` 来阻止错误版本上线。


`ci` 里的检查（`crawler/validate.mjs`）：

1. `parseMarketIndex()` —— 与 DSH 运行时同一份校验器，不是自己重写；
2. `site/index.json` 必须与 `dist/index.json` **逐字节一致**（防止发布物与验证物脱节）；
3. `site/index.html` < 1024 B，`style.css` 存在；
4. 页面里不允许出现 `127.0.0.1` / `localhost` / `file://` / 内联图片字体；
5. 每条 plugin 的 `name@version` 在 registry 上真实存在、仍声明 `dsh.bundle.patch`，且 `engines.dsh` 与索引里写的一致（防止**索引漂移**——DSH 安装侧会用真实包再判一次兼容性）。

本地复现（不需要网络可加 `--offline`）：

```bash
npm i --no-save @deepseek-ai/dsh-plugin-market-index@0.2.1-rc.5
node crawler/crawl.mjs --selftest
node crawler/validate.mjs
node crawler/crawl.mjs --dry-run
```


## 已知限制

- **索引没有签名**：format 1 里没有 signature / digest 字段，DSH 不验签。篡改只能靠外部核对 `dist/index.json` 的 sha256（见每次提交与 `stats.json`）。
- **没有 upgrade 流程**：DSH 侧「有新版」只显示 `update-available`，升级 = 卸载 + 重装。
- **索引是单文档全量读**：超过 ~5k 条要考虑拆多源（官方口径：20k 条 ≈ 7.6 MiB，反序列化约 35 ms）。
- **只覆盖 npm**：不发布到 npm 的插件（只在 GitHub 的）暂不收录；后续可加 `source.type=git` + commit 固定。
- **不做安全审计**：门禁只保证「是个能装的 bundle、版本兼容、许可清楚、不跑安装脚本」，不代表代码安全。

## 许可

本仓库的爬虫与站点代码以 **GPL-3.0-or-later** 授权，全文见根目录 [`LICENSE`](LICENSE)。

索引里的条目版权归各包作者：本仓库只写元数据，不分发任何包的代码或素材，插件图标一律从上**游地址外链加载而不打包**。第三方数据与素材的边界见 [`NOTICE`](NOTICE)。
