# dsh-llm-resilience

**English** | [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md)

**Make a flaky LLM gateway behave like a reliable one — per-target retries, streaming-safe fallback chains and persistent circuit breaking for DeepSeek Harness.**

This plugin was built from a concrete failure mode we hit in daily use. **OpenDesign Go**'s
tool-call stream and API connections were intermittently unstable: a malformed tool-call
stream, a transport drop, or a membership/quota error surfaced as a generic 500 could end
an entire agent step. DSH's built-in `retryPolicy` is provider-level — it can back off on
the same route, but it cannot switch provider/model, and it has no circuit breaker. In our
deployment this plugin moved OpenDesign Go from **barely usable** to **reliably usable**:
safe retries absorb transient faults, a second provider takes over when the gateway is out
of quota or broken, and a persistent breaker stops hammering a dead upstream.

> This is an independent plugin. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by OpenDesign or
> DeepSeek; OpenDesign Go is mentioned only as the deployment that motivated the design.
> The failure pattern is not unique to that service — any gateway that intermittently
> breaks tool-call streams or returns quota errors as generic 500s benefits from the same
> chain.

- [Why this exists](#why-this-exists)
- [What makes it different](#what-makes-it-different)
- [What it registers](#what-it-registers)
- [Install](#install)
- [Configuration](#configuration)
- [Error classification](#error-classification)
- [Streaming, tool calls and step replay](#streaming-tool-calls-and-step-replay)
- [Circuit breaker](#circuit-breaker)
- [Settings page](#settings-page)
- [Limits and honest non-goals](#limits-and-honest-non-goals)
- [Tests](#tests)
- [Compatibility and migration](#compatibility-and-migration)

## Why this exists

DSH's `retryPolicy` already retries at the provider level, but:

- the backoff multiplier is fixed at 2 — you cannot ask for 1.5;
- `agent/request-error` can only retry the **same route**; it cannot switch provider/model;
- there is no circuit breaker: when a provider is down, every step still hits it first;
- `MALFORMED_RESPONSE` (a broken tool-call stream) and a failed tool **execution** need
  different treatment.

This plugin registers a synthetic provider route (default `fallback`, model `auto`) that
internally walks a chain of real provider/model targets:

```
fallback/auto
  ├─ target 0: primary-gateway/your-model       independent retry budget + breaker
  ├─ target 1: backup-provider/your-model       independent retry budget + breaker
  └─ target 2: local/your-model                 independent retry budget + breaker
```

Every target has its own retry budget, backoff curve and breaker. Switching to the next
target resets the backoff instead of inheriting the previous target's already-doubled delay.

## What makes it different

- **Per-target retry budgets.** `maxRetries`, `initialDelayMs`, `multiplier` (including 1.5),
  `maxDelayMs` and `jitterRatio` are independent for each target.
- **Error-aware classification.** Membership/entitlement/quota errors surfaced as `SERVER`
  500 fall back immediately; ordinary 500/timeout/transport errors retry; invalid requests
  fail without trying another target. `codeActions` lets you override the defaults.
- **Streaming-safe tool calls.** Text and reasoning deltas are forwarded immediately.
  Tool-call block-start/delta chunks are buffered until `block-end`, so a malformed tool-call
  stream (no `block-end`) can be retried without the host ever seeing duplicate output.
- **Step-replay continuation.** After content has been delivered, a failure cannot switch
  targets inside the same request. The plugin remembers `sessionId + request fingerprint`;
  when the host replays the step it starts at the next target, and the plan **rotates** to
  cover the whole chain instead of truncating it. If the failure was the chain tail, it is
  retried in place — a retryable failure is never rewritten into a terminal
  `FALLBACK_EXHAUSTED`.
- **Persistent circuit breaker, per provider + model.** Consecutive failures lock a target
  for a configurable window; the lock expires into a half-open probe (foreground or
  background). State is written atomically to `stateFile` and merged across processes with
  a lock + tombstones, so a restart does not forget a partially accumulated failure count.
- **Global budget.** `limits.maxTotalMs` (default 10 minutes) and `limits.maxAttempts`
  (default 50) are enforced across targets and retries; backoff waits count toward the
  deadline. No combination of targets × retries can hang a step for an unbounded time.
- **Request-level recovery codes pass through.** `IMAGE_OFFLOAD_REQUIRED` (with
  `offloadImages`) and `CONTEXT_WINDOW_EXCEEDED` are re-thrown unchanged so the host's image
  offload / compaction layers can recover first.
- **Settings page.** Edit the chain, reorder targets, see each retry schedule, and watch live
  breaker state (`closed / open / half-open / probing`) next to version and uninstall.
- **Tested.** 90 `node --test` cases plus isolated DSH end-to-end smoke runs with a fake
  OpenAI-compatible server (see [DESIGN.md](DESIGN.md)).

## What it registers

| entry | value |
|:--|:--|
| synthetic route | `fallback` (configurable) |
| synthetic model | `auto` |
| profile entry id | `llm-fallback` (kept stable for settings compatibility) |
| package name | `dsh-llm-resilience` |
| default state file | `$DSH_HOME/storages/llm-resilience/state.json` |

`targets: []` (or every target `enabled: false`) leaves the route registered but dormant:
you can build the chain in the settings page first, then enable it.

## Install

Requirements: DSH `0.2.2-rc.x`, Node.js 20+.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/T-splines/dsh-llm-resilience.git
cd dsh-llm-resilience
dsh plugin --profile web add "$PWD"
```

The package is a bundle (`dsh.bundle.patch`), so the `llm-fallback` entry is already mounted
by the bundle. **Override that entry** — do not `insert` a second one. In
`$DSH_HOME/profiles/<profile>/cordis.patch.yml`, replacing the whole `config`:

```yaml
- id: llm-fallback
  name: 'dsh-llm-resilience'
  config:
    enabled: true
    route: fallback
    targets:
      - enabled: true
        provider: primary-gateway
        model: your-model
        maxRetries: 5
        initialDelayMs: 1500
        multiplier: 2
        maxDelayMs: 20000
        jitterRatio: 0.3
      - enabled: true
        provider: backup-provider
        model: your-backup-model
        maxRetries: 3
        initialDelayMs: 1000
    breaker:
      failureThreshold: 5
      lockMs: 3600000
      probe:
        enabled: true
        background: false
        timeoutMs: 10000
        maxTokens: 1
        prompt: 'ping'
      stateFile: '$DSH_HOME/storages/llm-resilience/state.json'
    limits:
      maxTotalMs: 600000
      maxAttempts: 50
    toolCalls:
      retryMalformed: true
```

Replace `primary-gateway` / `backup-provider` with real provider ids from your DSH model
catalog (the settings page shows them as read-only dropdowns). A target whose provider does
not exist fails with `NO_ADAPTER` and the chain moves on; it does not silently pretend the
target served.

Then point the agent's default model at the synthetic route:

```yaml
- id: agent-default-model
  config:
    provider: fallback
    model: auto
```

Verify composition without starting an agent (`web` is the common profile name; use yours):

```bash
dsh --profile web --dump-config | grep -A8 'id: llm-fallback'
```

> When overriding an existing `llm-fallback` entry with `--patch`, write the **whole**
> `targets` array. DSH's config merge fills omitted array fields with an empty default, so
> overriding only `breaker` would clear the chain.

**Do not give entitlement/quota errors 10 retries.** They are deterministic provider state;
retrying the same target only wastes the budget. They should fall back on the first failure.

## Configuration

| field | meaning |
|:--|:--|
| `enabled` | master switch; the route still exists when disabled, but rejects requests |
| `route` | synthetic provider name (default `fallback`); must not appear in `targets` |
| `targets[]` | ordered `{ provider, model, enabled, label, maxRetries, initialDelayMs, multiplier, maxDelayMs, jitterRatio }` |
| `breaker` | `failureThreshold`, `lockMs`, probe settings (`enabled`, `background`, `timeoutMs`, `maxTokens`, `prompt`), `stateFile` |
| `limits` | `maxTotalMs`, `maxAttempts`; `0` disables that dimension |
| `toolCalls.retryMalformed` | retry a broken model-generated tool call (default `true`); tool **execution** retries are not supported |
| `codeActions` | override the default action per stable error code (`retry` / `fallback` / `fail`) |

## Error classification

| error | action | why |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `SERVER` + membership/entitlement/quota/billing/credit/plan | fallback | deterministic account state; retrying is useless |
| `SERVER` / `TIMEOUT` / `TRANSPORT` / `RATE_LIMIT` / `EMPTY_RESPONSE` / `STREAM_CLOSED` | retry | transient |
| `MALFORMED_RESPONSE` | retry | broken model output; safe to retry the whole LLM request |
| `AUTH` / `INVALID_CREDENTIAL` / `MISSING_CREDENTIAL` | fallback | another provider may work |
| `QUOTA` / `ACCOUNT_QUOTA` | fallback | switch provider/quota |
| `NO_ADAPTER` / `UNKNOWN_MODEL` / `MODEL_NOT_FOUND` | fallback | target unavailable |
| `ABORTED` / `CANCELLED` | fail | the caller cancelled |
| `UNSUPPORTED_OPTION` / `INVALID_REQUEST` / `UNSUPPORTED_CONTENT` | fail | the request itself is wrong; another target will not fix it |
| `IMAGE_OFFLOAD_REQUIRED` | fail (re-thrown) | host image-offload recovery must see it |
| `CONTEXT_WINDOW_EXCEEDED` | fail (re-thrown) | host compaction recovery must see it |
| unknown code | fallback | the last target still throws the original failure; nothing is swallowed |

`IMAGE_OFFLOAD_REQUIRED` and `CONTEXT_WINDOW_EXCEEDED` cannot be overridden: they are part
of DSH's request-level recovery protocol, and the host's listeners depend on the original
code and metadata.

## Streaming, tool calls and step replay

- Only switch targets **before** yielding anything visible to the caller.
- Text/reasoning deltas are forwarded immediately.
- Tool-call block-start/delta chunks are buffered until `block-end`; a malformed tool call
  (no `block-end`) can be dropped and retried safely.
- After visible content has been delivered, a failure is returned to the host so
  `dsh-llm-retry` can replay the whole step. The plugin records a fingerprint and the
  target it reached; on replay it starts at the next target. The plan **rotates** rather
  than truncating, so a target before the failure point is not lost. If the failure was the
  chain tail, it retries that target in place.
- The replay envelope written by the synthetic route is unwrapped into the real target's
  provider/model before the request reaches the upstream adapter, preserving signatures and
  ids. Envelopes written by the pre-rename `dsh-llm-fallback` package are still accepted.

## Circuit breaker

```
closed --(failureThreshold consecutive failures)--> open
open --(lock expires)--> half-open
half-open --(probe succeeds)--> closed on the next real success
half-open --(probe fails)--> open for another lock window
```

- State is keyed by `provider + model`, not by provider alone.
- `stateFile` is written atomically with a lock + read-merge-write. Concurrent processes
  keep the later/more-failed entry; a successful clear writes a tombstone so an older lock
  cannot be resurrected.
- Unreached failure counts are persisted too (`updatedAt` is the merge timeline), so a
  restart does not reset the count below the threshold.
- When every target is open/probing, the plugin throws `ALL_TARGETS_LOCKED` with each
  target's `lockedUntil` — it does not force one last request into a locked provider.

## Settings page

Plugins → Installed → `dsh-llm-resilience` → **Model fallback chain**:

- per-target rows: enabled, provider, model (read-only dropdowns from the session model
  catalog), label, retry parameters, move up/down, delete, add;
- retry-plan tooltip: one line per retry, with the jitter range when `jitter > 0`;
- breaker and budget fields;
- live runtime state polled from the host (`closed / open / half-open / probing`, remaining
  lock time, consecutive failures and lock count);
- non-loopback browsers get the host's memory-state view and the card says so instead of
  rendering plugin defaults as if they were the deployed policy.

## Limits and honest non-goals

- **Tool execution is not retried.** Cordis 4.1's `tools/execute` waterfall calls `next()`
  once; calling it again throws `next() called multiple times`. Automatically replaying a
  tool body needs a retry hook in the DSH core/executor. The plugin does not ship a switch
  that silently does nothing. Retrying a malformed **model-generated** tool call is safe and
  supported.
- **No infinite retries.** The global deadline and attempt cap are required; `0` disables a
  dimension but is not recommended for production.
- **Does not replace `@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm-retry`.** That package still owns step-level
  retries; this plugin owns provider selection and request-level resilience.
- **No streaming buffer for late fallback.** Once visible content is delivered, switching
  targets would duplicate output; the plugin hands the step back to the host instead.

## Tests

```bash
npm test
```

90 cases cover backoff/jitter, error classification, chain validation, adapter execution,
streaming safety, step-replay rotation, breaker persistence and multi-process merging,
global budgets, background probing, settings-client pure functions and the replay envelope
(including the legacy package name). End-to-end smoke runs on an isolated `DSH_HOME` with a
fake OpenAI-compatible server are described in [DESIGN.md](DESIGN.md).

## Compatibility and migration

- DSH `0.2.2-rc.x` (`engines.dsh` is `>=0.2.2-0 <0.3.0-0`), Node.js 20+.
- **Renamed from `dsh-llm-fallback` in 0.5.0.** The profile entry id remains `llm-fallback`,
  so settings and existing patches keep working; update the `name:` field to
  `dsh-llm-resilience`.
- The default breaker state file moved to
  `$DSH_HOME/storages/llm-resilience/state.json`. Set `stateFile` explicitly if you want to
  keep using an older breaker file.
- Replay envelopes from the old package name still unwrap (`dsh-llm-fallback` is accepted as
  a legacy kind).

## License

MIT. See [LICENSE](LICENSE).

# dsh-web-fallback-chain

**English** | [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md)

**One ranked, cost-aware chain for web search and fetch in DeepSeek Harness — measured quality, free-only mode, and a single settings page.**

DSH's `ctx.web` selects exactly **one** provider per capability, and its config is a pinned
provider id rather than a priority list. "Best first, something free when the best fails"
cannot be expressed in a profile. This plugin registers one provider per capability whose
internal order *is* that list — and ships the individual legs so you can pin any of them
directly.

- [Why this exists](#why-this-exists)
- [What makes it different](#what-makes-it-different)
- [What it registers](#what-it-registers)
- [Install](#install)
- [Ranking](#ranking)
- [The free-only switch](#the-free-only-switch)
- [Settings page](#settings-page)
- [Configuration](#configuration)
- [Why one package and not four](#why-one-package-and-not-four)
- [Tests](#tests)
- [Compatibility](#compatibility)

## Why this exists

A DSH profile can say *which* web provider to use, but not *in what order to try several*.
When the primary search or fetch fails, the request fails; there is no "try the free leg
next" seam. Rebuilding that seam in every deployment means four packages, four settings
pages, and a lockstep upgrade problem.

This plugin puts the ordered chain back into the provider slot:

```
web_search ──▶ search-chain ──▶ deepseek-search-rich ──▶ anysearch ──▶ tavily
web_fetch  ──▶ fetch-chain  ──▶ anysearch ──▶ tavily ──▶ deepseek-fetch-rich ──▶ http*
```

`http*` is an optional plain-HTTP leg supplied by the deployment (for example a separate
web-fetch plugin); this package does not register it. The first **available** leg serves
each request; the rest are attempted only when it fails or returns too little. The order is
a quality ranking, not a cost ranking. With the default `freeOnly: true`, paid legs are
skipped at call time, so the first available leg is the first *free* one.

## What makes it different

- **Measured, not guessed.** Defaults come from this plugin's own benchmark: blind-scored
  fetches on 15 pages, blind-scored search relevance on 10 queries, and 20-site availability
  runs. The numbers are a starting point you can reorder, not a promise about any page.
- **Free-only actually skips paid legs.** `freeOnly` is checked at call time. Turning it off
  restores the *same* order instead of maintaining a second list.
- **One package, one settings page.** Reorder legs with ▲▼, toggle free-only, annotate which
  leg served a fallback, and switch read mode. No second config to keep in sync.
- **Honest fallback.** The chain returns lossless JSON, can write the serving leg into the
  output, and does not treat a short page as a failure unless you opt in
  (`minBodyChars` defaults to 0).
- **Provider-specific value.** DeepSeek search maps the `summary` field (600–800 chars), not
  just a snippet; AnySearch is the leg that got through bot walls in testing; Tavily is the
  free leg that extracts PDFs.
- **Tested where it matters.** 162 `node --test` cases, including the real settings client
  rendered through `vm` with a fake module loader, and round-trip tests for every
  registered settings field.

## What it registers

| id | capability | what it is |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `search-chain` | search | the ordered search chain (pin `searchProvider` to this) |
| `fetch-chain` | fetch | the ordered fetch chain (pin `fetchProvider` to this) |
| `deepseek-search-rich` | search | DeepSeek search, mapping `summary` (600–800 chars) not just `snippet` |
| `deepseek-fetch-rich` | fetch | DeepSeek fetch |
| `anysearch` | search + fetch | AnySearch; the only leg that got through bot walls in testing |
| `tavily` | search + fetch | Tavily; the only free leg here that extracts PDFs |

`http` is intentionally **not** in this table: it is a deployment-supplied leg, not part of
this package. The chains can name it, and a fetch that falls through to it will use it when
another plugin registers that id.

## Install

Requirements: DSH `0.2.2-rc.x`, Node.js 20+, and **at least one** of
`DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`, `ANYSEARCH_API_KEY`, `TAVILY_API_KEY`. A leg without its key is still
registered but reports itself unavailable, so a chain with no keys has nothing to call.
An optional plain-HTTP leg (`http`) can be supplied by a separate web-fetch plugin.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/T-splines/dsh-web-fallback-chain.git
cd dsh-web-fallback-chain
dsh plugin --profile web add "$PWD"
```

The package is a bundle (`dsh.bundle.patch`), so its default entry is mounted by the
bundle. Pin the chain providers in your profile patch
(`$DSH_HOME/profiles/<profile>/cordis.patch.yml`):

```yaml
- id: web
  config:
    searchProvider: search-chain
    fetchProvider: fetch-chain
```

Reload the profile (or restart the web app), then open **Plugins → Installed →
dsh-web-fallback-chain**. The settings card is rendered on the plugin's detail page.
If your profile already pins another provider, replace those pins with the two ids above.

The profile entry id stays `web-fallback`. If you are upgrading from the old package name
`dsh-web-fallback`, remove the old package first; installing both would mount the same entry
twice. Existing settings keep working because the entry id did not change.

To verify the composition without starting an agent:

```bash
dsh --profile web --dump-config | grep -A6 'id: web-fallback'
```

## Ranking

Defaults are **strictly by measured quality, descending**, identical for every read mode:

| leg | quality | cost | key |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `deepseek-search-rich` | 9.6 | paid | `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` |
| `anysearch` | 7.3 | free | `ANYSEARCH_API_KEY` |
| `tavily` | 7.3 | free | `TAVILY_API_KEY` |
| `deepseek-fetch-rich` | 5.4 | paid | `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` |
| `http` | 4.0 | free | — (external leg, not shipped) |

Search order: `deepseek-search-rich → anysearch → tavily`.
Fetch order: `anysearch → tavily → deepseek-fetch-rich → http` (the last one only when an
external web-fetch plugin registers it).

`quality` is for ordering only — it is not a promise about a particular page. The numbers
come from the plugin's own benchmark; your corpus may rank differently. Reorder the ladders
on the settings page and the plugin writes the flat `order` / `searchOrder` list.

**First available means primary.** The first leg whose key is present and that is not
skipped by `freeOnly` serves the request; the rest are tried only when it fails or returns
too little. The list is ordered by "how good is what comes back", not by "how cheap is the
attempt".

## The free-only switch

`freeOnly` (default **on**) skips every leg marked `paid` **at call time**. It does not
reorder anything: the ranking is one list, and turning the switch off restores the same
sequence. The settings page shows billed legs greyed out rather than hiding them, so the
displayed list always matches the stored one.

Reading only `process.env` and skipping paid legs is the whole of it — there is no second
configuration to keep in sync.

## Settings page

It lives on the plugin's detail page — **Plugins → Installed → dsh-web-fallback-chain** —
not under Settings. The card has five primary controls, because every setting already has a
measured default and none of them is something you must fill in:

- two switches — `freeOnly`, `annotateFallback`
- one choice — `defaultMode` (`brief` / `deep` / `list` / `page`)
- two ladders with ▲▼ to reorder a leg

There is also an **Advanced** section for the settings you are more likely to touch:
`minBodyChars`, `timeoutMs`, the `enable` allow-list (as mount checkboxes), per-leg
`cost`, `deepseekNeedContent`, `anysearchTag`, and the three API keys.

## Configuration

The table below is the full field reference, including the few fields that remain
patch-only:

| field | where | meaning |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `minBodyChars` | Advanced | **Default 0 (off): HTTP status alone decides.** When set, a shorter body counts as a miss and the chain continues. A length floor cannot separate a site footer (142–332 chars) from a legitimately short page: `example.com` has 171 characters of real content. |
| `timeoutMs` | Advanced | per-leg timeout. Default 30000. |
| `order` / `searchOrder` | ▲▼ arrows | the flat ladder per capability. Covers every mode at once and takes precedence over the shipped per-mode defaults. |
| `modeOrders` | patch only | per-capability, per-mode override: `{ fetch: { deep: [...] } }`. Only set this to make one mode behave differently; an uncovered mode falls back to `order`. If `order` is empty too, the shipped per-mode defaults apply — that is how the no-config default works. |
| `enable` | Advanced | an **allow-list** of legs this plugin registers. **Empty means all.** Use it to keep a provider from ever being called — e.g. leaving a billed leg out so it is unreachable even with free-only off. |
| `providers` | Advanced (cost) / patch (rest) | per-leg metadata overrides: `cost` (what `freeOnly` reads), `maxChars` (per-mode budget), `requiresKey`, `kinds`, `note`. `quality` is documentation only; runtime ordering comes from `order` / `modeOrders`. |
| `deepseekNeedContent` | Advanced | DeepSeek search full-text. Billed per call either way; the response grows from ~5 KB to ~45 KB. |
| `anysearchTag` | Advanced | vertical routing, e.g. `code.doc`. It changes query semantics, not ranking. |
| `anysearchParams` | patch only | extra AnySearch query parameters, passed through as-is. |

> **Save rewrites the config block.** The settings page writes the whole `config` mapping
> through the host's `configForms` writer, which replaces the block wholesale — comments
> placed inside a config block do not survive a save. That is why this table exists instead
> of comment blocks in `cordis.patch.yml`. Comments elsewhere in the file are unaffected.

API keys are entered on the page and stored in the host credential store, which the legs
consult **before** the environment. A key typed into the page works without a restart.

## Why one package and not four

This started as four packages (policy / vendors / fetch chain / search chain) on a
single-responsibility argument. In practice that produced four settings pages, one package
that could not be configured at all (the shared policy has no `apply()`), and a lockstep
upgrade problem. Modules are the right unit for internal separation; a package is the right
unit for installing and configuring, and there should be exactly one.

```
config.js         one schema -> one settings page
policy/           who is free, which mode wants which order, how much text
providers/        the vendor HTTP legs
chains/           ordering and fallback logic
prompt.js         the one system-prompt section (when to reach for web_search)
client.js         the settings page
cordis.patch.yml  the default config, every field listed
```

## Tests

```bash
npm install --no-audit --no-fund   # peer dependencies provide the test imports
npm test
```

There is no build step. `npm install` is still required in a fresh checkout because the
tests import `@deepseek-ai/schemastery` and `@deepseek-ai/dsh-web`; they are declared as
peer dependencies, not bundled.
`test/client-render.test.js` runs the real `client.js` through `vm` with a fake
`__ModuleLoader__`, a fake `primitives` shaped like the shipped one, and a fake context that
expands `inject().hooks` the way the shell does. It exists because static checks missed five
different ways this page disappeared — including `Button` being a `forwardRef` object rather
than a callable function, which blanked the entire card.

One class of bug appeared three times and is now covered systematically: `settingsTextField`
is a *string* field, so a spec that overrides only `parse` leaves the read direction broken
and any non-string value (boolean, array, object) reads back as `''`. A test asserts the round
trip for every registered field spec.

## Compatibility

- DSH `0.2.2-rc.x` (the `engines.dsh` range is `>=0.2.2-0 <0.3.0-0`).
- Node.js 20+.
- The plugin is independent of DeepSeek; DSH and the named providers are separate projects.

## License

MIT. See [LICENSE](LICENSE).

# my-bench

A minimal [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) **UI plugin** that adds
one sidebar page of its own: an icon in the left column, and a full page in the main area when it is
selected.

It is the smallest complete example of a Client-half plugin: bundle manifest, loader patch, empty Host
module, and a `client.js` that registers into `sidebar.panellist` and `main`.

## Install

From the Harness Web UI: sidebar **Plugins → Add plugin → local directory**, pointing at this
directory. For a Git install, give the repository URL instead:

```
git+https://github.com/<you>/my-bench.git
```

After installing, **refresh the page** (the Client half does not need an app restart).

## What you should see

1. The **Plugins** page lists `my-bench` with this title and icon.
2. The left column gains a 🛠 entry at the bottom (`order: 20`).
3. Selecting it opens the page in the main area.

## Layout

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `package.json` | `dsh.bundle.patch` makes it installable; `dsh.client` makes it a browser bundle |
| `cordis.patch.yml` | inserts the `my-bench` row |
| `index.js` | Host half; empty here, and where tools would be registered |
| `client.js` | registers the sidebar entry and the page; owns all UI text |
| `locale/*.json` | `meta.title` / `meta.description` shown in the Plugins page |
| `icon.svg` | icon shown in the Plugins page |

## Extending

- Add a tool: register it in `index.js` with `ctx.tools.register(defineTool({...}))`.
- Show tool output: call it from `BenchPage` through the Client remote service, or subscribe to a
  session projection.
- Change the surface: swap `sidebar.panellist` + `main` for `conversation.composer.dock` or
  `conversation.view`.

## License

MIT

# dsh-a-plan-board · DSH 计划看板

> 一块和模型共同维护的任务看板：**任务写在文件里，执行交回模型**。
> 你在面板上挑任务、批注、否决；点一次「让他做」，模型按顺序开工，做完自己打勾。

这是一个 [DeepSeek Harness（DSH）](https://github.com/deepseek-ai) 插件（bundle），
包含 Host 半区、浏览器半区、一个模型侧工具组，以及一份随插件分发的执行约定技能。

---

## 目录

- [它解决什么问题](#它解决什么问题)
- [界面](#界面)
- [安装](#安装)
- [计划文件格式](#计划文件格式)
- [命令](#命令)
- [模型侧工具](#模型侧工具)
- [技能](#技能)
- [架构](#架构)
- [开发](#开发)
- [已知限制](#已知限制)
- [许可证](#许可证)

---

## 它解决什么问题

和模型协作时，任务列表通常散落在对话里：说过的话会沉底，做完的没标记，改主意了也留不下痕迹。

这个插件把它变成一份**文件即真相**的计划板：

- 任务是 markdown 里的一行，带「做法」「验收」，可以批注、可以否决；
- 你在看板上挑选和排序，形成"接下来"队列；
- 点一次按钮，队列被交给模型，模型开工时自己标进行中、做完标完成；
- 一切状态变化都回写到文件，面板、会话视图、聊天卡片读的是同一份数据。

## 界面

三个入口，同一份数据：

| 入口 | 位置 | 用途 |
|---|---|---|
| 计划板页 | 左侧导航图标 → 整页 | 主界面：正在做、整体分组、接下来队列 |
| 计划板视图 | 会话头部的视图行 | 与当前会话绑定的同一块板 |
| `/aboard` 卡片 | 对话流 | 输入 `/aboard` 得到一张带进度的摘要卡，可一键跳回面板 |

面板顶部是压缩过的状态条（运行状态、完成数、进度条、搜索），下面是三段：

```
正在做 · 1                 ● 运行中          排队 2 条   ▾
◐ 给模型一个写板工具…        P0   3m12s   ✎ ✓
  验收：提交「打通 API」这类简短条目会被工具退回…
──────────────────────────────────────────────
排队中 · 2 条
#1  给模型一个更新条目状态的工具            P0   排队
#2  让 /aboard 命令既能给人看也能当接口      P0   排队
```

左列是**整体**（按阶段分组、可折叠、组头带子进度、完成的收进「已完成 n」），
右列是**接下来**（你的队列，可拖拽排序、可切串行/并行、可整队清空）。

支持：拖拽入队/排序/移出、优先级 P0–P3、批注、否决（灰掉保留）、搜索、
键盘操作（↑↓ 移动、空格选择、0–3 设优先级、Enter 标进行中）、
中英双语、亮暗主题（所有颜色都取自主题 token，并对配色做了 WCAG 对比度校准）。

## 安装

插件包就在仓库根目录（`package.json` 声明了 `dsh.bundle.patch` 与 `dsh.client`）。

**本地安装**：DSH → 设置 → Plugins → Add plugin → 选择本目录；
或者用插件管理器安装：

```text
plugin_manager install_bundle target=/Users/<you>/codespace/plan-board
```

安装后需要刷新页面；若 Host 端代码有更新，需要重启 DSH（Host 在发布时会快照插件包，
热更新依赖 `/plugins/events` 流，该流不可用时只能重启）。

## 计划文件格式

数据在**当前会话工作区**的 `.dsh/plan-board.md`。建议把它加进 `.gitignore`（属于本地数据）。

```md
# 计划板 · 项目名

> 目标：一句话说明这一轮要达成什么。

## P1 · 分组名

- [ ] 一句完整人话的任务标题  @P0 @选 @start=2026-11-15T16:53
  做法：具体怎么做。
  验收：怎么算做完，尽量写可验证的标准。
  批注：用户的意见，会写回文件。
```

**状态**：`[ ]` 未开始 · `[~]` 进行中 · `[x]` 完成 · `[-]` 已否决（灰掉保留）。

**标记**：`@P0`–`@P3` 优先级 · `@选` 已挑选 · `@弃` 已否决 · `@start=` 开始时间 · `@序=N` 拖拽顺序。

样例见 [`examples/plan-board.md`](examples/plan-board.md)。

## 命令

`/aboard` 既给人用，也是**面板和模型之间的接口**（Client 通过 `remote.commands.execute` 调用同一批子命令）。

| 子命令 | 作用 |
|---|---|
| `/aboard` | 结构化摘要（聊天卡片用） |
| `/aboard list` | 人读的分组摘要 |
| `/aboard json` | 完整结构化数据 |
| `/aboard pick <n>` | 选中 / 取消选中 |
| `/aboard prio <n> <P0-P3\|->` | 设优先级 |
| `/aboard doing\|done\|undone <n>` | 状态流转 |
| `/aboard drop\|undrop <n>` | 否决 / 恢复 |
| `/aboard note <n> <text>` | 追加批注 |
| `/aboard reorder <i,j,k>` | 写入队列顺序 |
| `/aboard next` | 按队列顺序开工第一条 |
| `/aboard start <n>` | 开工指定条目 |
| `/aboard batch <serial\|parallel> <i,j,k>` | 批量派活 |
| `/aboard clear` | 清空队列里的选择与优先级（不动任务） |
| `/aboard goal <text>` | 改本轮目标 |

## 模型侧工具

| 工具 | 作用 | 校验 |
|---|---|---|
| `plan_board_write` | 往指定分组写任务 | 标题 ≥ 20 字、必须有做法与验收，否则拒绝并给出补齐提示 |
| `plan_board_status` | 切换条目状态，进行中写 `@start`，完成清除 | 序号/状态必须合法 |

这两个工具让模型**自己维护看板**：写计划、开工、打勾，不需要人代劳。

## 技能

`skills/plan-board/SKILL.md` 随插件分发，通过 `dsh-skill-filesystem` 的
`bundledSkillDir` 挂载（见 `cordis.patch.yml`），因此**装到任何工作区都自带执行约定**。

它规定了：开工前必须用工具标进行中、做完标完成、卡住时留批注而不是假装完成、
不许改条目原文、不许清理别人的选择标记、最后只做简短汇总。

派活消息因此可以极短：

```
【计划板】串行做第 4、5、6 条。执行约定：加载 skill `plan-board`。
```

## 架构

```
                     ┌──────────────────────────────┐
  对话 / 模型  ──────▶│ Host 半区 (index.js)          │
                     │  /aboard 命令 · 两个工具      │
                     └──────────────┬───────────────┘
                                    │ 读写
                                    ▼
                        .dsh/plan-board.md  ← 唯一真相
                                    ▲
                     ┌──────────────┴───────────────┐
   面板 / 卡片  ─────▶│ Client 半区 (client.js)      │
                     │ 读: remote.workspaceFiles     │
                     │ 写: remote.commands.execute   │
                     └──────────────────────────────┘
```

- **Host 半区**：注册命令与工具，解析/改写 markdown，负责所有写入。
- **Client 半区**：注册四个插槽入口（左栏图标、整页面板、会话视图、聊天卡片行），
  读文件用只读的 workspace-files Remote（不产生会话记录），写文件复用命令通道。
- **为什么写要走命令**：DSH 的第三方 bundle 没有自定义 Remote 命名空间，
  但"命令"是官方支持的 UI → Host 调用入口；命令产生的事件在聊天里被
  `conversation.chat.commandview` 接管，机器调用渲染为空，不打扰对话。
- **唤醒机制**：开工时 Host 调 `agent.followup()` 投递一条真实的用户消息，模型因此被唤醒。

没有改任何模型提示词，没有往会话日志里写自定义事件类型。

## 开发

```bash
# 本地目录以 link 方式装进 profile，改文件即改源码
plugin_manager install_bundle target=/absolute/path/to/this/repo
```

改完代码后的生效方式：

- **客户端改动**：刷新页面（bundle 会重新发布）。
- **Host 改动**：禁用再启用插件（重启 Loader 条目），或重启 DSH。
- 一键切换：设置 → Plugins → 关闭再打开「计划板」。

`docs/DESIGN.md` 记录了完整的需求演进与设计取舍（含被推翻的方案）。

## 已知限制

- 面板 3 秒轮询文件，没有用文件系统监听；
- 「当前在跑哪个工具」未接入，只显示会话运行/空闲；
- 拖拽排序只在「接下来」列内生效，不能跨分组拖动条目；
- 并行模式依赖模型自己派子代理，插件只负责把批次交代清楚；
- 包名仍是 `@local/plan-board`，发布到 npm 前需要改成正式 scope。

## 许可证

[MIT](LICENSE)

Neither the fixed manifest nor captured README supplies a versioned DSH compatibility contract. No candidate code or lifecycle hooks were executed; runtime safety and compatibility are unproven.

# dsh-openloop-mas

OpenLoop MAS 插件（DeepSeek Harness）。

把「会闭合的多智能体循环」带进 DSH 对话：规划 → 执行 → **机检验收** → 复盘 →
闭合 / 升级人工工单，每一轮都写进 **append-only 账本**。

## 它做什么

在 DSH 里直接可用 6 个工具：

| 工具 | 用途 |
| --- | --- |
| `mas_run` | 跑一个闭环任务，返回状态 + 逐条验收判定 + 票数 + 账本路径 |
| `mas_status` | 当前配置、运行数、未结工单 |
| `mas_ledger` | 读闭环账本（可按 run_id 过滤） |
| `mas_tickets` | 列出人工升级工单 |
| `mas_report` | 渲染某次运行的 Markdown 报告 |
| `mas_doctor` | 运行环境自检 |

插件**不重写闭环逻辑**：它通过 MCP（stdio JSON-RPC 2.0）调用本地 OpenLoop MAS
运行时，因此 DSH 对话里的判定与账本记录和 Codex / Claude Code 客户端**完全一致**。

## 前提

- **DSH >= 0.2.2-rc.1**（声明兼容区间 `>=0.2.2-rc.1 <0.3.0`）
- **Node.js >= 22.19**
- 已装好 OpenLoop MAS 运行时（默认在 `~/.mas`）

## 安装

前置：机器上已装好 OpenLoop MAS 运行时（默认在 `~/.mas`）。

```bash
# 从本仓库打包
cd integrations/dsh-openloop-mas
npm pack            # -> dsh-openloop-mas-0.7.13.tgz

# 装进 DSH Desktop profile
dsh plugin --profile desktop add "dsh-openloop-mas@file:<绝对路径>/dsh-openloop-mas-0.7.13.tgz"
dsh plugin --profile desktop list dsh-openloop-mas --depth 0
```

> `desktop` profile 由桌面应用独占管理，命令行会报
> `profile "desktop" is managed exclusively by the Electron application`。
> 这种情况下请在 DSH Desktop 的插件面板里安装，或改用 `--profile cli`。

## 配置

```json
{
  "dsh-openloop-mas": {
    "masHome": "C:/Users/<you>/.mas",
    "python": "C:/Python314/python.exe",
    "timeoutMs": 900000
  }
}
```

- `masHome`：OpenLoop MAS 安装根目录（`install.ps1` 写入的位置）。留空则只依赖
  PATH 上的 `mas` 运行时。
- `python`：解释器路径。留空则从 `masHome` 推断，再退回 `python`。
- `timeoutMs`：单次 MCP 调用超时。默认 900000（15 分钟）——闭环可能要跑好几轮。

## 前提与边界

- 本插件**只负责调用**，判定权在 OpenLoop MAS 引擎手里：机检结果永远压过模型
  主观判断；缺席的评审在 `all` 模式下判**不通过**（不闭合）。
- 插件不引入任何第三方 npm 依赖（只用 DSH 自带的 `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools` 与
  `@deepseek-ai/schemastery`）。
- `lib/mcp-client.js` **零依赖**，可以脱离 DSH 单独跑单元测试：
  `node --test integrations/dsh-openloop-mas/tests/`。

## 挂载机制（容易踩的坑）

DSH 认的字段是 **`dsh.bundle.patch`**（指向 `cordis.patch.yml`），
不是 `dsh.profile.bundles`。放错的结果是：插件被当成普通依赖装上、
**根本不挂载**，pnpm 会警告 `declares no dsh.bundle`。

挂载后，DSH 启动时自动应用 patch：

```
- insert:
    - id: openloop-mas
      name: 'dsh-openloop-mas'
      config: ...
```

工具参数 schema 必须满足 DSH 的 JSON Schema 子集：`items.additionalProperties`
要**显式**为 `true` / `false`，否则 `defineTool` 会抛 `JsonSchemaError`，
整个插件 entry 不激活（`1 entry did not activate`）。

## 与 MOKI 的分工

MOKI 资料库（`dsh-moki-library`）管的是**资料与草稿**：本地文件/文件夹/链接管理、
多格式预览、Word/Excel/PPT 隔离草稿编辑、选区协同（`Alt+D` 唤起 DSH 对话），
修改先入草稿、用户确认后才写回原文件。

OpenLoop MAS 管的是**闭环**：验收标准、机检判定、账本、人工升级。

两者可以同时装，各管一段：MOKI 负责把资料整理成一份可交付的产物，
OpenLoop MAS 负责判定这份产物到底过不过。

## License

MIT

# OpenLoop MAS · 会闭合的多智能体系统

> 一个 **零依赖、纯标准库** 的多智能体闭环运行时：把「规划 → 执行 → 验证 → 复盘」写成**有验收标准、有退出条件、有过程账本**的工程循环。
> **下载一个脚本就能装**，初学者也能跑起来。

**v0.7.63 加了什么**（**装完即自证**）：

- **安装脚本现在会自己跑门禁** —— `install.ps1` 与 `install.sh` 装完后
  自动执行一次 `mas selftest --iterations 20`。**装坏了当场看得见**，
  不用等到第一次真跑任务才发现。
- **两项新门禁**（全程离线：不要端点、不要 key、不要网络）：

**v0.7.43 加了什么**（让**报告讲出整个循环**，而不只是最后一轮）：

- **反思终于看得见了** —— reflector 是**唯一说得出「下一轮必须改什么」的角色**，

**v0.7.42 加了什么**（让**「没判定过」不再被写成「没通过」**）：

- **没人判定过的标准，被报告写成了 `[FAIL]`** —— 引擎对每条验收标准
  其实有**三种状态**：**通过了**、**没通过**、**没人能判定**
  （没有机检、评审没给出结论、lead 也判不了）。引擎对第三种状态
  **特别小心**：它**永远不会算通过**，也**不会让它自己闭合闭环**。
  但报告在最后一步**把这三种压成了两种** —— 判失败的列表用
  `not pass` 筛选，**`None` 也被算进去了**。于是**从没被检查过的标准，
  在报告里成了「检查过且被否决」**。现在判失败的列表**只认
  `pass is False`**，那才是「判了，而且没判过」的准确含义；
- **「交付物不合格」这句话本身就是假的** —— 以前只要交付物没通过，
  报告就写「❌ 未通过验收标准」，**哪怕根本没查完**。
  现在**有标准从未被判定时，报告会直说**，并**把标准号点出来**：
  **不是被否决，是压根没查完**；
- **Markdown 里终于有了第三种标记** —— 验收表以前只有 `PASS` 和
  `FAIL`，现在**没人判定的是 `UNDECIDED`**，并注明**不能算通过**；
  报告还会**单列一节**，把判定来源（`rule` / `file` / `model` /
  `lead` / `model-missing`）写出来，**让人看到"为什么没人能判"**；
- **JSON 报告也分得清了** —— `run_summary` 新增 `unjudged` 键，
  和 `failed` / `optional_failed` 并列，**读 JSON 的人不用去猜**；
- 配套回归测试 **8 个**，**每一层改动都做过反证**：单独回退后确认对应测试会挂。

**v0.7.41 加了什么**（让**闭环的最后一环真的接上**）：

  但**工单号根本没写进账本**，于是报告除了「escalated」**什么也说不出来**，
  人拿到报告**没法找到那张工单**。现在**工单号入账**；
- **报告能指到工单，也能告诉你下一步** —— 报告现在**报出工单号**，

**v0.7.40 加了什么**（让**「为什么没闭合」不再消失**）：

- **报告从来不说为什么没闭合** —— 引擎**把理由记在结束条目里**，
  v0.7.37 起还专门把停滞的理由写具体了
  （"交付物连续 N 次没有变化"），**但报告只读了状态、把理由扔了**。

  报告**会说明"未记录具体原因"，而不是闷着**；

**v0.7.39 加了什么**（让**「没闭合」不再是一句糊涂话**）：

- **交付物明明合格，报告却说「没闭合」** —— 引擎其实**分别知道两件事**：
  **交付物过没过验收标准**、**这次运行闭没闭合**，而且**把第一件事记在了结束条目里**，
  但**报告把它扔了**。真机实测过：交付物**通过了全部验收标准**，
  运行因为停滞升级而没闭合 —— 旧报告只写「not closed」，
  **看起来像活儿做砸了**，用户**只能靠猜**是哪一半出了问题。
  现在这种运行**单独报成 `deliverable_ok_but_not_closed`**：
  **这是一个能区分的状态**，不是「没做完」的第三种说法；
- **Markdown 里也没说清是哪一半坏了** —— 现在**直接用话讲**：
  **交付物通过了全部验收标准，但本次运行没有闭合（预算或死线到了）——
  交付物可用，直接取用即可**；
- **「运行没来得及说」不等于「交付物是坏的」** —— 没有结束条目的运行，
  引擎**根本不知道**交付物如何，报告现在报 `deliverable_ok: None`，
  **而不是自信地报 `False`**；
- 配套回归测试 **5 个**，**每一层改动都做过反证**：单独回退后确认对应测试会挂。

**v0.7.38 加了什么**（让**「负责拍板的那个角色」真的上线**）：

- **`lead` 角色一直只有合同，没有接线** —— `roles.py` 写清了 lead 的职责，
  `providers.py` 有它的 mock 分支，README 和 Skill 都把「闭合」写在它名下，
  **但引擎从头到尾没调用过它**：结局是代码里那句
  `decision = "close" if passed else "revise"`。现在**该问的时候真的会问**：
  **有验收标准既没有机检、评审也没判定**时，lead 拿到这些标准和交付物，
  回答 `{"decision", "reason", "judged": [{"id", "met", "note"}]}`；
- **lead 是顾问，不是事实的法官** —— **机检失败是事实**，这种情况
  **根本不咨询 lead**；咨询了也**只能填空**，机检已经定了的标准
  **原样保留**，lead 说什么都不算。**停滞、预算、死线**这些硬约束，
  **引擎保留最终否决权**，lead 关不掉一个已经超预算的运行；
- **lead 说不清楚就什么也关不掉** —— `met` 读不出布尔值时，
  标准**保持未判定**，循环**继续追问**（和「读不懂的评审答复」同一套规矩）。
  lead **坏了**（端点不通、答复是乱码）也只是**不判定**，
  **不会削弱引擎自己的判断**；
- **lead 的调用没进账** —— lead 也是**要花钱的**，但它的角色
  **不在账本的计费名单里**，于是**凡是问了 lead 的运行，报账都少算**。
  现在**入账**，**账本合计 == 运行报告的 token 用量**；
- 配套回归测试 **5 个**，**每一层改动都做过反证**：单独回退后确认对应测试会挂。

**v0.7.37 加了什么**（让**「读不懂的答复」不再能蒙混过关**）：

- **分数不是判定** —— 模型答 `"pass": 0.5`（意思是「这条标准满足了一半」），
  旧代码用 `bool(value)`，**0.5 直接变成 True**：这条标准被记成**完全通过**，
  **循环就这么闭合了**。现在**数字只有正好是 0 或 1 才算判定**，
  其余的**一律算「读不懂」**，而**读不懂就不是答复**；
- **「读不懂」曾被悄悄记成「不通过」** —— 归一化把读不懂的判定折成
  `pass: False`，引擎**分不出**「评审说不行」和「评审没说清」，
  于是这条标准**看起来已经判定过了**，引擎**再也不追问评审**，
  白白烧掉一轮迭代去改一个根本改不动的地方。
  现在**读不懂的标记在入口就被读出来**：标准**保持未判定**，
  **追问一次**，**以回来的那个答复为准**；
- **多评审和单评审对同一份乱码答复处置不一致** —— panel 聚合把标记丢了，
  **配 1 个评审会追问，配 3 个评审却记成「已判定为不通过」**。
  现在聚合**带上标记**，**两条路行为一致**；
- **另一条 JSON 形状一直没人管** —— 归一化有两条路：
  `{"scores": [...]}` 和 `{"criteria": [...]}`。v0.7.12 只在第一条路上
  让顶层总结服从逐条判定，**第二条路漏了**：模型**逐条答 FAIL、顶层答 pass**，
  顶层总结**还是 pass**。现在**两条路规矩一样**；
- **总结不能替读不懂的评审开绿灯** —— 所有判定都读不懂时，
  模型的顶层总结会被保留，于是
  `{"verdict": "pass", "scores": [{"pass": "maybe"}]}` **报的是通过**。
  引擎本来就是按逐条判定闭合的，**报告现在也这么说**：
  **没人判定过，就没人通过**；
- **报告里的迭代次数有时是 `null`** —— 旧表达式 `a or b if rows else 0`
  实际解析成 `(a or b) if rows else 0`，行里没有 `iteration` 字段时
  报的是 **null**，而**写着「null 次迭代」的报告，脚本读不了**。
  现在按**运行自己的结束条目 → closure 行 → 所有行里最大的迭代号**取，**永远是个数字**；
- **升级处理不说是为什么** —— 交付物不再变化导致的升级，
  理由写的是「循环无法自行闭合」，**会让人去找错的东西**。
  现在**点名原因**：交付物连续 N 次没有变化；
- 配套回归测试 **11 个**，**每一层改动都做过反证**：单独回退后确认对应测试会挂。

**v0.7.36 加了什么**（让**死线真的是死线**，让**自检不再沉默几分钟**）：

- **`deadline_sec` 不是天花板，它只是一句说明** —— 墙钟预算**只在两轮迭代之间**被检查。
  **一次 provider 调用超了预算**（端点慢、回答长）**是被允许跑完的**，
  **而运行依然会报「闭环成功」**。实测：死线 1s 配 3s 的慢 provider，
  **跑了 9.0s 仍然报成功**；真机死线 180s，**耗时 185.26s 仍然报成功**。
  **配置里写的那个数字，当时只是文档，不是约束**。
  现在**每一次 provider 调用都带着剩余墙钟预算这个硬天花板**：HTTP 层取
  **「配置超时」与「剩余预算」里更小的那个**，**每次重试重新计算**，
  预算耗尽时抛出一个**专门的 `BudgetExceeded`** —— 那是**主动止损**，不是**端点坏了**，
  报告里也**分开说**。**闭合判定本身也要过一遍钟**：交付物**通过了全部机检**，
  **但到得比死线晚**，那就**升级处理（escalate）而不是闭合**，
  **并且把原因写清楚**。顺带修掉一个更隐蔽的 bug：**判定顺序**原来是
  「检查通过就无条件收工」，于是引擎**判出来的 escalate 会被自己丢掉**；
- **自检会沉默好几分钟** —— 实测真机一整轮 **460.5s 一个字都没有**，
  **看起来和卡死完全一样**。现在 `mas verify` **每一步慢操作之前都先报一声**：
  端点握手、指令校验、真实闭环，**闭环结束时报用时**。进度走 **stderr**，
  **`--json` 的 stdout 契约不受影响**；
- **自检判的是一份用户根本没跑过的配置** —— verify 运行时把用户自己配置的墙钟预算
  **覆盖成了一个写死的 180 秒**。真机实测一轮 **342 秒**、而用户自己的预算是 **900 秒**，
  结果**报「未闭环」** —— **自检把一个本来能跑通的配置判成了失败**。现在自检
  **用用户真正配的那个预算**（上限 900 秒，**免得沉默一刻钟**）；
- **「未闭环」把「哪一半坏了」给藏住了** —— 交付物**通过了全部机检**、只是**超了预算**的运行，
  和**交付物一塌糊涂**的运行，**报的是同一句话**。用户于是**去找一个根本不存在的坏交付物**，
  **真正的问题——那个钟——却没被点名**。现在引擎**把两件事分开记**：
  `deliverable_ok` 说**交付物过没过机检**，`status` 说**运行闭没闭合**；
  自检会**点名是哪一种**：**「交付物已通过全部机检，但本次运行超出时间预算」**，
  **直接告诉你该调哪个旋钮**；
- 天花板通过**线程局部上下文**传给 provider，**不给 `Provider.complete` 加新参数** ——
  **所有既有自定义 provider 和插件一行都不用改**。并行工作线程**显式继承**天花板，
  因为**线程池不继承线程局部状态**；
- 配套回归测试 **5 个**。

**v0.7.35 加了什么**（让自检**诊断的是你自己的配置**，而不是一个假象）：

- **端点握手**没带密钥**，却报 401** —— v0.7.34 让 provider 按 `api_key_env`

  **都带着密钥、都成功了**。**用户被告知要去修一个本来就没错的配置**，

  现在握手**和运行时用同一套方式解析凭据**：provider 检查、指令检查、
  端点检查**说的是同一种方言、带着同一份凭据**，
  **诊断终于诊断的是用户自己的配置**；
- 已实测（对着一个拒绝无鉴权请求的本地服务器）：**修之前** endpoint 行报
  `HTTP 401`、而服务器日志显示**其余每个请求都带着密钥**；**修之后**
  endpoint 行报**端点可达**、**闭环真的闭合**。

**v0.7.34 加了什么**（让自检说真话 —— 并且**把你设好的密钥真的发给模型**）：

- **你设好的密钥，从来没被发出去过** —— 初始化向导让你把密钥放进

- **`mas verify` 的 provider 那一行是橡皮图章** —— 它**只把配置里的字符串打印出来**，

  **中间什么都没有告诉你真正的原因**。现在 provider 行会**说清端点地址、密钥找没找到**，

- mock 模式**依然完全离线**：**不发握手、不发指令探测、一次网络请求都没有**；
- 配套回归测试 **10 个**。已实测：`mas verify` 指向本机真实端点 →
  **握手 ok、指令生效 ok、闭环 ok、账本 5 条**；指向一个死端口 →

**v0.7.33 加了什么**（让回放真的能看懂 —— 以及修掉默认配置下的「None 之谜」）：

- **闭合运行的回放，closure 那一行是空白的** —— closure 行恰恰是**唯一说明

  **一个人也算面板**，现在**数字齐了**；
- **沉默的评审者没有被记成「缺席票」** —— 单评审者模式下，**没给出任何可判定内容的评审**

**v0.7.32 加了什么**（让报告说的状态 == 运行真实的状态）：

- **报告分不清「停了」「炸了」「没干完」** —— 引擎**从不把最终状态写进账本**，
  报告只能**靠 closure 行去猜**，于是**凡是没走完决策就结束的运行，猜的全是错的**；
- **撞预算上限停下的运行，被报告成「未闭环」** —— 那读起来像「**还没做完**」，
  可它其实是**主动停的、有明确原因的停**。现在报告直接写 `budget_exhausted`；
- **provider 报错挂掉的运行，被报告成「incomplete」** —— **错误原因一个字都没有**。
  **失败的运行**，不能被当成**从未完成的运行**；
- **失败运行的产物是隐形的** —— 产物哈希挂在 closure 行上，而**在评分之前就挂掉的运行
  根本没有 closure 行**，于是报告显示空产物，读者**根本查不到这次到底做出了什么**；
- **账本现在自己交代「这次是怎么结束的」** —— 每次运行末尾新增一条 `run_end` 条目，
  带上**状态、决策、错误、迭代数、产物哈希、未解决 issues、总花费**；
  报告**直接读它，不再猜**，原始账本表格也**逐行交代结局**；
- 配套回归测试 **15 个**。已实测：逐个去掉修复 → **5 处回退全部被测试抓住**。
  真机跑通一次闭环，**运行状态 == 报告状态**，**引擎记账 == 账本求和 == 报告花费**，
  **三者分毫不差**。

**v0.7.31 加了什么**（让账本能自己回答「这次运行花了多少」）：

- **账本根本回答不了「花了多少钱」** —— 花费数字**只活在引擎的内存里**，
  账本里没有，**复盘报告里也没有**。现在**每次计费都在账本里记一次**，

- **单 worker 路径**一条账本都不写 —— 并行候选池**记得账**，**单 worker 不记得**，
  于是**worker 花的钱在账本里凭空消失**。现在**同角色记账**；
- **reflector 从来没被记过账** —— 它**每次失败后都要跑**，**是要花钱的调用**，
  账本里却**一个字都没有**：一次反复自我修正的运行，**从不说复盘花了多少钱**。
  现在**记账**；
- **只记了最后一轮评审** —— 首轮评审和**追问**是**两次独立的计费调用**，
  现在**分开记账**，并且**一个 token 不会被记两次**；
- 配套回归测试 **14 个**。已实测：逐个去掉修复 → **每一处都有测试失败**。
  不变式扫描覆盖 **45 种池子形状**，现在同时校验
  **端点实收 == 引擎记账 == 账本求和**，**三者分毫不差**。

**v0.7.30 加了什么**（修掉「追问轮」的两个缺陷 —— 面板模式与单评审者模式**行为不一致**）：

- **靠追问答案闭合的运行，账本却记成「评审什么都没判」** —— 评审者漏判的标准，
  引擎会**追问一次**（一次便宜的小问题，而不是重来一整轮）。
  但**单评审者模式**在追问之后**账本里留的还是旧面板** ——
  于是账本显示「评审没有给出任何判定」，**旁边却是一次已经闭合的运行**。
  审计者看着像白纸黑字写着「没评审过」。**面板模式本来就把追问结果带下去了**，
  现在**单评审者模式也带** —— 账本记的，**就是引擎真正据以决策的那个面板**；
- **追问失败 = 整个运行直接报错结束** —— 追问是**补充提问**，它失败了，
  正确处理是**该标准保持「未判定」**，交给循环正常往下走。
  **面板模式本来就是这么降级的**，**单评审者模式却让异常逃了出去** ——
  **同一个漏判，在一个配置里让运行崩溃，在另一个配置里只是变慢**。
  现在**两种模式行为一致**。失败的调用**照样记账**（端点收了钱），
  并且**写进账本**；
- 配套回归测试 6 个。已实测：逐个去掉修复 → **3 个 / 2 个测试失败**。

**v0.7.29 加了什么**（修掉「失败的调用没被记账」的三个缺陷）：

- **失败的候选，只有「恰好排在赢家前面」才被记账** —— 并行池里失败成员的开销，

  **这笔钱永远消失**。同一个池子，**花费取决于哪个成员先跑完** ——
  而**取决于赛跑结果的预算不是预算**。现在开销在**和截断同一个 pre-pass 里统一收齐**，
  排完名之后**一次性入账**，**顺序不再影响任何数字**；
- **被整池丢掉的池子，失败的那个成员没被记账** —— 截断让整池作废时，
  被截断的、被丢弃后已完成的**都记账了**，唯独**直接失败的那个成员漏了**。
  被丢掉的每个成员**端点都收了钱**，现在**全都记账**；
- **被丢弃的评审轮，失败的那个评审者没被记账** —— 同样的毛病，发生在评审面板上：
  截断让这一轮作废时，**直接失败的那个评审者**被排除在账单之外。
  现在**第一轮评审**和**追问轮**都把它记上；
- **一个被计费的失败调用不会说自己花了多少钱** —— `ProviderError` 现在**带着这次失败调用的用量**，
  于是**响应形状坏了**、**流在半路死了**、**降级链倒到下一个后端**这三种情况，
  花费都能**跟着异常一起走到引擎**。以前**死在 provider 错误上的运行**，
  会为**已经付过钱的活儿**报告**零开销**；
- 配套回归测试 5 个。已实测：逐个去掉修复 → **每个对应测试都会失败**。
  不变式扫描现在覆盖 **50 种池子形状**（1~4 个 worker × 1~3 个评审者，
  跨越干净运行、截断、失败与混合），**每一种都分毫不差地记下端点收的账**。

**v0.7.28 加了什么**（修掉三个「预算账本说谎」的缺陷 + 一个「永远闭合不了」的缺陷）：

- **被整个丢掉的候选池，账本当成免费** —— 并行候选池里只要**有一个**被输出上限截断，
  **整池作废重试**；但引擎**只给被截断的那个记账**，
  **已经跑完的那几个候选等于白送**。实测：账本记 **6,000** token，
  端点实收 **16,010**。**token 上限因此系统性地放水**，预算根本不是预算。
  现在**整池花费先收齐**再抛截断 —— 账本上的数字**就是端点开的账单**；
- **planner 和 reflector 干脆一次都没记账** —— 这两个都是**要花钱的调用**：
  planner 在第一轮、reflector 在每一次失败后。实测：计划→写→失败→复盘→评审，
  账本记 **922**，端点实收 **1,033**。现在**两个都记账**，
  账本里也**看得见 planner 这一次的开销**；
- **被截断的评审者被当成「缺席的投票人」** —— 评审者**用完输出额度**，
  **不是「不同意」**，是**根本没写完**。严格模式把它算成**缺席票**，
  于是循环**永远闭合不了**：每一轮烧掉整个预算，最后**为一个「再试一次就能过」的理由升级**。
  现在评审面板里的截断**是可重试的失败**，下一轮**给更大的输出空间** ——
  和 worker 路径**早就是这么做的**保持一致。**追问轮**（re-ask）同样适用；
- 配套回归测试 10 个。已实测：逐个去掉修复 → **每个对应测试都会失败**。

**v0.7.27 加了什么**（修掉三个「循环闭合得不对」的缺陷）：

- **列表形式的文件机检让循环永远闭合不了** —— 引擎把「要写哪些文件」交给 worker 时，
  **自己解析了一遍**机检参数，而机检**用的是另一套解析器**。两套解析器在**列表写法**上不一致：
  机检看到的是 `notes/a.txt`，引擎看到的是字面量 `['notes/a.txt']`。
  于是 worker 被要求去写一个**名字里带方括号**的文件，而机检去看的是**另一个路径** ——
  循环**跑多少轮都闭合不了**。现在引擎**用机检自己的解析器**读路径，两边永远一致；
- **跑通了的运行却报告着上一次的错误** —— 一次截断重试后成功闭合的运行，
  `status` 是 `closed`，`error` 却还留着 `truncated answer: ...`。
  CLI 于是打出「说明：truncated answer」，**读起来像一次失败的运行**。
  现在**瞬时故障只属于它发生的那一轮**：闭合即清零，
  但**账本里那条 `truncated` 记录照旧保留** —— 审计线索一条不少；
- **token 上限不是上限** —— 预算只在**一轮结束后**检查，而**截断重试是在那之前发生的**。
  一个不停撞输出上限的运行**可以花掉远超上限的 token**（实测上限 20 万、实花 24 万）。
  现在**每轮开头也检查上限**，它才真的是上限；
- 配套回归测试 7 个。已实测：逐个去掉修复 → **2 + 2 + 1 个测试失败**。

**v0.7.26 加了什么**（修掉一个「出错时账本没有记录」的缺陷）：

- **意外异常会抹掉审计线索** —— 引擎只捕获 `ProviderError`，**其他任何异常**都会直接冲出 `run()`。
  结果是：**账本里只剩一条「开始了」的记录，没有结局** —— 没有 error 条目、没有 closure、没有工单。
  那次运行的**闭环状态就此无从查证**，而这恰恰是本项目存在的意义；
- **引擎不是一个安全的库入口** —— CLI、MCP 工具、HTTP 路由**各自都有异常边界**，
  所以命令行用户看到的是干净报错。但引擎**也被直接调用**（库用户、脚本、嵌入式运行时），
  在那里它抛的是**裸 traceback**；
- 现在循环**捕获所有非 `ProviderError` 的异常**，**记进账本**（标为 `internal`），
  然后**返回正常的 `error` 结果**。而**区分被保留**：
  provider 故障仍然读作 `provider error`，
  **验收标准的参数校验仍然照旧抛 `ValueError`** —— 因为**坏掉的规则绝不能看起来像闭合过**；
- 配套回归测试 7 个。已实测：去掉兜底 → **6 个测试失败**。

**v0.7.25 加了什么**（修掉一个「预算账本说谎」的缺陷）：

- **被截断的那次调用是「免费」的** —— 端点**已经生成了 token、已经计费**，然后才停。
  但异常只带走了答案、**没带走用量**，所以引擎**没扣这笔账**。
  截断五次的运行**看起来比实际便宜五倍**，**预算上限实际上宽松了五倍**；
- **并行候选池少算了 N 倍** —— 三个 worker 就是**三次截断、三份 token**，
  但**只有被重新抛出的那一个**被计入，**另外两个候选的 token 直接消失了**。
  现在**整个池的花费先收齐**再抛截断，**账本上的数字就是端点开的账单**；
- `TruncatedAnswer` 现在**带着那次调用的用量**，引擎**照实扣进预算**，
  账本里的 `truncated` 条目**同时报告花掉的 token**；
- 配套回归测试 2 个。已实测：去掉计费 → 并行测试报 **0 token**（应为 2400）。

**v0.7.24 加了什么**（修掉一个「回答被截断了却照样闭合」的缺陷）：

- **被截断的回答被当成完整回答交付** —— 端点返回的 `finish_reason` 被收进了原始数据，
  然后**再也没被读过**。于是唯一那句「这个回答不完整」的信号被静默丢弃了；
- **截断的回答能闭合整个循环** —— 模型用完输出 token 时产出的是**残缺**回答，
  而残缺回答**可能碰巧满足验收标准**：要找的关键词可能就在第一段里，
  片段也可能已经够 `min_chars`。于是循环**在半截交付物上闭合**、报告 `closed`、
  把**没写完的东西交给用户**。这正是本项目要防的那一类假闭合，而且**实践中最容易发生**；
- **输出预算从来没被放大过** —— 每次调用都用 provider 默认的 **4000 输出 token**，
  且**永不增加**。写不进 4000 token 的交付物**必然被截断**，并且**必然被静默接受**；
- 现在：**截断的回答变成「可重试的迭代失败」** —— provider 抛出 `TruncatedAnswer`
  而不是返回残缺答案，引擎**把截断记进账本**并**重试这一轮**。
  残缺回答被**故意丢弃**：碰巧满足检查的片段**绝不能**成为交付物；
- **重试时给更多空间** —— 输出预算**随尝试次数翻倍**（8000 → 16000 → 32000，有上限），
  循环**真的有机会写完**，而不是用同样的方式失败两次。预算可用 `output_max_tokens` 配置；
- **并行路径行为一致** —— 被截断的候选**不算「丢失的角度」**，而是**整个候选池一起重试**；
  否则循环会**在一堆碎片里排名**，然后挑出**最长的那个**；
- 配套回归测试 13 个（provider 8 + 引擎 5）。已实测：去掉检测 → 1 个 provider 测试失败；
  去掉引擎重试 → **5 个引擎测试全部失败**。

**v0.7.23 加了什么**（修掉两个「推理块又漏出来了」的缺陷）：

- **未闭合的推理块被整段交付** —— 模型在思考草稿写到一半时**用完了 token**，
  闭合标签 `</think>` 根本不会到达，回答就是一个**永远不闭合的 `<th

🇨🇳 中文 • 🇹🇼 繁體中文 • 🇯🇵 日本語 • 🇵🇹 Português • 🇧🇷 Português • 🇰🇷 한국어 • 🇪🇸 Español • 🇩🇪 Deutsch • 🇫🇷 Français • 🇮🇱 עברית • 🇸🇦 العربية • 🇷🇺 Русский • 🇵🇱 Polski • 🇨🇿 Čeština • 🇳🇱 Nederlands • 🇹🇷 Türkçe • 🇺🇦 Українська • 🇻🇳 Tiếng Việt • 🇵🇭 Tagalog • 🇮🇩 Indonesia • 🇹🇭 ไทย • 🇮🇳 हिन्दी • 🇧🇩 বাংলা • 🇵🇰 اردو • 🇷🇴 Română • 🇸🇪 Svenska • 🇮🇹 Italiano • 🇬🇷 Ελληνικά • 🇭🇺 Magyar • 🇫🇮 Suomi • 🇩🇰 Dansk • 🇳🇴 Norsk

Your coding agent forgets everything between sessions. Claude-Mem remembers for it.


Quick Start • How It Works • Search Tools • Documentation • Configuration • Troubleshooting • License

Every new session, your agent starts from zero. It re-reads the same files, re-asks the same questions, and walks back into mistakes you already fixed together.

Claude-Mem runs a second agent beside it that takes notes while it works. The next session starts with a short index of what matters, and pulls in the details only when it needs them. Works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode and 11 more agents. Copilot CLI, Goose, Roo Code, Warp and Zed can search your memory, but their sessions aren't recorded.

--- ## Quick Start **Installing for someone as an AI agent?** If the user is available, run `npx claude-mem install --setup browser` on their computer and keep it running. It prepares the local runtime, then opens setup in their browser; if the page doesn't open, give them the printed URL. Every choice (agents, integrations, skills, model, usage analytics, the optional email) is made by the user on that page, so there are no terminal questions to relay. If the user is away, run `npx claude-mem install --setup defer`: it prepares the runtime and leaves setup waiting for their first visit, and their next session shows them the link. Don't make their choices for them. ```bash npx claude-mem install ``` The installer finds the agents on your machine and asks which ones to set up. Then just start working: observations stream in from your first prompt, and your second session in a project opens with memory from the first. (Copilot CLI, Goose, Roo Code, Warp and Zed get memory search only, so their sessions don't add to it.) The installer sets everything up first, then asks you to sign in to claude-mem in your browser (email magic link, no card required to sign in). Choosing the **claude-mem observer** then starts its **30 Day Free Trial** on a checkout page that asks for a payment method; once it completes, the installer saves your memory key. With the observer, memory runs off-plan, so you get up to 100% more usage from your plan. When the free trial ends, memory automatically falls back to your Anthropic plan unless you subscribe. After sign-in you pick your memory provider: the claude-mem observer, your own OpenRouter or Gemini key, or your Anthropic plan. Prefer to skip the sign-in? Pass an explicit `--provider` flag, set `CLAUDE_MEM_ONLINE_OPTIN=false`, or run in CI/non-interactive shells — the installer completes without any account interaction. Your memory lives in `~/.claude-mem` on your machine. Cloud sync is opt-in. Anonymous usage analytics are on by default; `npx claude-mem telemetry disable` turns them off ([what's collected](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/telemetry)). Or install from the plugin marketplace inside Claude Code: ```bash /plugin marketplace add thedotmack/claude-mem /plugin install claude-mem ``` Restart Claude Code. Context from previous sessions will automatically appear in new sessions. > **Note:** Claude-Mem is also published on npm, but `npm install -g claude-mem` installs the **SDK/library only** — it does not register the plugin hooks or set up the worker service. Always install via `npx claude-mem install` or the `/plugin` commands above. ### Other agents `npx claude-mem install` covers every supported agent. To set up one agent directly, pass `--ide`. **OpenCode** (1.3.4 or later, including OpenCode 2). Restart OpenCode after installing. ```bash npx claude-mem install --ide opencode ``` **T3 Code** (Codex and Claude Code providers). The installer discovers T3 Code's enabled providers, registers native Claude-Mem plugins in their configured homes, and supports T3-managed Codex. Restart T3 Code, trust the provider's hooks when prompted, and start a new thread. See the [T3 Code integration guide](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/t3code-integration) for custom server settings, status, and removal. ```bash npx claude-mem install --ide t3code ``` **Antigravity CLI** ([setup guide](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/antigravity-cli/setup)): ```bash npx claude-mem install --ide antigravity ``` **OMP (Oh My Pi):** ```bash npx claude-mem install --ide omp ``` **Pi and DeepSeek Harness** use the worker runtime. See [native harness setup](docs/native-harness-integrations.md) for capture, recall, and troubleshooting. ```bash npx claude-mem install --ide pi npx claude-mem install --ide dsh --dsh-profile tui ``` **Grok Bot:** see [Grok Bot](#grok-bot) below. ```bash npx claude-mem install --ide grok-bot ``` The full list of `--ide` values is in `npx claude-mem --help`. #### Grok Bot Grok Bot has no host hooks, so we watch the chat log files. Default is CMEM Pro, the hosted memory. Local observer is opt-in: `--provider host`. Installing this plugin does not install Cursor. **Opt-in awareness push:** needle observations (`decision`, `bugfix`, `security_alert`, `sensitive`) are appended as dated `- YYYY-MM-DD [awareness] …` lines into that bot's `memory/log/YYYY-MM.md`. Grok Bot already re-reads the log from disk. This does not write `profile.md`, user-memory, or project memory. Enable with `CLAUDE_MEM_GROK_BOT_AWARENESS_ENABLED=true` and set `CLAUDE_MEM_GROK_BOT_AWARENESS_AGENT_IDS` to your agent UUIDs (empty by default). #### 🦞 OpenClaw Gateway Install claude-mem as a persistent memory plugin on [OpenClaw](https://openclaw.ai) gateways with a single command: ```bash curl -fsSL https://install.cmem.ai/openclaw.sh | bash ``` The installer handles dependencies, plugin setup, AI provider configuration, worker startup, and optional real-time observation feeds to Telegram, Discord, Slack, and more. See the [OpenClaw Integration Guide](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/openclaw-integration) for details. ## What You Get - 🧠 **The next session starts where the last one left off.** Each session opens with a compact index of past observations, layered so the agent opens full details only when it needs them, and the header can show what each layer costs in tokens. - 🔍 **Find anything you worked on.** The mem-search skill searches your project history in three steps (index, timeline, details), so the agent spends tokens only on what it opens. - 🖥️ **Watch it work, and keep track of yours.** My Work shows live requests, progress, human handoffs and a saved review queue at the worker URL printed on startup. [Guide](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/usage/my-work). Memory, sessions and settings remain at `/viewer`. - 👥 **Share with your team, if you want.** TeamBrain is an optional shared workspace beside My Work, with real team work lists, member attribution and linked findings. Each person chooses what to share; personal requests and review notes stay separate. [Set up a team](https://cmem.ai/teambrain/start). - 💻 **Search from Claude Desktop.** Search your memory from Claude Desktop conversations. - 🔒 **Keep secrets out.** Wrap anything in `` tags and it never gets stored. - 🖼️ **Screenshots, kept by default.** Keep converted copies of tool screenshots under `~/.claude-mem/media-v1/` and show them in My Work, upload them to cmem.ai only when Cloud Sync is on, and send them to the observer model only when image inference is separately enabled. Turn it off with the "Keep images" switch in Settings ([details](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/configuration#screenshots-and-images)). - ⚙️ **Choose what gets injected.** Fine-grained settings for what context a new session starts with. - 🤖 **Nothing to remember to do.** It runs on its own once installed. - 🔗 **Point back to past work.** Every observation has an ID you can cite through the worker API or open in the web viewer. --- ## Documentation 📚 **[View Full Documentation](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/)** - Browse on official website ### Getting Started - **[Installation Guide](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/installation)** - Quick start & advanced installation - **[Usage Guide](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/usage/getting-started)** - How Claude-Mem works automatically - **[Search Tools](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/usage/search-tools)** - Query your project history with natural language - **[Cloud Sync](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/cloud-sync)** - Back up your memory to cmem.ai — no daemon, the worker syncs on write ### Best Practices - **[Context Engineering](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/context-engineering)** - AI agent context optimization principles - **[Progressive Disclosure](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/progressive-disclosure)** - Philosophy behind Claude-Mem's context priming strategy ### Architecture - **[Overview](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/architecture/overview)** - System components & data flow - **[Architecture Evolution](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/architecture-evolution)** - The journey from v3 to v5 - **[Hooks Architecture](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/hooks-architecture)** - How Claude-Mem uses lifecycle hooks - **[Hooks Reference](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/architecture/hooks)** - Every hook entry explained - **[Worker Service](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/architecture/worker-service)** - HTTP API & Bun management - **[Database](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/architecture/database)** - SQLite schema & FTS5 search - **[Search Architecture](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/architecture/search-architecture)** - Hybrid search with Chroma vector database ### Configuration & Development - **[Configuration](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/configuration)** - Environment variables & settings - **[Development](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/development)** - Building, testing, contributing - **[Troubleshooting](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/troubleshooting)** - Common issues & solutions --- ## How It Works 1. **Your agent works.** Hooks in your agent hand each tool call (what it reads, edits and runs) to a small local worker. 2. **The observer takes notes.** A second agent turns that activity into short observations, and writes a summary when the session ends. 3. **The next session starts with them.** When a session starts, your agent gets a compact index of the observations that matter for this project, and fetches full details only when it needs them. Memory injection starts on your second session in a project. To front-load a whole repo instead, run `/learn-codebase` (~5 minutes on a typical repo, optional). See [Architecture Overview](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/architecture/overview) for details. ### How it fits together For contributors, the main parts and where they live: - **The `claude-mem` command** (`src/npx-cli/index.ts`): install, repair, doctor, start, search and the rest. The installer puts a small launcher on PATH so hooks can run `claude-mem` directly. - **Hooks** (`src/cli/hook-command.ts`, one adapter per agent in `src/cli/adapters/`): each agent event runs one shell-free command, such as `claude-mem hook claude-code `. For Claude Code that's Setup (`claude --init` / `--maintenance`), SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure, Stop, SubagentStop and SessionEnd. - **The worker** (`src/services/worker-service.ts`, routes in `src/services/worker/http/routes/`): a local HTTP service managed by Bun. It takes tool activity from the hooks, runs the observer, and serves the viewer and search. - **The observer** (prompts in `src/sdk/`, one provider per model source in `src/services/worker/`, such as `ClaudeProvider.ts` and `OpenRouterProvider.ts`): turns tool activity into observations and summaries. - **Storage** (`src/services/sqlite/`): SQLite at `~/.claude-mem/claude-mem.db` holds sessions, observations and summaries. Chroma adds semantic search on top of SQLite's keyword search (`src/services/worker/search/`). - **Context** (`src/services/context/`): builds the block a new session starts with. - **Search** (`src/servers/mcp-server.ts`, `plugin/skills/mem-search/`): the MCP tools and the mem-search skill that drives them. - **The viewer** (`src/ui/viewer/` at `/viewer`, `src/ui/my-work/` at `/`): memory, sessions and settings, plus My Work. - **The built plugin** (`plugin/`): written by `npm run build`; edit `src/`, not the generated scripts. The words we use for each of these, and the story they tell, are in [docs/story.md](docs/story.md). --- ## MCP Search Tools Search runs through three MCP tools in a token-efficient three-step workflow. The mem-search skill drives it for you: **The three steps:** 1. **`search`** - Get compact index with IDs (~50-100 tokens/result) 2. **`timeline`** - Get chronological context around interesting results 3. **`get_observations`** - Fetch full details ONLY for filtered IDs (~500-1,000 tokens/result) **Step by step:** - Your agent uses MCP tools to search your memory - Start with `search` to get an index of results - Use `timeline` to see what was happening around specific observations - Use `get_observations` to fetch full details for relevant IDs - **Index rows are about a tenth the size of a full record**: ~50-100 tokens versus ~500-1,000. Filtering decides how many records you pay to fetch, not how large each one is; the workflow's total cost also includes the timeline and the selected details. The ratio is not a measured recall or end-to-end saving ([#4138](https://github.com/thedotmack/claude-mem/issues/4138)). **Available MCP Tools:** 1. **`search`** - Search memory index with full-text queries, filters by type/date/project 2. **`timeline`** - Get chronological context around a specific observation or query 3. **`get_observations`** - Fetch full observation details by IDs (always batch multiple IDs) **Example Usage:** ```typescript // Step 1: Search for index search(query="authentication bug", type="bugfix", limit=10) // Step 2: Review index, identify relevant IDs (e.g., #123, #456) // Step 3: Fetch full details get_observations(ids=[123, 456]) ``` The worker also offers tools for code navigation (`smart_search`, `smart_outline`, `smart_unfold`), saving a note on purpose (`save_memory`) and tracking work in progress. See [Search Tools Guide](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/usage/search-tools) for detailed examples. --- ## System Requirements - **Node.js**: 20.19 or later in the 20.x line, or 22.12 or later - **A supported agent**: Claude Code (latest, with plugin support) or any agent in [Other agents](#other-agents) - **Bun**: JavaScript runtime and process manager (auto-installed if missing) - **uv**: Python package manager for vector search (auto-installed if missing) - **SQLite 3**: For persistent storage (bundled) --- ### Windows Setup Notes If you see an error like: ```powershell npm : The term 'npm' is not recognized as the name of a cmdlet ``` Make sure Node.js and npm are installed and added to your PATH. Download the latest Node.js installer from https://nodejs.org and restart your terminal after installation. Claude Code hooks do not need Git Bash. Each hook runs `claude-mem` directly, and `npx claude-mem install` places that launcher at `%LOCALAPPDATA%\claude-mem\bin\claude-mem.exe` and adds the folder to your user Path. Restart your terminal or IDE afterwards so Claude Code picks up the new Path. If hooks report `Executable not found in $PATH: "claude-mem"`, run `npx claude-mem doctor` and see [Troubleshooting](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/troubleshooting#claude-mem-command-not-found-in-hooks). --- ## Configuration Settings are managed in `~/.claude-mem/settings.json` (auto-created with defaults on first run). Configure AI model, worker port, data directory, log level, and context injection settings. To include observations from every harness in Claude Code and Codex SessionStart context, set `"CLAUDE_MEM_SESSION_START_INCLUDE_ALL_SOURCES": "true"` in that file, or enable **Include all sources at session start** in the viewer settings. The default is `"false"`, which limits startup context to the current harness. The observation count limit still applies across the selected sources. See the **[Configuration Guide](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/configuration)** for all available settings and examples. ### Mode & Language Configuration Claude-Mem supports multiple workflow modes and languages via the `CLAUDE_MEM_MODE` setting. This option controls both: - The workflow behavior (e.g. code, chill, investigation) - The language used in generated observations #### How to Configure Edit your settings file at `~/.claude-mem/settings.json`: ```json { "CLAUDE_MEM_MODE": "code--zh" } ``` Modes are defined in `plugin/modes/`. To see all available modes locally: ```bash ls ~/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/thedotmack/plugin/modes/ ``` #### Available Modes | Mode | Description | |------------|-------------------------| | `code` | Default English mode | | `code--chill` | Records fewer observations, keeping only what would be painful to rediscover | | `code--[lang]` | Same as `code`, with observations and summaries written in another language | Built-in language codes: `ar`, `bn`, `cs`, `da`, `de`, `el`, `es`, `fi`, `fr`, `he`, `hi`, `hu`, `id`, `it`, `ja`, `ko`, `nl`, `no`, `pl`, `pt-br`, `ro`, `ru`, `sv`, `th`, `tr`, `uk`, `ur`, `vi`, `zh`. For example, `code--ko` writes observations and summaries in Korean. See [Modes](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/modes) for each language's name, the email investigation mode, and custom modes. > Note: All of these modes are built in. No additional installation or plugin update is required. #### After Changing Mode Restart Claude Code to apply the new mode configuration. --- ## Development See the **[Development Guide](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/development)** for build instructions, testing, and contribution workflow. --- ## Troubleshooting Start with `npx claude-mem doctor`. It checks Bun, uv, the hook launcher and the worker, and tells you what to fix. See the **[Troubleshooting Guide](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/troubleshooting)** for common issues and solutions. --- ## Bug Reports Create comprehensive bug reports with the automated generator: ```bash cd ~/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/thedotmack npm run bug-report ``` ## Contributing Contributions are welcome! Please: 1. Fork the repository 2. Create a feature branch 3. Make your changes with tests 4. Update documentation (user-facing words follow [docs/story.md](docs/story.md)) 5. Submit a Pull Request against `main` Releases ship from `main` and are published to npm. See [Development Guide](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/development) for contribution workflow. --- ## License Claude-Mem is licensed under the Apache License 2.0. We chose Apache-2.0 because durable agentic memory should be easy to embed in developer tools, local agents, MCP servers, enterprise systems, robotics stacks, and production agent harnesses. See the [LICENSE](LICENSE) file for full details. See [docs/license.md](docs/license.md) and [docs/ip-boundary.md](docs/ip-boundary.md) for licensing scope and the open/commercial boundary. --- ## Support - **Documentation**: [docs/](docs/) - **Issues**: [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/thedotmack/claude-mem/issues) - **Repository**: [github.com/thedotmack/claude-mem](https://github.com/thedotmack/claude-mem) - **Official X Account**: [@Claude_Memory](https://x.com/Claude_Memory) - **Official Discord**: [Join Discord](https://discord.com/invite/J4wttp9vDu) - **Author**: Alex Newman ([@thedotmack](https://github.com/thedotmack)) --- **Built with Claude Agent SDK** | **Works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode and more** | **Made with TypeScript** --- ### What About CMEM? CMEM is a token created by a 3rd party but officially embraced by the creator of Claude-Mem (Alex Newman, @thedotmack). The token acts as a community catalyst for growth and a vehicle for bringing CMEM to the developers and knowledge workers that need it most. Official BASE CA: 0x76b1967eec0ccaeb001bbbb2b40dc4badba31ba3

# 📚 1410知识库 (`1410-kb-plugin` · DSH 原生插件 V3.1)

> **“三大页签（📚 书架 / 🏭 工坊 / 🌐 共享）· 纯 Markdown 单轨 · MiniSearch BM25 毫秒级倒排索引 · 三级知识锻造炉（anydoc + `@arcships/light-ocr` 扫描识别 + DeepSeek AI 润色）。”**

---

## 🌟 V3.1 四大核心能力

1. **📖 纯 Markdown 单轨阅读器 + 荣誉署名 UI**：
   - 彻底废除 `data.json`，全量内置《焦氏易林》64 林 4,096 条纯 Markdown 原典（`packs/易学/六爻/焦氏易林/chapters/*.md`）；
   - 左侧四级专业分类树（`📂 易学 ➔ 📁 六爻 ➔ 📘 焦氏易林 ➔ 64林章节`），打开任何知识库封面均醒目展示：**`“由 @作者名 贡献（版本号：X.X）”`** 与原始仓库链接。
2. **🔍 MiniSearch + 中文分词 BM25 倒排索引**：
   - 内置 CJK Bigram/Unigram 分词与 MiniSearch BM25 倒排索引；
   - AI 工具 `query_knowledge` 命中时在工具层返回记忆内化提示词与 `[1](#1410-kb-yilin "《焦氏易林》坎之比")` 原生角标，未命中时静默返回 `{ content: "" }`。
3. **🔥 升级版三级「知识锻造炉」+ 左右双屏预览编辑器**：
   - **第一级（智能路由与转换）**：文本型 PDF/Word/TXT/HTML 直接高速提取（`anydoc` / `MarkItDown` / `PyMuPDF`）；
   - **第二级（`light-ocr` 离线扫描识别）**：自动识别扫描版 PDF 并调用 `@arcships/light-ocr` 的 `recognizeDocument` 接口离线 OCR 提取文本行；
   - **第三级（DeepSeek AI 润色与排版）**：去除页眉页脚与水印、修复错漏、统一 `#` 与 `##` 标题层级，在左右双屏编辑器中左屏看排版预览、右屏改源码。
4. **🏛️ 双轨存储去向 + 藏经阁三层审核防线**：
   - **【🔒 仅存入本地（默认）】**：写入 `packs/私有/`，标记 `"visibility": "private"`，完全离线免审；
   - **【🏛️ 上交藏经阁（主动）】**：一键生成包含 `.md` 与 `manifest.json` 的 `.zip` 贡献包并引导提 PR；
   - **三层防线**：`.github/workflows/validate.yml`（`scripts/validate_pr.py` 硬性门禁 + `scripts/ai_review_pr.py` AI 初审评分 + `registry.json` 官方钦定/社区精选/最近更新分类同步）。

---

## 🧪 运行验收测试与 CI 门禁校验

```bash
python scripts/validate_pr.py
python scripts/ai_review_pr.py
python tests/test_1410_kb.py
```

It can invoke document conversion/OCR tooling and modify a local knowledge registry. The fixed manifest and captured docs do not establish a versioned DSH target. No candidate code or lifecycle hooks were executed; runtime safety and compatibility are unproven.

# dsh-ask-first · 先问

> 不明白就先问。用户那句话说不清楚时，模型不许猜着做。

[English](README.en.md) | **中文**

[![test](https://github.com/Tirpitz-39/dsh-ask-first/actions/workflows/test.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/Tirpitz-39/dsh-ask-first/actions/workflows/test.yml)

## 它做什么

主触发是**思考链**：每次模型准备调工具时，扫它最近几条思考（reasoning）——一旦出现「我猜用户 / 不确定用户 / 不知道用户要」这类**指向用户意图的猜测**，就视为它自己在承认「在猜」，拦下要求先问。

被拦后：

1. 先用 `ask_user_question` 问清两层：**要干什么**（目标/交付物/范围）和**要怎么干**（方式/约束/验收标准），每条给 2-4 个具体选项；
2. 本轮问过之后**还接着调工具**，再拦一次——问完就停，不许「问一句然后自己猜着填完」；
3. 每轮最多拦 `maxBlocksPerTurn`（默认 2）次，拦满放行，宁少拦不卡死。

**字面规则是可选兜底**（`ruleGate`，默认关）：短消息 + 指代/疑问 + 无动作词也拦。开了误伤会多（「你确定吗」「重启了」这种都会被拦）。

读思考的细节：DSH 的 assistant 消息里 `reasoning` 块带完整思考文本（实测最长 4459 字），但**工具调用前的过渡消息 reasoning 会被清空**，所以要扫最近 5 条合并再匹配。

## 不拦的情况

- 回执：「继续」「好」「收到」「ok」「1」「2」……
- **疑问/确认句**：「你确定吗」「可以吗」「有问题吗」这类对对话本身的质疑/确认——那不是任务，不拦
- 子代理会话、定时任务、QQ/桥接等没人能回答的会话
- **机器轮次不武装**：`[SCHEDULE REMINDER]`、插件 followup 这类注入消息不算真人说话——本轮没有真人 `lastText` 时，思考检测也不触发（2026-11-16 实测修复：定时任务会话曾被误卡）
- `subagent` / `subagent_fork` / `workflow` 派活工具本身（子代理内部本来就不拦）
- 总开关关闭（设置页或输入框旁按钮）
- `ask_user_question` / `todo_write` / `claim_*` / `wrapup_check` 本身

## 配置项

设置页（设置 → 先问）或 HTTP 接口 `POST /dsh-ask-first/config` 都可改；手改 `config.json` 也行，坏值会被夹回合法区间。

| 配置项 | 默认 | 说明 |
|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | `true` | 总开关 |
| `thinkingGate` | `true` | 主触发：思考链里的「猜」信号 |
| `ruleGate` | `false` | 字面规则兜底，误伤较多 |
| `modelGate` | `false` | 模型判断（未完善，花钱） |
| `timeoutMinutes` | `10` | 被拦后多久没回复就按最小假设继续，1–120 |
| `maxBlocksPerTurn` | `2` | 每轮最多拦几次，1–10 |
| `vagueMaxLength` | `40` | 多短算「说不清」，10–200 |

## 超时

被拦后用户 `timeoutMinutes`（默认 10）分钟没回，插件往会话里投递一条消息：按最小假设继续，并在回答开头写明假设。之后本轮不再拦。

## 模型判断（modelGate，未完善，默认关）

> **状态：未完善（beta）**。2026-11-16 实测：链路是通的（调模型 → 判 needClarify → 拦），但判断器只喂**单条消息**、看不到对话上下文，容易把「测一下吧」这种明确指令判成缺信息（实测复现）。思考链主触发已经够准，这个当备用；启用请接受它会偏严。

规则判不出「说不清」时，可以再让模型看一眼：开了之后，每条没被规则拦下的消息会额外调一次模型，判断需求是否「信息不足或自相矛盾」——比如「在酒吧点蛋炒饭」「不放油不开火做蛋炒饭」。

- 默认**关**，关着就完全不花 token
- 每次判断花少量 token（约几百）
- 模型不可用 / 超时 30 秒 / 输出解析失败 → 一律放行（fail-open）
- 已知未完善：只看单条消息，没有对话上下文；后续可以考虑把最近 2-3 轮一起喂进去

## 思考里的「猜」信号

模型的思考/正文里出现这些**承认自己在猜**的短语时，直接拦下要求先问——不管用户那句话字面上清不清楚：

- 中文：「我猜用户 / 不确定用户 / 不知道用户要 / 用户可能是想 / 用户要的应该是」
- 英文：「I guess the user / not sure what the user / I think the user / the user probably wants / I guess that / not sure what you mean」

匹配大小写不敏感、匹配前去掉空白（思考里换行拆词也能抓到）。英文对话靠这些信号触发；正常推理（没写猜测词）不拦。

> 实测（2026-11-16）：`deepseek-flash` 的 assistant 消息里 `reasoning` 块是空的（只有空 reasoning + tool-call），所以这个信号对 flash 主要靠正文；换成带思考内容的模型时，思考也会被扫。

## 数据

都在 `DSH_HOME` 下的 `ask-first/`：宿主设置了 `DSH_HOME` 就用它，否则用 `~/.dsh/ask-first/`（与 DSH 官方的目录解析一致，Windows / macOS / Linux 通用）。

| 文件 | 内容 |
|---|---|
| `config.json` | 上面的配置项；写入是原子的（临时文件 + rename） |
| `sessions.json` | 每会话的临时覆盖（预留） |
| `ask-first.log` | 每次拦截/提问/超时的 JSONL 记录，超过 2 MiB 自动轮转保留尾部一半（可用 `DSH_ASK_FIRST_LOG_MAX_BYTES` 调整上限） |

## 安装

要求：DSH（带 `tools` 和 `webServer` 服务）、Node.js ≥ 18。

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Tirpitz-39/dsh-ask-first
dsh plugin add file:./dsh-ask-first
```

本地开发时也可以直接指向自己的目录（`dsh plugin add file:<插件目录>`）。

装完**重启 DSH**。设置 → 先问，或输入框旁的「先问」按钮。

## 测试

```bash
npm test                 # 四组一起跑
node test/smoke.mjs      # 38 项：规则判定 / 拦截 / 放行 / 回执 / 子代理 / 机器轮次 / 思考链
node test/edge-cases.mjs # 20 条边界样本矩阵
node test/attack.mjs     # 10 条对抗样本（伪造前缀、拆词、硬抗次数、借道子代理…）
node test/config.mjs     # 19 项：配置默认值/夹紧、原子写、日志轮转、跨平台数据目录
```

测试不需要 DSH 运行时：假 `ctx` / 假 `agent`，`DSH_HOME` 指向临时目录。CI 在 ubuntu 和 windows 上跑 Node 18/20/22。

对抗测试目前 **漏洞 0 / 10**：伪造 `[SCHEDULE REMINDER]` 前缀、思考换行拆词两个漏洞已修；伪造 `source` 属宿主生成、用户不可构造，标为低风险；「思考不暴露猜测就抓不到」是方案固有局限。

## 已知局限

- 思考里不暴露猜测就抓不到（方案固有）
- `modelGate` 只看单条消息，会偏严
- 借道 `subagent` / `workflow` 时子代理内部不拦（设计如此：子代理内部本来就不该问人）

## License

MIT
